sections.title: Before You Start

sections.say: Thirty-four rounds. Each one says which unit it is testing.
sections.title: Unit By Unit

rounds.say: Nine verbs in ten. Four of the six endings make no sound.
rounds.label: Unit 1 · Regular -ER verbs

questions.q: Which form goes with « ils » for the verb parler?
questions.why: ils parlent. The -ent is silent, so it sounds identical to je parle and tu parles, and only the pronoun in front tells you which one it was. Unit 1.

questions.q: Write the nous form of travailler.
questions.why: -ons is one of the two endings you can actually hear, which is what makes nous and vous the easy half of the six. Unit 1.
accept: nous travaillons
travaillons
questions.answer: nous travaillons

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Nous parlons. The first, second and fourth are one sound between them, so the ear has only the pronoun to go on and -ons is the ending that arrives. Unit 1.

questions.q: A learner writes « Nous parlez français ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: The two audible endings are the two that get swapped, because they are the two anybody notices. -ons belongs to nous and -ez to vous. Unit 1.
accept: Nous parlons français
questions.answer: Nous parlons français.
questions.prompt: Nous parlez français.

questions.q: Which two endings can you hear?
questions.why: -ons and -ez. The other four are silent, and that is why the subject pronoun in front of the verb is doing the work the ending cannot. Unit 1.

rounds.say: The spelling moves so the sound can stay still.
rounds.label: Unit 2 · The -ER verbs that change their stem

questions.q: Write the nous form of manger.
questions.why: nous mangeons, with an e that belongs to nothing except the g in front of it. Without it the g would harden in front of the o. Unit 2.
accept: nous mangeons
mangeons
questions.answer: nous mangeons

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: nous commençons. The cedilla does for c what the added e does for g: it keeps the soft sound in front of a back vowel. It has to be picked rather than typed, because a typed answer is compared with the cedilla stripped. Unit 2.

questions.q: Write the tu form of appeler.
questions.why: tu appelles, with two l. The ending went silent, so the vowel in front of it needs something to hold it open, and the doubled consonant is that something. Unit 2.
accept: tu appelles
appelles
questions.answer: tu appelles

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: je préfère. The second accent turns and the first does not, for the same reason appelles doubles its l: the silent ending leaves the vowel needing support. Only a picked answer can ask this, because a typed one folds the accents away. Unit 2.

questions.q: A learner writes « Nous mangons à midi ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: nous mangeons. The nous cell is the only one of the six where a -ger verb changes at all, which is why it is mostly met in writing. Unit 2.
accept: Nous mangeons à midi
questions.answer: Nous mangeons à midi.
questions.prompt: Nous mangons à midi.

rounds.say: The plural of this family puts a sound on the end.
rounds.label: Unit 3 · Regular -IR verbs

questions.q: Which form goes with « ils » for the verb finir?
questions.why: ils finissent. The plural of this family carries -iss-, which you hear, where the singular carries nothing you can. Unit 3.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Ils finissent. This is the one family where the plural is genuinely audible, because -iss- is a syllable and the silent endings of the other two families are not. Unit 3.

questions.q: Write the nous form of choisir.
questions.why: nous choisissons. The -iss- goes in before the ending, in all three plural persons, without exception in this family. Unit 3.
accept: nous choisissons
choisissons
questions.answer: nous choisissons

questions.q: A learner writes « Vous finez à cinq heures ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: vous finissez. The -ez is right and the missing piece is the -iss- in front of it. Borrowing the -er endings whole is the commonest way this family goes wrong. Unit 3.
accept: Vous finissez à cinq heures
questions.answer: Vous finissez à cinq heures.
questions.prompt: Vous finez à cinq heures.

questions.q: Which of these does NOT take -iss- in the plural?
questions.why: partir. It ends in -ir and it is not in this family: ils partent, not ils partissent. The ending of the naming form does not tell you which of the three -ir families a verb is in, which is the unit’s second lesson. Unit 3.

rounds.say: One cell in this family has nothing written in it at all.
rounds.label: Unit 4 · Regular -RE verbs

questions.q: Which form goes with « il » for the verb vendre?
questions.why: il vend, with no ending at all. The stem ends in d and French will not write a second consonant after it, so the third person of this family is the bare stem. Unit 4.

questions.q: Write the nous form of attendre.
questions.why: nous attendons. The stem-final d is silent at the end of a word and said the moment a letter follows it, which is why the plural of this family is audible. Unit 4.
accept: nous attendons
attendons
questions.answer: nous attendons

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Ils vendent. The d is silent in il vend and said in ils vendent, so this family gives the ear something the -er family never does. Unit 4.

questions.q: A learner writes « Il répondt au téléphone ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: il répond. Adding a letter here is the reflex the other two families train: -e on parler, -t on finir, and nothing at all on vendre. Unit 4.
accept: Il répond au téléphone
questions.answer: Il répond au téléphone.
questions.prompt: Il répondt au téléphone.

questions.q: What do the three regular families write in the « il » cell?
questions.why: il parle, il finit, il vend: one letter, two letters and none. Setting the three side by side is the point of having reached the third one. Unit 4.

rounds.say: Where the method stops. Three verbs you cannot build.
rounds.label: Unit 5 · Aller, venir and tenir

questions.q: Which form goes with « ils » for the verb venir?
questions.why: ils viennent. The third person singular is nasal and the plural is not, which is a change you can hear and the only reliable signal this verb gives. Unit 5.

questions.q: Write the French for: I have just eaten
questions.why: Je viens de manger. French says you are coming from the action, and the verb after de never changes for the person. Unit 5.
accept: Je viens de manger
questions.answer: Je viens de manger.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Ils viennent. The vowel is nasal in vient and open in viennent, so this is one of the few third-person contrasts in A2 that the ear can settle on its own. Unit 5.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je vien de finir ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je viens, with the -s. It is silent, so nothing in the sentence tells you it is missing, and this is why the recent past is a written trap rather than a spoken one. Unit 5.
accept: Je viens de finir
questions.answer: Je viens de finir.
questions.prompt: Je vien de finir.

questions.q: Which of these means: I have just left Paris
questions.why: Je viens de quitter Paris. One form, two jobs: venir de plus a place is where you are from, and venir de plus a verb is what you just did. Only the next word separates them. Unit 5.

rounds.say: Two endings almost nothing else in the language has.
rounds.label: Unit 6 · Faire, dire and lire

questions.q: Which form goes with « vous » for the verb faire?
questions.why: vous faites. Only three verbs in the language take -tes here, and you have all three: être, faire and dire. Unit 6.

questions.q: Write the ils form of faire.
questions.why: ils font. Four verbs take -ont in the third person plural and you now have all four: être, avoir, aller and faire. Unit 6.
accept: ils font
font
questions.answer: ils font

questions.q: Write the vous form of dire.
questions.why: vous dites, not vous disez. The regular ending is what the ear expects and it is wrong here, which is why this is the cell that gets corrected in public. Unit 6.
accept: vous dites
dites
questions.answer: vous dites

questions.q: Which is the French for: to go shopping
questions.why: faire les courses. French keeps faire where English reaches for a different verb each time, and the same verb does the cooking, the washing up and the weather. Unit 6.

questions.q: Write the vous form of lire.
questions.why: vous lisez, the ordinary ending. lire is the control case: it sits beside faire and dire so the two odd endings stand out as odd rather than looking like a pattern. Unit 6.
accept: vous lisez
lisez
questions.answer: vous lisez

rounds.say: One verb changes for the person. The one behind it never does.
rounds.label: Unit 7 · Vouloir, pouvoir and devoir

questions.q: Which form goes with « ils » for the verb vouloir?
questions.why: ils veulent. The third-person plural stem is the singular stem plus the last consonant of the nous stem, and that holds for all three of these verbs. Unit 7.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Ils veulent. The l arrives in the plural and nothing else changes, which is the same shape as viennent against vient. Unit 7.

questions.q: Write the French for: We must leave
questions.why: Nous devons partir. The second verb stays in its naming form whatever the first one does, and that holds for every verb in the language. Unit 7.
accept: Nous devons partir
questions.answer: Nous devons partir.

questions.q: A learner writes « Elle veut part ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Elle veut partir. Conjugating the second verb as well is the mistake this frame exists to prevent, and it costs nothing to avoid once you see that only the first verb carries the person. Unit 7.
accept: Elle veut partir
questions.answer: Elle veut partir.
questions.prompt: Elle veut part.

questions.q: You are asking a stranger for something. Which?
questions.why: Je voudrais. It is learnt as a fixed form rather than built, and je veux at a counter reads as an instruction rather than a request. Unit 7.

rounds.say: English has one word here. French has two and they are not interchangeable.
rounds.label: Unit 8 · Savoir and connaître

questions.q: Write the French for: I know Paris
questions.why: Je connais Paris. A noun and nothing after it takes connaître, which stops at the thing it names. Unit 8.
accept: Je connais Paris
questions.answer: Je connais Paris.

questions.q: Which verb goes in: « Je ___ où il habite. »
questions.why: Je sais où il habite. What follows decides: a clause takes savoir, a bare noun takes connaître, and the choice is made by the shape of the sentence rather than by what it is about. Unit 8.

questions.q: Write the nous form of connaître.
questions.why: nous connaissons, with the double s. savoir shortens in the plural and connaître lengthens, which is the fastest way to keep the two verbs apart. Unit 8.
accept: nous connaissons
connaissons
questions.answer: nous connaissons

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: il connaît, with the circumflex on the i in front of the t. It is the only accent in either verb, and it can only be asked as a picked answer, because a typed one is compared with the accent stripped off. Unit 8.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je connais nager ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je sais nager. A verb behind it takes savoir, every time. connaître accepts a noun and nothing else, which is what stops at the thing means. Unit 8.
accept: Je sais nager
questions.answer: Je sais nager.
questions.prompt: Je connais nager.

rounds.say: Cover the front of the verb and build what is left.
rounds.label: Unit 9 · Prendre, mettre and battre

questions.q: Which form goes with « ils » for the verb prendre?
questions.why: ils prennent. Three stems: prend- in the singular, pren- for nous and vous, prenn- here. The doubled n is holding a vowel open in front of a silent ending, which is the same job it did in appelles. Unit 9.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Ils prennent. The singular is nasal and the plural is not, exactly as in vient against viennent. Two verbs, one signal. Unit 9.

questions.q: Write the nous form of mettre.
questions.why: nous mettons, with two t. mettre and battre carry a single consonant in the singular and a doubled one in the plural, which is a smaller change than prendre makes. Unit 9.
accept: nous mettons
mettons
questions.answer: nous mettons

questions.q: A learner writes « Nous prennons le bus ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: nous prenons, with one n. The doubling belongs to the third person plural alone, because that is the only plural cell whose ending is silent. Unit 9.
accept: Nous prenons le bus
questions.answer: Nous prenons le bus.
questions.prompt: Nous prennons le bus.

questions.q: Which form goes with « ils » for the verb apprendre?
questions.why: ils apprennent. Cover the front of the verb and what is left is prendre, which is what makes comprendre, surprendre, permettre and combattre free rather than four more things to learn. Unit 9.

rounds.say: The plain form tells you the other three.
rounds.label: Unit 10 · Adjective agreement

questions.q: Write the feminine of heureux.
questions.why: heureuse. The -eux group swaps its ending for -euse, and the change is one you can hear, which is unusual: most agreement in French is written and silent. Unit 10.
accept: heureuse
questions.answer: heureuse

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Elle est heureuse. The feminine of this group is audible and the plural of any group is not, so what the ear catches here is the gender, never the number. Unit 10.

questions.q: Write the feminine of sportif.
questions.why: sportive. The -if group replaces its consonant rather than adding to it, and the v is audible where the f was. Unit 10.
accept: sportive
questions.answer: sportive

questions.q: Which is right for brown shoes?
questions.why: marron never moves. It was a chestnut before it was a colour, and a colour named after a thing keeps the thing’s shape. The same holds for orange and for bleu marine. Unit 10.

questions.q: A learner writes « une fille sportif ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: une fille sportive. The four classes are productive, so a describing word you have never met is agreeable from its plain form without being told anything else about it. Unit 10.
accept: une fille sportive
questions.answer: une fille sportive
questions.prompt: une fille sportif

rounds.say: These three have a fifth shape, and it only appears in front of a vowel.
rounds.label: Unit 11 · Beau, nouveau and vieux

questions.q: Which goes in: « un ___ appartement »?
questions.why: un nouvel appartement. Say the feminine and drop its last two letters: nouvelle gives nouvel. The same move gives bel and vieil. Unit 11.

questions.q: Write the masculine plural of beau.
questions.why: beaux, with an x. No unit at any level before this one claimed the -eaux plural, and it is silent, so it is a written form and nothing else. Unit 11.
accept: beaux
questions.answer: beaux

questions.q: Tap the letters you do not say in « nouveaux ».
questions.why: The x is silent, so nouveau and nouveaux are one sound and the number lives on the page alone. That is why five written forms come out of the mouth as two. Unit 11.

questions.q: A learner writes « un beau appartement ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: un bel appartement. French will not run two vowel sounds together here, which is the same reason le becomes l’ and ma becomes mon in front of a vowel. Unit 11.
accept: un bel appartement
questions.answer: un bel appartement
questions.prompt: un beau appartement

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Cet homme est vieux. The short form only exists in front of the noun. Behind the verb there is no vowel coming, so there is nothing for it to solve. Unit 11.

rounds.say: Say the feminine, then add the ending.
rounds.label: Unit 12 · Adverbs

questions.q: Write the adverb built on lent.
questions.why: lentement, off the feminine lente. The t you never say in lent is said in lentement, so the base is audible in the derivative and the rule is a sound rule as well as a spelling one. Unit 12.
accept: lentement
questions.answer: lentement

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: évidemment. A describing word in -ent gives -emment and one in -ant gives -amment, and the two endings are one sound, so nothing in the mouth tells you which you are writing. A picked answer is the only kind that can ask this. Unit 12.

questions.q: Write the adverb built on heureux.
questions.why: heureusement, off the feminine heureuse. Going through the feminine is not a memory aid: it is where the consonant comes from. Unit 12.
accept: heureusement
questions.answer: heureusement

questions.q: Which is the adverb for bon?
questions.why: bien. Three adverbs stand outside the rule: bien for bon, mal for mauvais, and vite, which has no describing word behind it at all. Unit 12.

questions.q: A learner writes « Il parle lent ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Il parle lentement. English lets a describing word stand in for an adverb in speech and French does not: what modifies a verb has to be built. Unit 12.
accept: Il parle lentement
questions.answer: Il parle lentement.
questions.prompt: Il parle lent.

rounds.say: What the little word does to the article is the whole choice.
rounds.label: Unit 13 · Prepositions of place

questions.q: Which is the French for: to Japan
questions.why: au Japon, which is à plus le folded into one word. A masculine country keeps its article and the article contracts. Unit 13.

questions.q: Write the French for: at the doctor’s
questions.why: chez le médecin. chez is the one locative preposition that neither contracts with the article nor throws it away, and it only ever takes a person. Unit 13.
accept: chez le médecin
questions.answer: chez le médecin

questions.q: Which is the French for: in France
questions.why: en France. en throws the article out, where à folds it in and chez leaves it alone. Three prepositions, three things done to one article. Unit 13.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je vais à le marché ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je vais au marché. à le is never written in French; it is always au. The same operation gives aux with les. Unit 13.
accept: Je vais au marché
questions.answer: Je vais au marché.
questions.prompt: Je vais à le marché.

questions.q: Write the French for: to Paris
questions.why: à Paris, with no article at all. A city takes a bare à, and the absence is a fact about city names rather than something a rule removed. Unit 13.
accept: à Paris
questions.answer: à Paris

rounds.say: If it is still going, French keeps the verb in the present.
rounds.label: Unit 14 · Prepositions of time

questions.q: Which is the French for: I have been living here for three years
questions.why: J’habite ici depuis trois ans, in the present, because you still live there. English reaches for a past tense here and French does not, which is the one calque this unit exists to stop. Unit 14.
opts: J’ai habité ici depuis trois ans.
J’habite ici il y a trois ans.

questions.q: Write the French for: during the holidays
questions.why: pendant les vacances. depuis is a span that is still open and pendant is one that is closed, and English says for in both places. Unit 14.
accept: pendant les vacances
questions.answer: pendant les vacances

questions.q: Write the French for: three years ago
questions.why: il y a trois ans. One form, two jobs again: a measurement of time behind it makes it ago, and a plain noun behind it makes it there is. Unit 14.
accept: il y a trois ans
questions.answer: il y a trois ans

questions.q: A learner writes « Je pars en trois jours ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je pars dans trois jours. dans is the time before something starts and en is the time it takes to finish, which is the pair that decides whether you have left yet. Unit 14.
accept: Je pars dans trois jours
questions.answer: Je pars dans trois jours.
questions.prompt: Je pars en trois jours.

questions.q: Which means: it took me ten minutes
questions.why: en dix minutes. en measures the work and dans measures the wait, and choosing wrong turns a finished job into an appointment. Unit 14.

rounds.say: Two verbs, and the small words go round the first one.
rounds.label: Unit 15 · The near future

questions.q: Write the French for: I am going to eat
questions.why: Je vais manger. aller carries the person and the second verb stays in its naming form, exactly as it did behind vouloir and pouvoir. Unit 15.
accept: Je vais manger
questions.answer: Je vais manger.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Je vais manger. Four ways of placing one action in time, and the first word of each is what separates them. The verb at the end of the first two is one sound either way. Unit 15.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Je ne vais pas partir. The two halves of the negative wrap the verb that changed, not the one carrying the meaning. Unit 15.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je vais ne pas sortir ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je ne vais pas sortir. Wrapping the second verb is the reflex English gives you, and the rule holds unchanged for the modals and for the compound past. Unit 15.
accept: Je ne vais pas sortir
questions.answer: Je ne vais pas sortir.
questions.prompt: Je vais ne pas sortir.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT the near future?
questions.why: Je vais à Paris is a journey, not a plan. aller plus a verb is the future and aller plus a place is movement, and the next word is the only thing separating them. Unit 15.

rounds.say: One verb, two words, and the small ones go in between.
rounds.label: Unit 16 · The passé composé with avoir

questions.q: Write the French for: I ate at noon
questions.why: J’ai mangé à midi. avoir carries the person and the second word is the past form, which for an -er verb ends in -é. Unit 16.
accept: J’ai mangé à midi
questions.answer: J’ai mangé à midi.

questions.q: Which is the past form of vendre?
questions.why: vendu. One ending per family: -er gives -é, -ir gives -i, -re gives -u. Three endings cover every regular verb in the language. Unit 16.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: J’ai fini. The past form of an -ir verb is the same sound as its je form, so the first word is the only thing that puts the sentence in the past. Unit 16.
opts: Je viens de finir le travail.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je n’ai mangé pas ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je n’ai pas mangé. The negative wraps the first word, which is the same rule the near future ran, and the gap between the two words is where the small words live. Unit 16.
accept: Je n’ai pas mangé
questions.answer: Je n’ai pas mangé.
questions.prompt: Je n’ai mangé pas.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Elle a mangé. After avoir the second word never agrees with the subject, in any person or gender. That is what makes the être verbs of unit 18 different rather than difficult. Unit 16.

rounds.say: Do not build these. Reach for the group they are in.
rounds.label: Unit 17 · The past forms you cannot build

questions.q: Write the past form of prendre.
questions.why: pris. An -re verb giving -is rather than -u is the clearest sign that the naming form tells you nothing about the past form. mettre gives mis the same way. Unit 17.
accept: pris
questions.answer: pris

questions.q: What is the past form of avoir?
questions.why: eu, and it is said /y/, which none of its three letters would lead you to expect. It is one of the five that belong to no group at all. Unit 17.

questions.q: Write the past form of ouvrir.
questions.why: ouvert. An -ir verb giving -ert is the other direction of the same point, and offrir and souffrir go with it. Unit 17.
accept: ouvert
questions.answer: ouvert

questions.q: Which is the past form of devoir?
questions.why: dû, with the little roof. It is the only thing separating it in writing from the du that means some, and it comes off in the feminine due. A typed answer cannot ask this, because the accent is stripped before the comparison. Unit 17.

questions.q: A learner writes « J’ai prendu le train ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: J’ai pris le train. Building the form from the family ending is the reflex, and for these thirty-three verbs it is always wrong. Cover the prefix and apprendre gives appris the same way. Unit 17.
accept: J’ai pris le train
questions.answer: J’ai pris le train.
questions.prompt: J’ai prendu le train.

rounds.say: Fifteen verbs take the other first word, and then the second one moves.
rounds.label: Unit 18 · The passé composé with être

questions.q: Which first word does aller take in the past?
questions.why: être. Fifteen verbs of movement and change of state take it, and once you are on être the second word agrees with the subject. Unit 18.

questions.q: Write the French for: She went out
questions.why: Elle est sortie, with the -e. The agreement is written and silent, so nothing in the sentence out loud tells you it is missing. Unit 18.
accept: Elle est sortie
questions.answer: Elle est sortie.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Elle est morte. Of the fifteen, mourir is the only one whose agreement you can hear: the feminine ending lets the t out. On the other fourteen the ear has the pronoun and nothing else. Unit 18.

questions.q: Tap the letters you do not say in « allées ».
questions.why: Both the final e and the s are silent, so all four written forms of this past form are one sound. The agreement is a fact about the page. Unit 18.

questions.q: A learner writes « Elle a allé au marché ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Elle est allée. Two things move together: the first word becomes être and the second word then has to agree. Getting the first one right and forgetting the second is the commonest half-repair in the band. Unit 18.
accept: Elle est allée au marché
questions.answer: Elle est allée au marché.
questions.prompt: Elle a allé au marché.

rounds.say: The extra word changes with the subject, because it is the subject.
rounds.label: Unit 19 · The verbs with an extra word

questions.q: Write the French for: I get up early
questions.why: Je me lève tôt. The extra word is the subject in its other shape, so it moves through all six persons rather than sitting there as a fixed particle. Unit 19.
accept: Je me lève tôt
questions.answer: Je me lève tôt.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Je ne me lève pas tôt. The two halves of the negative go round the extra word AND the verb together, because the two behave as one thing. Unit 19.
opts: Je ne me lève pas tôt.
Je ne lève pas me tôt.
Je me ne lève pas tôt.
Je ne me pas lève tôt.

questions.q: Write the nous form of se lever.
questions.why: nous nous levons. The word appears twice and that is correct: the first is the subject, the second is the object, and they happen to be spelled the same. Unit 19.
accept: nous nous levons
questions.answer: nous nous levons

questions.q: Write the French for: His name is Marc
questions.why: Il s’appelle Marc, with the extra word shortened in front of the vowel. s’appeler is one of the verbs that carries the word without turning the action back on the subject. Unit 19.
accept: Il s’appelle Marc
questions.answer: Il s’appelle Marc.

questions.q: Which means: I wash the car
questions.why: Je lave la voiture. The same verb with the extra word turns the action back on the subject, and without it takes an ordinary object. One verb, two jobs, and the extra word decides. Unit 19.

rounds.say: If the little word is there, the first word is être.
rounds.label: Unit 20 · The extra word in the past

questions.q: Which first word does se laver take in the past?
questions.why: être, always, whatever the verb takes without the extra word. laver on its own takes avoir and se laver takes être, and the little word is the whole reason. Unit 20.

questions.q: Write the French for: She got up
questions.why: Elle s’est levée. Four things in a row: subject, little word, first word, second word, and the second word agrees with the subject exactly as it did in unit 18. Unit 20.
accept: Elle s’est levée
questions.answer: Elle s’est levée.

questions.q: Write the French for: They got up (two men)
questions.why: Ils se sont levés, with the -s. Nothing in the sentence is audibly plural except the pronoun, so the whole agreement lives on the page. Unit 20.
accept: Ils se sont levés
questions.answer: Ils se sont levés.

questions.q: A learner writes « Elle s’a lavée ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Elle s’est lavée. The little word is the signal and it is a reliable one: wherever it appears, the first word is être. Unit 20.
accept: Elle s’est lavée
questions.answer: Elle s’est lavée.
questions.prompt: Elle s’a lavée.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Il ne s’est pas levé. Three elements now sit inside the wrap and the second word stays outside it, which is the same rule stretched over one more piece. Unit 20.

rounds.say: The word that replaces the thing goes in front of the verb.
rounds.label: Unit 21 · Direct object pronouns

questions.q: Replace « le livre »: I see the book.
questions.why: Je le vois. English puts it behind the verb and French puts it in front, and that placement is not optional in a finished sentence. Unit 21.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Je les vois. These three pronouns are the one part of the system the ear can settle, because le, la and les are three different vowels. Unit 21.

questions.q: Write the French for: I bought them (les fleurs)
questions.why: Je les ai achetées. The pronoun goes in front of the first word, and because it is standing in front of the verb the second word agrees with it. Unit 21.
accept: Je les ai achetées
questions.answer: Je les ai achetées.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je vois le ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je le vois. The English word order survives the vocabulary, which is why this comes out right in the head and wrong in the mouth. Unit 21.
accept: Je le vois
questions.answer: Je le vois.
questions.prompt: Je vois le.

questions.q: In « Je l’aime », what is being loved?
questions.why: The sentence does not say. In front of a vowel both le and la shorten to l’, so the gender you would have read off the pronoun is gone. Unit 21.

rounds.say: If the person sits behind à, the word is lui or leur.
rounds.label: Unit 22 · Indirect object pronouns

questions.q: Write the French for: I speak to him
questions.why: Je lui parle. parler puts its person behind à, so the pronoun is lui, and the à disappears into it rather than being said twice. Unit 22.
accept: Je lui parle
questions.answer: Je lui parle.

questions.q: Write the French for: I write to them
questions.why: Je leur écris. leur here is a pronoun and never takes an -s, whatever the number of people. The leur that does take one belongs to unit 34. Unit 22.
accept: Je leur écris
questions.answer: Je leur écris.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Je leur téléphone. téléphoner is one of the verbs English marks with nothing and French marks with à, which is why the direct pronoun feels right here and is not. Unit 22.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je leurs parle ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je leur parle. The -s is silent, so the mistake is invisible out loud and only ever appears in writing. Unit 22.
accept: Je leur parle
questions.answer: Je leur parle.
questions.prompt: Je leurs parle.

questions.q: Write the French for: I gave her the book
questions.why: Je lui ai donné le livre, with no agreement on the second word. The past form never agrees with an indirect object, which is exactly why « Elle s’est lavé les mains » does not agree either. Unit 22.
accept: Je lui ai donné le livre
questions.answer: Je lui ai donné le livre.

rounds.say: The preposition goes inside the pronoun, so it is not said twice.
rounds.label: Unit 23 · Y and en

questions.q: Write the French for: I am going there
questions.why: J’y vais. y swallows the à as well as the place, which is why saying à again after it is the classic double. Unit 23.
accept: J’y vais
questions.answer: J’y vais.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: J’en veux. y and en are two clearly different sounds, so the pair the ear cannot settle is not this one: it is which preposition the verb wanted in the first place. Unit 23.

questions.q: Which is the French for: I have three of them
questions.why: J’en ai trois. The number stays and the noun goes, and English has no word doing en’s job here at all. Unit 23.

questions.q: A learner answers « Vous avez du pain ? » with « Oui, j’ai ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Oui, j’en ai. English lets you stop at I do and French does not: the pronoun is required, not decorative. Unit 23.
accept: Oui, j’en ai
questions.answer: Oui, j’en ai.
questions.prompt: Oui, j’ai.

questions.q: Which order is right?
questions.why: Il y en a. y comes before en, and this is the one pair of these pronouns whose order the A2 band settles. Unit 23.

rounds.say: You never start. He asks, you answer.
rounds.label: Unit 24 · At the restaurant

questions.q: You sit down and the server arrives. What does he say?
questions.why: Vous avez choisi ? Your half of this encounter is the answering half, and knowing which of his eight questions has arrived is most of the work. Unit 24.

questions.q: Say it: ask for the bill
questions.why: L’addition, s’il vous plaît. Four words and it closes the encounter. The bill does not arrive on its own in France, so this one has to be said. Unit 24.
accept: L’addition, s’il vous plaît
questions.answer: L’addition, s’il vous plaît.

questions.q: Write the French for: I will have the fish
questions.why: Je vais prendre le poisson. The near future is the ordinary way to order, which is one of the two or three places where a whole grammar unit turns out to be a piece of the script. Unit 24.
accept: Je vais prendre le poisson
questions.answer: Je vais prendre le poisson.

questions.q: A learner says « Je veux le poisson » to a server. Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je voudrais le poisson. je veux is the one rung on the ordering ladder that reads as an instruction, and it is the rung an English speaker reaches for first. Unit 24.
accept: Je voudrais le poisson
questions.answer: Je voudrais le poisson.
questions.prompt: Je veux le poisson.

questions.q: You did not catch what he said. Which?
questions.why: Pardon, vous pouvez répéter ? The repair ladder is ordered by what it costs you to use, and this rung costs almost nothing. Quoi on its own costs a great deal. Unit 24.

rounds.say: The number comes once. Asking again is part of the script.
rounds.label: Unit 25 · Shopping and money

questions.q: Listen. What is the total?
questions.why: Twelve euros forty. The cents are said as a bare number with no word after them, which is what makes a price shorter than a learner expects. Unit 25.

questions.q: The cashier says « sur vingt euros ». What is the twenty?
questions.why: The note you handed over. She is counting up from the price to what you gave her, and hearing it as the change is how you walk away short. Unit 25.

questions.q: Write the French for: How much is it?
questions.why: Ça fait combien ? The same frame the cashier uses to tell you, turned round. Reusing her words is the shortest route to being understood. Unit 25.
accept: Ça fait combien
questions.answer: Ça fait combien ?

questions.q: A learner writes « un kilo des pommes ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: un kilo de pommes. A container takes a plain de and nothing else, whatever the noun behind it. Unit 25.
accept: un kilo de pommes
questions.answer: un kilo de pommes
questions.prompt: un kilo des pommes

questions.q: A shop assistant offers help and you want to look on your own. Which?
questions.why: Non merci, je regarde. Leaving without going silent is a script of its own, and this is its whole first move. Unit 25.

rounds.say: Find the joints, then take one move at a time.
rounds.label: Unit 26 · Getting about

questions.q: Write the French for: the second on the right
questions.why: la deuxième à droite. A spoken direction counts turnings, so the ordinals are the part of it you cannot afford to lose. Unit 26.
accept: la deuxième à droite
questions.answer: la deuxième à droite

questions.q: Write the French for: A return ticket, please
questions.why: Un aller-retour, s’il vous plaît. The ticket names the journey rather than the direction, so it is one word rather than a sentence. Unit 26.
accept: Un aller-retour, s’il vous plaît
questions.answer: Un aller-retour, s’il vous plaît.

questions.q: Which word separates one move from the next?
questions.why: jusqu’à, and puis, ensuite, après and au bout de do the same job. Hearing the joints is how four moves stay four moves rather than becoming one long noise. Unit 26.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je vais à métro ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je vais en métro. You go IN the things you get inside and ON the ones you sit astride, which is why it stays à pied and à vélo. Unit 26.
accept: Je vais en métro
questions.answer: Je vais en métro.
questions.prompt: Je vais à métro.

questions.q: Write the French for: Where is the station?
questions.why: Où est la gare ? The street form of the question, which is shorter than the counter form and is what you use to a passer-by. Unit 26.
accept: Où est la gare
questions.answer: Où est la gare ?

rounds.say: English gives you one shape for a symptom. French picks one of three.
rounds.label: Unit 27 · At the doctor

questions.q: Which is the French for: My head hurts
questions.why: J’ai mal à la tête. French has the pain and English is the pain, and the body part sits behind à with its article. Unit 27.
opts: Je suis mal à la tête.

questions.q: Listen. How often?
questions.why: Three times a day. Against toutes les trois heures, which is eight, and mishearing one for the other changes the amount taken. Unit 27.

questions.q: Write the French for: I have a temperature
questions.why: J’ai de la fièvre. This is the second of the three symptom shapes: avoir plus the thing itself, and the article is the one that means an amount rather than a count. Unit 27.
accept: J’ai de la fièvre
questions.answer: J’ai de la fièvre.

questions.q: A learner writes « J’ai mal à le dos ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: J’ai mal au dos. à le contracts wherever it appears, and it appears in the middle of the sentence you most need at a surgery. Unit 27.
accept: J’ai mal au dos
questions.answer: J’ai mal au dos.
questions.prompt: J’ai mal à le dos.

questions.q: You do not know the French for the symptom. What do you do?
questions.why: Describe around it. Asking for a repeat cannot help here, because the missing word is yours rather than his. Unit 27.
opts: Describe around it: c’est comme une brûlure

rounds.say: Take the person out of the sentence.
rounds.label: Unit 28 · At the hotel

questions.q: You arrive at the desk. Which?
questions.why: Bonjour, j’ai une réservation. The greeting is not optional at a desk, and the sentence after it is one you can have ready before you walk in. Unit 28.

questions.q: Say it: report that a towel is missing
questions.why: Il manque une serviette. No subject, so nobody is being accused of anything, which is the whole reason this frame exists. Unit 28.
accept: Il manque une serviette
questions.answer: Il manque une serviette.

questions.q: Write the French for: The room is too noisy
questions.why: La chambre est trop bruyante, agreeing with chambre. Reporting the room rather than the staff is the same move as il manque, one rung further up. Unit 28.
accept: La chambre est trop bruyante
questions.answer: La chambre est trop bruyante.

questions.q: A learner says « Je veux une autre chambre » at the desk. Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je voudrais une autre chambre. Correct French and still wrong: the register does the work here and je veux spends goodwill you may need later in the stay. Unit 28.
accept: Je voudrais une autre chambre
questions.answer: Je voudrais une autre chambre.
questions.prompt: Je veux une autre chambre.

questions.q: What does « toujours pas » tell the person you are speaking to?
questions.why: That you have already asked once. It marks the second asking without raising the voice, which is exactly what you want it to do. Unit 28.
opts: That you have already asked once

rounds.say: The first sentence is the anchor, not the answer.
rounds.label: Unit 29 · Work and jobs

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Je suis professeur, with no article. A job after être takes nothing in front of it, which is the one place French drops an article where English keeps one. Unit 29.

questions.q: Write the French for: I work in a school
questions.why: Je travaille dans une école. This is the second move, and stopping after the first one is what leaves the conversation on the floor. Unit 29.
accept: Je travaille dans une école
questions.answer: Je travaille dans une école.

questions.q: Say it: hand the question back
questions.why: Et vous, qu’est-ce que vous faites ? The hand-back is the fourth move and it is what turns an answer into a conversation. Unit 29.
accept: Et vous, qu’est-ce que vous faites
questions.answer: Et vous, qu’est-ce que vous faites ?
questions.target: Et vous, qu’est-ce que vous faites ?

questions.q: A learner writes « Je suis un ingénieur ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je suis ingénieur. The article comes back the moment you describe the job rather than name it: « Je suis un bon ingénieur » is correct. Unit 29.
accept: Je suis ingénieur
questions.answer: Je suis ingénieur.
questions.prompt: Je suis un ingénieur.

questions.q: Which pair are both used?
questions.why: un serveur, une serveuse. Where a pair exists this band uses it, and where one does not the masculine form covers both. Unit 29.

rounds.say: They will not know the name of your diploma. Say what it was.
rounds.label: Unit 30 · School and studies

questions.q: Which is the French for: I study maths
questions.why: Je fais des maths. faire de plus the subject is the everyday way to say it, and the article that follows de is the one that means an amount. Unit 30.

questions.q: Write the French for: I studied for three years
questions.why: J’ai étudié pendant trois ans. The span is finished, so it is pendant rather than depuis, and the verb is in the past because the studying stopped. Unit 30.
accept: J’ai étudié pendant trois ans
questions.answer: J’ai étudié pendant trois ans.

questions.q: Which is the French for: I am good at languages
questions.why: Je suis fort en langues. fort, moyen and nul are the three rungs, and the preposition is en for all three. Unit 30.

questions.q: Write the French for: I am good at maths
questions.why: Je suis fort en maths, with en and not à. The preposition here is fixed to the frame rather than chosen from the place system. Unit 30.
accept: Je suis fort en maths
questions.answer: Je suis fort en maths.

questions.q: Write the French for: I have a degree
questions.why: J’ai un diplôme. Naming the diploma tells a French listener nothing, so what follows it is how long it took and what it was in. Unit 30.
accept: J’ai un diplôme
questions.answer: J’ai un diplôme.

rounds.say: One device, three names, and the listener picks which.
rounds.label: Unit 31 · Technology

questions.q: You are on the phone to a support line. Which word for the machine?
questions.why: mon ordinateur. The full word to somebody official, the short one to a friend. The device does not change and the listener does. Unit 31.

questions.q: Write the French for: I do not have wifi
questions.why: Je n’ai pas de wifi. After avoir in the negative the article collapses to de, which is a rule from A1 doing its work inside a sentence about a router. Unit 31.
accept: Je n’ai pas de wifi
questions.answer: Je n’ai pas de wifi.

questions.q: A French screen offers to help you sign in again. Which does it say?
questions.why: Mot de passe oublié. Interface strings are learnt whole rather than built, because the screen will not accept a synonym. Unit 31.

questions.q: Write the French for: I am going to send an email
questions.why: Je vais envoyer un mail. envoyer, not téléphoner: the verb English shares between a call and a message is two verbs in French. Unit 31.
accept: Je vais envoyer un mail
questions.answer: Je vais envoyer un mail.

questions.q: Write the French for: I forgot my password
questions.why: J’ai oublié mon mot de passe. The screen says it without a subject and you say it with one, which is the difference between reading a button and asking for help. Unit 31.
accept: J’ai oublié mon mot de passe
questions.answer: J’ai oublié mon mot de passe.

rounds.say: Pick the middle word and keep the frame.
rounds.label: Unit 32 · Comparatives and superlatives

questions.q: Which is the French for: taller than me
questions.why: plus grand que moi. One frame with one slot in the middle, and que plus its object is not optional: dropping it gives a sentence that means something else. Unit 32.

questions.q: Write the French for: the most beautiful city
questions.why: la plus belle ville. The same frame with an article in front, and it is the article that carries the agreement rather than the describing word. Unit 32.
accept: la plus belle ville
questions.answer: la plus belle ville

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Elle chante mieux. mieux goes with a verb and meilleur goes with a noun, which is the whole of the split. plus bon and plus bien do not exist. Unit 32.
opts: Elle chante plus bien que moi.
Elle chante plus bon que moi.

questions.q: A learner writes « Il est plus grand de moi ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Il est plus grand que moi. que is the comparison word and de belongs to the superlative, which is why the two get swapped. Unit 32.
accept: Il est plus grand que moi
questions.answer: Il est plus grand que moi.
questions.prompt: Il est plus grand de moi.

questions.q: Write the French for: the best restaurant in the city
questions.why: le meilleur restaurant de la ville, with de and not dans. A superlative names the field it is the best of, and the field takes de. Unit 32.
accept: le meilleur restaurant de la ville
questions.answer: le meilleur restaurant de la ville

rounds.say: A noun after it means it points. No noun means it replaces.
rounds.label: Unit 33 · This one and that one

questions.q: Which goes in: « ___ homme »?
questions.why: cet homme. The h is silent so a vowel sound is coming, and ce cannot sit in front of one. It sounds exactly like cette and it is not spelled like it. Unit 33.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: ces livres. ce and ces are two different vowels, so the number is audible here, which is the opposite of what happens in the pronoun series. Unit 33.

questions.q: Write the French for: this table
questions.why: cette table. The word is chosen by the noun coming after it, so what you have to know is the gender of the thing rather than anything about the pointing. Unit 33.
accept: cette table
questions.answer: cette table

questions.q: A learner writes « Je préfère celui ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je préfère celui-ci. The replacing word cannot end a sentence: it needs -ci, -là, a de phrase or a clause behind it, and bare it is not French. Unit 33.
accept: Je préfère celui-ci
Je préfère celui-là
questions.answer: Je préfère celui-ci.
questions.prompt: Je préfère celui.

questions.q: Which is NOT a member of either series?
questions.why: c’est vrai. The ce in c’est is a subject standing in for nothing in particular, and it neither points at a noun nor replaces one. Unit 33.

rounds.say: Two words, and the thing owned picks them both.
rounds.label: Unit 34 · Mine, yours and theirs

questions.q: Somebody asks whose car it is. Which?
questions.why: C’est la mienne, because voiture is feminine. The form follows the thing owned and not the person owning it, and the article in front is compulsory. Unit 34.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: les miens. The -s is silent on all eighteen forms, so the number you hear is carried by the article alone. Unit 34.

questions.q: Write the French for: yours (a book, speaking to a friend)
questions.why: le tien, because livre is masculine and you are using tu. Two decisions, and only one of them is about the owner. Unit 34.
accept: le tien
questions.answer: le tien

questions.q: Write the French for: That car is mine
questions.why: Cette voiture est la mienne. Both words are picked by voiture, and leaving the article off is the mistake English trains, because English says mine with nothing in front of it. Unit 34.
accept: Cette voiture est la mienne
questions.answer: Cette voiture est la mienne.

questions.q: Which « leur » takes an -s?
questions.why: leurs enfants, where leur sits in front of a noun. As the word that replaces a person behind à it never takes one, and as the possessive pronoun le leur it takes one only in les leurs. Unit 34.

sections.say: Read the round scores, not the total.
sections.body: The percentage at the top is the least useful number on that screen. What is worth reading is the list underneath it, because a round is a unit and a low round is an afternoon of work rather than a verdict on your French. Three or four weak rounds after thirty-four units is an ordinary result, and the fix is specific: go back to those units, sit them again, and come back here. Watch in particular for a run of weak rounds rather than a scattering. Three low scores anywhere between rounds sixteen and twenty is the past tense rather than four separate problems, and it is one afternoon rather than four.
sections.title: Where You Are
points: Every round is one unit, so a low score has an address.
Read the round scores rather than the total. The total hides which unit went.
A run of low rounds next to each other is usually one gap, not three.
The exam is a separate sitting, and it is the one that answers whether you have A2.

errorTriggers.description: Builds a form the verb does not have, or borrows one family’s endings for another.
Loses the stem change: the e in mangeons, the doubled l, the accent that turns.
Conjugates the second verb, or puts the wrong one of the three tenses in the slot.
Reaches for avoir where French wants être, or leaves the participle unagreed after it.
Builds a past form that has to be reached for, or drops the ending that agrees.
Wraps the wrong half of a two-word verb, or leaves an article the negative collapses.
Leaves a describing word in its plain form, or agrees one that never moves.
Puts the standing-in word behind the verb, or picks the direct one where French wants the other.
Says the preposition twice, or drops a word English lets you leave out.
Picks the pointing or owning word off the owner rather than off the thing owned.
Picks the wrong little word in front of a place, or in front of a length of time.
Answers a script on the wrong rung, or starts a turn that was not theirs to start.

grammarAssumed: The whole A2 band, seq 1 to 34. Every question quotes a unit that has already been taught and none of them is taught again here

acts.title: The brief
acts.milestone: You know the rules of the sitting.

acts.title: Sixty questions
acts.milestone: A2 complete.

lessons.intro: Sixty questions across twelve parts, grouped by what they ask you to do rather than by unit, so that nothing tells you which lesson a question came from. Half of it is the verb. No explanations until the end, and no drills. Seventy percent is a pass.
lessons.title: L’examen A2
lessons.reframe: Nothing in here carries an address.

overview.introFr: Soixante questions, douze parties, aucune indication de leçon.

sections.say: Sixty questions, and it will not help you while you answer.

goals.s: Each part is a job rather than a unit, and every one of them crosses three or four units. Nothing in here carries an address.
goals.t: Sixty questions, twelve parts

goals.s: Six parts on the three tenses, three on the words that stand in for things, two on the everyday encounters and one on what modifies them.
goals.t: Half of it is the verb

goals.s: Right or wrong, you get the next question. Everything you missed is collected and explained on the result card, with the unit to go back to.
goals.t: No explanations until the end

goals.s: Sit the review first if you have not. Coming here cold is allowed and it mostly tells you what you already suspected.
goals.t: Seventy percent is a pass

sections.title: The Exam

sections.say: Once you start, it does not stop to explain.
sections.body: Nothing in here carries an address. That is the only way this differs from the review, and it is the whole difficulty.
sections.title: Before You Start

sections.say: Twelve parts. Nothing is explained until you finish.
sections.title: L’examen A2

rounds.say: Five verbs, and none of them tells you which family it is in.
rounds.label: Saying what happens

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Ils finissent. The regular -ir family puts -iss- in front of every plural ending. Lesson 3 in A2.

questions.q: Write the French for: We are waiting for the bus
questions.why: Nous attendons le bus, with no preposition: attendre carries its object directly where English needs for. Lesson 4 in A2.
accept: Nous attendons le bus
questions.answer: Nous attendons le bus.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Ils répondent. The stem-final d is silent at the end of a word and said when a letter follows it. Lesson 4 in A2.

questions.q: A learner writes « Nous mangons ensemble ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: nous mangeons. The e protects the soft g in front of the o, and the nous cell is the only one where it appears. Lesson 2 in A2.
accept: Nous mangeons ensemble
questions.answer: Nous mangeons ensemble.
questions.prompt: Nous mangons ensemble.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: nous appelons, with one l. The doubling belongs to the cells whose ending is silent, and -ons is not one of them. Lesson 2 in A2.

rounds.say: Nothing here can be built out of a stem and an ending.
rounds.label: The verbs that go their own way

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: vous faites. Three verbs take -tes in this cell and you have all three: être, faire and dire. Lesson 6 in A2.

questions.q: Write the French for: They take the train
questions.why: Ils prennent, with two n holding the vowel open in front of a silent ending. Lesson 9 in A2.
accept: Ils prennent le train
questions.answer: Ils prennent le train.

questions.q: Which verb goes in: « Elle ne ___ pas où j’habite. »
questions.why: Elle ne sait pas où j’habite. A clause behind it takes savoir; connaître stops at a noun. Lesson 8 in A2.

questions.q: A learner writes « Ils veut partir ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Ils veulent partir. The plural stem is the singular stem plus the last consonant of the nous stem, across all three of these verbs. Lesson 7 in A2.
accept: Ils veulent partir
questions.answer: Ils veulent partir.
questions.prompt: Ils veut partir.

questions.q: Write the French for: We are going to the market
questions.why: Nous allons au marché. aller for the verb, and à plus le folded into au for the place. Lesson 5 in A2 and lesson 13 in A2.
accept: Nous allons au marché
questions.answer: Nous allons au marché.

rounds.say: Two verbs in a row, and only the first one moves.
rounds.label: What has not happened yet

questions.q: Write the French for: I am going to leave at six
questions.why: Je vais partir. aller carries the person and the verb behind it stays in its naming form. Lesson 15 in A2.
accept: Je vais partir à six heures
questions.answer: Je vais partir à six heures.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Nous n’allons pas sortir. The negative wraps the verb that changed, and ne shortens in front of the vowel. Lesson 15 in A2.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Je viens de manger, which is twenty minutes ago rather than tonight. Four ways of placing one action in time, separated by their first word. Lesson 5 in A2.

questions.q: A learner writes « Elle doit partir maintenant, elle doit part ». Write the second half corrected.
questions.why: elle doit partir. The second verb never takes a person, behind a modal or behind aller. Lesson 7 in A2.
accept: elle doit partir
questions.answer: elle doit partir
questions.prompt: elle doit part

questions.q: Which of these is a plan rather than a journey?
questions.why: Je vais travailler. aller plus a verb is the future; aller plus a place is movement. The next word is the only thing separating them. Lesson 15 in A2.

rounds.say: Two words, and the small ones go in between.
rounds.label: What you did

questions.q: Write the French for: I finished the work yesterday
questions.why: J’ai fini. The -ir family gives -i, and the past form after avoir never agrees with anything. Lesson 16 in A2.
accept: J’ai fini le travail hier
questions.answer: J’ai fini le travail hier.

questions.q: Which is the past form of attendre?
questions.why: attendu. One ending per regular family: -é, -i and -u. Lesson 16 in A2.

questions.q: Write the French for: She has not eaten
questions.why: Elle n’a pas mangé, with no -e on the past form: after avoir there is no agreement with the subject in any person. Lesson 16 in A2.
accept: Elle n’a pas mangé
questions.answer: Elle n’a pas mangé.

questions.q: A learner writes « J’ai bien pas dormi ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je n’ai pas bien dormi. The negative goes round the first word and the short adverb sits in the gap after it. Lesson 16 in A2 and lesson 12 in A2.
accept: Je n’ai pas bien dormi
questions.answer: Je n’ai pas bien dormi.
questions.prompt: J’ai bien pas dormi.

questions.q: Which means: I finished ten minutes ago
questions.why: il y a dix minutes. A measurement of time behind it makes it ago; a plain noun behind it makes it there is. Lesson 14 in A2.
opts: J’ai fini il y a dix minutes.

rounds.say: The family ending will not help you here.
rounds.label: The forms you cannot build

questions.q: Write the past form of mettre.
questions.why: mis. An -re verb giving -is rather than -u, exactly as prendre gives pris. Lesson 17 in A2.
accept: mis
questions.answer: mis

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: J’ai vu. voir is one of the forms that has to be reached for rather than derived. Lesson 17 in A2.

questions.q: Write the French for: They understood
questions.why: Ils ont compris. Cover the prefix and comprendre is prendre, so the past form comes free. Lesson 17 in A2 and lesson 9 in A2.
accept: Ils ont compris
questions.answer: Ils ont compris.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: J’ai dû partir, with the little roof, which is all that separates it in writing from the du that means some. Lesson 17 in A2.

questions.q: A learner writes « J’ai ouvri la porte ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: J’ai ouvert. An -ir verb giving -ert, with offrir and souffrir alongside it. Lesson 17 in A2.
accept: J’ai ouvert la porte
questions.answer: J’ai ouvert la porte.
questions.prompt: J’ai ouvri la porte.

rounds.say: Some of these move the second word as well.
rounds.label: When the first word changes

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Elle est arrivée. arriver is one of the fifteen, and once the first word is être the second one agrees with the subject. Lesson 18 in A2.

questions.q: Write the French for: They went out (two women)
questions.why: Elles sont sorties, with -es. Nothing here is audibly feminine or plural except the pronoun. Lesson 18 in A2.
accept: Elles sont sorties
questions.answer: Elles sont sorties.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Il est mort. mourir is the one verb of the fifteen whose agreement you can hear, because the feminine ending lets the t out. Lesson 18 in A2.

questions.q: Tap the letters you do not say in « levées ».
questions.why: The final e and s are both silent, so all four written forms are one sound and the agreement is a fact about the page. Lesson 20 in A2.

questions.q: A learner writes « Ils se ont couchés tard ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Ils se sont couchés. Wherever the little word appears, the first word is être, whatever the verb takes without it. Lesson 20 in A2.
accept: Ils se sont couchés tard
questions.answer: Ils se sont couchés tard.
questions.prompt: Ils se ont couchés tard.

rounds.say: Where it goes, and which one it is.
rounds.label: Standing in for the thing

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Je lui téléphone. téléphoner puts its person behind à, so the pronoun is lui, and it goes in front of the verb. Lesson 22 in A2.

questions.q: Write the French for: I saw them yesterday (les enfants)
questions.why: Je les ai vus, with -s. The pronoun sits in front of the first word and the past form agrees with it because it came first. Lesson 21 in A2.
accept: Je les ai vus hier
questions.answer: Je les ai vus hier.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: Je la vois. Three pronouns, three vowels, and this is the one part of the system the ear can settle on its own. Lesson 21 in A2.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je leurs ai écrit ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je leur ai écrit. As the word replacing a person behind à it never takes an -s, and the past form never agrees with it either. Lesson 22 in A2.
accept: Je leur ai écrit
questions.answer: Je leur ai écrit.
questions.prompt: Je leurs ai écrit.

questions.q: Write the French for: I am not going to buy it (le livre)
questions.why: Je ne vais pas l’acheter. The pronoun goes in front of the verb it belongs to, and the negative still wraps the one that changed. Lesson 21 in A2 and lesson 15 in A2.
accept: Je ne vais pas l’acheter
questions.answer: Je ne vais pas l’acheter.

rounds.say: Two words that swallow the preposition as well.
rounds.label: A place and an amount

questions.q: Write the French for: I am going there tomorrow
questions.why: J’y vais. y takes the à and the place together, which is why saying à again after it is the classic double. Lesson 23 in A2.
accept: J’y vais demain
questions.answer: J’y vais demain.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Oui, j’en veux. English lets you stop at I do and French does not: the pronoun is required rather than optional. Lesson 23 in A2.

questions.q: Listen. Which one was it?
questions.why: J’en ai deux. The number stays and the noun goes, which is a shape English has no word for at all. Lesson 23 in A2.

questions.q: Write the French for: There is no more bread
questions.why: Il n’y a plus de pain. il y a does not come apart, and after a negative the article collapses to de. Lesson 23 in A2 and lesson 24 in A2.
accept: Il n’y a plus de pain
questions.answer: Il n’y a plus de pain.

questions.q: Which order is right?
questions.why: Il y en a trois. y comes before en, and it is the one pair of these pronouns whose order this level settles. Lesson 23 in A2.

rounds.say: Two little words, and what comes after decides them.
rounds.label: Pointing and owning

questions.q: Which goes in: « ___ hôtel est cher »?
questions.why: Cet hôtel. The h is silent so a vowel sound is coming. It sounds exactly like cette and it is not spelled like it. Lesson 33 in A2.

questions.q: Write the French for: This one is mine (une valise)
questions.why: Celle-ci est la mienne. Both words follow valise, and both need what comes after them: -ci on the first, an article in front of the second. Lesson 33 in A2 and lesson 34 in A2.
accept: Celle-ci est la mienne
questions.answer: Celle-ci est la mienne.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: Ce sont les leurs. The possessive pronoun is two words and the article is not optional, which is the reverse of the possessive that sits in front of a noun. Lesson 34 in A2.

questions.q: A learner writes « Je préfère celui de rouge ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: Je préfère le rouge. celui needs -ci, -là, a de phrase naming an owner, or a clause; a colour behind de is none of those. Lesson 33 in A2.
accept: Je préfère le rouge
questions.answer: Je préfère le rouge.
questions.prompt: Je préfère celui de rouge.

questions.q: Which « leur » takes an -s?
questions.why: leurs livres, where it sits in front of a noun. As the word replacing a person behind à it never takes one. Lesson 22 in A2 and lesson 34 in A2.

rounds.say: Everything here modifies something else.
rounds.label: Describing and comparing

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: un nouvel appartement. Say the feminine and drop its last two letters, and the same move gives bel and vieil. Lesson 11 in A2.

questions.q: Write the French for: She speaks slowly
questions.why: Elle parle lentement, built off the feminine lente, and it goes behind the verb. Lesson 12 in A2.
accept: Elle parle lentement
questions.answer: Elle parle lentement.

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: mieux, because it is modifying a verb. meilleur goes with a noun, and plus bon and plus bien do not exist. Lesson 32 in A2.
opts: Elle travaille plus bien que moi.
Elle travaille plus bon que moi.

questions.q: A learner writes « une femme sportif et heureux ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: sportive et heureuse. Two classes, two feminines, and both of them are audible, which is unusual: number never is. Lesson 10 in A2.
accept: une femme sportive et heureuse
questions.answer: une femme sportive et heureuse
questions.prompt: une femme sportif et heureux

questions.q: Write the French for: the oldest hotel in the city
questions.why: le plus vieil hôtel de la ville. The pre-vocalic form survives inside the superlative frame, and the field a superlative names takes de. Lesson 11 in A2 and lesson 32 in A2.
accept: le plus vieil hôtel de la ville
questions.answer: le plus vieil hôtel de la ville

rounds.say: Somebody is waiting for you, and it is his turn first.
rounds.label: At the counter

questions.q: The server arrives at your table. What has he said?
questions.why: Vous avez choisi ? Your half of this encounter is the answering half, and recognising which question arrived is most of the work. Lesson 24 in A2.

questions.q: Say it: order the fish
questions.why: Je vais prendre le poisson. The near future is the ordinary way to order, so a whole grammar unit turns out to be a piece of the script. Lesson 24 in A2 and lesson 15 in A2.
accept: Je vais prendre le poisson
questions.answer: Je vais prendre le poisson.

questions.q: Write the French for: Do you take card?
questions.why: Vous prenez la carte ? Rising intonation and nothing else, which is the question form a counter actually uses. Lesson 25 in A2.
accept: Vous prenez la carte
questions.answer: Vous prenez la carte ?

questions.q: A learner asks for « une bouteille du vin ». Write it out corrected.
questions.why: une bouteille de vin. A container takes a plain de, whatever the noun behind it. Lesson 25 in A2.
accept: une bouteille de vin
questions.answer: une bouteille de vin
questions.prompt: une bouteille du vin

questions.q: The cashier says « sur cinquante euros ». What is the fifty?
questions.why: The note you handed over. She is counting up from the price, and hearing it as the change is how you leave short. Lesson 25 in A2.

rounds.say: A street, a surgery, a desk and an office.
rounds.label: Out in the world

questions.q: Which is right?
questions.why: J’ai mal au ventre. French has the pain where English is it, and à le contracts wherever it appears. Lesson 27 in A2.

questions.q: Write the French for: Take the second on the left
questions.why: Prenez la deuxième à gauche. A spoken direction counts turnings, so the ordinal is the part you cannot afford to lose. Lesson 26 in A2.
accept: Prenez la deuxième à gauche
questions.answer: Prenez la deuxième à gauche.

questions.q: Something in your room has not been dealt with. Which?
questions.why: Il manque une serviette. No subject, so nobody is accused of anything, which is the whole reason the frame exists. Lesson 28 in A2.

questions.q: Write the French for: I have worked here for two years
questions.why: Je travaille ici depuis deux ans, in the present, because you still work there. English reaches for a past tense and French does not. Lesson 14 in A2 and lesson 29 in A2.
accept: Je travaille ici depuis deux ans
questions.answer: Je travaille ici depuis deux ans.

questions.q: Write the French for: My phone does not work
questions.why: Mon téléphone ne marche pas. marcher for a device, not travailler, which is the verb for a person. Lesson 31 in A2.
accept: Mon téléphone ne marche pas
questions.answer: Mon téléphone ne marche pas.

sections.say: What the number means, and what comes after it.
sections.body: Seventy percent across sixty mixed questions is a real A2, and it is worth being clear about what that means, because it is easy to undersell. It means you can talk about yesterday and about now in the same breath, plan tomorrow, say what you want and can and have to do, replace half the nouns in a sentence with the small words that stand in for them, describe and compare, and get through a restaurant, a till, a station, a surgery, a hotel desk and a first day at work without the sentence dying in the middle. Below seventy, the part scores tell you roughly where it went and the review lesson tells you exactly. There is no version of this where the answer is start over.
sections.title: That Is A2
points: Nothing in here carries an address.
A part is a job, not a unit, so a weak part usually means three units rather than one.
The three past-tense parts are a quarter of the paper, because that is what A2 is judged on.
Sit the review lesson for anything that went badly, then come back and sit this again.

recorded.desc: THE THREE vous FORMS, IN ONE TAKE, AND THE THREE MUST SOUND EQUALLY ORDINARY: « Vous faites le lit. » then « Vous dites bonjour. » then « Vous lisez le menu. » This is the single most important instruction in this lesson. The whole screen is that two of these three walk away from an ending and the third does not, and the learner has to notice that from the SPELLING rather than from the reading. A reader who knows faites is the difficult one will lean on it, put a fraction of extra space in front of it, or brighten it; every one of those instincts has to be suppressed completely. If a listener can tell which of the three is the odd one out with their eyes shut, the recording has done the work the screen is asking the learner to do. Conversational pace, no teaching pause anywhere, and the three back to back.

THE SIX NUMBER LINES, IN THREE PAIRS, SINGULAR THEN PLURAL, EACH PAIR IN ONE TAKE: Il fait le lit / Ils font le lit, Il dit bonjour / Ils disent bonjour, Il lit le menu / Ils lisent le menu. Here the difference MUST be audible, which is the opposite instruction from the vous clip and is why they are separate recordings. Pair one is the big one: FEH against FOHⁿ is a completely different vowel and it goes into the nose, so do not soften it. Pairs two and three land a z at the very end of the verb and change nothing else at all, so the z must be clean and the vowel in front of it must not move. In every pair the PRONOUN must sound identical on both sides, because it is: il and ils are one sound. Any difference in the pronoun destroys the pair, because the learner will use it instead of the verb.

ALL THREE PARADIGMS, IN THE USUAL PRONOUN ORDER (je, tu, il, nous, vous, ils), one voice, one speed, faire then dire then lire, and the ten dictée sentences come out of this same take. Within each verb THE FIRST THREE MUST BE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM EACH OTHER: fais, fais and fait are one sound, dis, dis and dit are one sound, lis, lis and lit are one sound. Do not help by touching the final letter of any of them; the learner is being taught that the page is the only place those differences exist. nous faisons is the one to watch in the other direction: it is fuh-ZOHⁿ and not feh-ZOHⁿ, and a reader looking at the spelling will want to say the ai. The dictée sentences are the ones a learner replays four times while typing, so they need to be even in pace and completely flat in emphasis: any lean on an ending is a hint the screen is not supposed to give.

ONE EXPRESSION FROM EACH OF THE SIX GROUPS, read as a flat list at conversational pace, one voice: faire les courses, faire le lit, faire du sport, faire un voyage, il fait beau, faire la cuisine. The instruction is sameness. Every one of these begins with the same syllable and that repetition IS the teaching, so do not vary the intonation to keep the list interesting and do not put a break after faire in any of them: these are single lexical units to a French speaker and reading them as verb-plus-object teaches the learner to assemble what they should be storing whole. Keep roughly a second between them so a learner can repeat into the gap.

The three naming forms alone, read as a flat list at conversational pace, one voice: faire, dire, lire. The last two rhyme and the first does not, and that is a fact about them rather than something to perform. Keep roughly a second between them so a learner can repeat into the gap.

The ten do-and-make expressions, one take, flat: faire les courses, faire le ménage, faire la vaisselle, faire la lessive, faire ses devoirs, faire le lit, faire du bruit, faire un effort, faire des progrès, faire une erreur. Ten phrases beginning with the same word is monotonous to read and the monotony is the point, so resist varying it. No break after faire in any of them.

The eight go-and-take expressions, one take, flat: faire du sport, faire du vélo, faire du ski, faire de la natation, faire de la musique, faire une promenade, faire un voyage, faire les valises. The small word between faire and the noun (du, de la) must be unstressed and quick: a learner who hears it emphasised will think it is a choice they have to make, and this lesson deliberately does not teach that choice.

The seven expressions where English has a verb of its own, one take, flat: faire la cuisine, faire la queue, faire la fête, faire la sieste, faire attention, faire semblant, faire plaisir. faire semblant is two nasal vowels in a row and no n is released in either; do not let the second one become a consonant. faire attention runs the two words together across the vowel and should not be separated.

The five weather expressions, one take, flat, and read exactly as lesson 14 in A1 reads them: il fait beau, il fait chaud, il fait froid, il fait frais, il fait mauvais. The learner has heard these before as single lumps and this lesson is taking them apart, so the reading must NOT change to help: no extra space after fait, no lift on the adjective. If they sound different here from the way they sound in lesson 14 in A1, the learner will conclude that the two lessons are about two different things, which is the opposite of what this mission says.

The opening scene, French bubbles only. A flatmate at a kitchen table on a Sunday morning, entirely relaxed, holding a pen over a list. He is not testing anybody and he is not impatient: the whole scene turns on nobody minding, so any edge in « Alors, tu fais quoi ce matin ? » or any resignation in « D'accord. Je m'occupe du reste. » would destroy it. He asked an ordinary question, got nothing back, and moved on, and he is right to have done so.
