items.ipa: /il paʁl fʁɑ̃.sɛ/
items.respell: eel parl frahⁿ-SEH
items.notes: Said exactly like Ils parlent français. Nothing in the sound separates them.

items.fr: Nous parlons français.
items.en: We speak French.
items.ipa: /nu paʁ.lɔ̃ fʁɑ̃.sɛ/
items.respell: noo par-lohⁿ frahⁿ-SEH
items.notes: One of the two endings you can hear. Out loud most rooms say on parle instead.

items.fr: Vous parlez français.
items.en: You speak French.
items.ipa: /vu paʁ.le fʁɑ̃.sɛ/
items.respell: voo par-lay frahⁿ-SEH
items.notes: The other audible one, and it sounds exactly like the infinitive parler.

items.fr: Ils parlent français.
items.en: They speak French.
items.ipa: /il paʁl fʁɑ̃.sɛ/
items.respell: eel parl frahⁿ-SEH
items.notes: Six letters at the end and not one of them sounds. Identical to Il parle français.

items.fr: Nous regardons la télé.
items.en: We watch TV.
items.ipa: /nu ʁə.ɡaʁ.dɔ̃ la te.le/
items.respell: noo ruh-gar-dohⁿ la tay-LAY
items.notes: What you write.

items.fr: On regarde la télé.
items.en: We watch TV.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ ʁə.ɡaʁd la te.le/
items.respell: ohⁿ ruh-gard la tay-LAY
items.notes: What you say. Same meaning, and on takes the form il takes.

items.fr: Elle travaille ici.
items.en: She works here.
items.ipa: /ɛl tʁa.vaj i.si/
items.respell: el tra-vahy ee-SEE
items.notes: One person.

items.fr: Elles travaillent ici.
items.en: They work here.
items.ipa: /ɛl tʁa.vaj i.si/
items.respell: el tra-vahy ee-SEE
items.notes: A whole team, and not one sound has changed. Only elles told you.

items.fr: Tu cherches la gare.
items.en: You are looking for the station.
items.ipa: /ty ʃɛʁʃ la ɡaʁ/
items.respell: tü shairsh la GAR
items.notes: Four letters at the end, no sound.

items.fr: Il cherche la gare.
items.en: He is looking for the station.
items.ipa: /il ʃɛʁʃ la ɡaʁ/
items.respell: eel shairsh la GAR
items.notes: The verb is the same sound as tu cherches. The pronoun is the whole difference.

items.fr: Ils parlent fort.
items.en: They talk loudly.
items.ipa: /il paʁl fɔʁ/
items.respell: eel parl FOR
items.notes: The -ent that everyone wants to say. It is not there.

items.fr: ceux-là
items.en: those (masculine)
items.respell: suh-LAH

items.fr: celles-ci
items.en: these (feminine)
items.respell: sehl-SEE

items.fr: Je préfère ceux-là.
items.en: I prefer those.
items.respell: zhuh pray-FEHR suh-LAH

items.fr: Ce sac est petit, mais celui-là est grand.
items.en: This bag is small, but that one is big.
items.respell: suh SAK eh puh-TEE meh suh-lwee-LAH eh GRAHⁿ

items.fr: Cette robe est bleue, mais celle-là est noire.
items.en: This dress is blue, but that one is black.
items.respell: seht ROB eh BLUH meh sehl-LAH eh NWAR

items.fr: Ces gants sont noirs, mais ceux-là sont blancs.
items.en: These gloves are black, but those are white.
items.respell: say GAHⁿ sohⁿ NWAR meh suh-LAH sohⁿ BLAHⁿ

items.fr: Ces chaussures sont neuves, mais celles-là sont vieilles.
items.en: These shoes are new, but those are old.
items.respell: say shoh-SÜR sohⁿ NUHV meh sehl-LAH sohⁿ VYEY

items.fr: celle-là
items.en: that one (fem.)
items.ipa: /sɛlla/
items.respell: sehl-LAH

items.fr: Elles dansent bien.
items.en: They dance well.
items.ipa: /ɛl dɑ̃s bjɛ̃/
items.respell: el dahⁿs BYAⁿ
items.notes: dansent is one syllable. The -ent adds nothing you can hear.

items.fr: Nous cherchons la gare.
items.en: We are looking for the station.
items.ipa: /nu ʃɛʁ.ʃɔ̃ la ɡaʁ/
items.respell: noo shair-shohⁿ la GAR
items.notes: Here the ending is a syllable and you hear it.

items.fr: Vous cherchez la gare.
items.en: You are looking for the station.
items.ipa: /vu ʃɛʁ.ʃe la ɡaʁ/
items.respell: voo shair-shay la GAR
items.notes: And here. These two are the only ones the ear can pick out on its own.

items.fr: J'aime beaucoup mon quartier.
items.en: I like my neighbourhood a lot.
items.ipa: /ʒɛm bo.ku mɔ̃ kaʁ.tje/
items.respell: zhem bo-koo mohⁿ kar-TYAY
items.notes: je aime cannot stand, so je loses its e. The ending is still silent.

items.fr: On donne son adresse à l'agent.
items.en: You give your address to the officer.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ dɔn sɔ̃.na.dʁɛs a la.ʒɑ̃/
items.respell: ohⁿ don sohⁿ-na-dress a la-ZHAHⁿ
items.notes: on takes the il form, so it is donne and never donnons.

items.fr: Tu montres tes papiers à l'entrée.
items.en: You show your papers at the entrance.
items.ipa: /ty mɔ̃tʁ te pa.pje a lɑ̃.tʁe/
items.respell: tü mohⁿtr tay pa-pyay a lahⁿ-TRAY

items.fr: Tu trouves toujours une solution.
items.en: You always find a solution.
items.ipa: /ty tʁuv tu.ʒuʁ yn sɔ.ly.sjɔ̃/
items.respell: tü troov too-zhoor ün so-lü-SYOHⁿ

items.fr: Elle habite près de la gare.
items.en: She lives near the station.
items.ipa: /ɛ la.bit pʁɛ də la ɡaʁ/
items.respell: e la-beet preh duh la GAR
items.notes: elle habite runs together as one word, and the ending is still silent underneath it.

items.fr: Nous restons à la maison.
items.en: We are staying home.
items.ipa: /nu ʁɛs.tɔ̃ a la mɛ.zɔ̃/
items.respell: noo res-tohⁿ a la meh-ZOHⁿ

items.fr: Vous travaillez le samedi ?
items.en: Do you work on Saturdays?
items.ipa: /vu tʁa.va.je lə sam.di/
items.respell: voo tra-va-yay luh sam-DEE
items.notes: travaillez sounds exactly like travailler. Only the vous in front tells you which one it is.

items.fr: Ils arrivent demain matin.
items.en: They arrive tomorrow morning.
items.ipa: /il.za.ʁiv də.mɛ̃ ma.tɛ̃/
items.respell: eel-za-reev duh-maⁿ ma-TAⁿ
items.notes: The silent s of ils wakes up in front of the vowel. The -ent at the end still does nothing.

items.fr: Je mange ici.
items.en: I eat here.
items.ipa: /ʒə mɑ̃ʒ i.si/
items.respell: zhuh mahⁿzh ee-SEE
items.notes: No change. The ending is silent and there is no o for the g to go hard in front of.

items.fr: Elle étudie le français.
items.en: She studies French.
items.ipa: /ɛ le.ty.di lə fʁɑ̃.sɛ/
items.respell: e lay-tü-dee luh frahⁿ-SEH
items.notes: The stem ends in a vowel already, so the silent -e just sits behind it.

items.fr: Nous téléphonons à nos voisins.
items.en: We phone our neighbours.
items.ipa: /nu te.le.fɔ.nɔ̃ a no vwa.zɛ̃/
items.respell: noo tay-lay-fo-nohⁿ a no vwa-ZAⁿ

items.fr: Nous mangeons ici.
items.en: We eat here.
items.ipa: /nu mɑ̃.ʒɔ̃ i.si/
items.respell: noo mahⁿ-ZHOHⁿ ee-SEE
items.notes: The e is written so the g stays soft in front of the o. Without it: mangons, with a hard g.

items.fr: Il commence ici.
items.en: He starts here.
items.ipa: /il kɔ.mɑ̃s i.si/
items.respell: eel koh-MAHⁿS ee-SEE
items.notes: No change. The plain c is already soft in front of the silent e.

items.fr: entrer
items.en: to enter, to go in
items.ipa: /ɑ̃tʁe/
items.respell: ahⁿ-TRAY
items.notes: regular -er verb

items.fr: chanter
items.en: to sing
items.ipa: ʃɑ̃.te
items.respell: shahⁿ-TAY

example.en: We are going to sing together.
example.fr: Nous allons chanter ensemble.

items.fr: danser
items.en: to dance
items.ipa: dɑ̃.se
items.respell: dahⁿ-SAY

example.en: They dance during the party.
example.fr: Ils dansent pendant la fête.

items.fr: Nous commençons.
items.en: We start.
items.ipa: /nu kɔ.mɑ̃.sɔ̃/
items.respell: noo koh-mahⁿ-SOHⁿ
items.notes: The tail under the c is what keeps it soft in front of the o. Without it: commencons, said koh-mahⁿ-KOHⁿ.

items.fr: Vous voyagez en train.
items.en: You travel by train.
items.ipa: /vu vwa.ja.ʒe ɑ̃ tʁɛ̃/
items.respell: voo vwah-yah-ZHAY ahⁿ TRAⁿ
items.notes: No change. The ending starts with e, not o, so the g was never in danger.

items.fr: Nous voyageons en train.
items.en: We travel by train.
items.ipa: /nu vwa.ja.ʒɔ̃ ɑ̃ tʁɛ̃/
items.respell: noo vwah-yah-ZHOHⁿ ahⁿ TRAⁿ
items.notes: The same e as mangeons, on a second verb, so the pattern reads as a system rather than a word.

items.fr: Je préfère le thé.
items.en: I prefer tea.
items.ipa: /ʒə pʁe.fɛʁ lə te/
items.respell: zhuh pray-FEHR luh TAY
items.notes: The ending is silent, so fère is the last sound in the word and the vowel opens.

items.fr: Je parle français.
items.en: I speak French.
items.respell: zhuh parl frahⁿ-SEH
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je","t":"I"},{"w":"parle","t":"speak"},{"w":"français.","t":"French"}]}

items.fr: Nous sommes arrivés le premier septembre.
items.en: We arrived on September first.
items.ipa: nu sɔm.z‿a.ʁi.ve lə pʁə.mje sɛp.tɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: Only "le premier" uses the ordinal for dates, every other day uses a plain number like le deux, le trois.

items.fr: Ils vont célébrer leurs retrouvailles le trente et un décembre.
items.en: They are going to celebrate their reunion on December thirty-first.
items.ipa: il vɔ̃ se.le.bʁe lœʁ ʁə.tʁu.vaj lə tʁɑ̃.t‿e œ̃ de.sɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: The t of trente stays pronounced in this compound number despite et normally blocking liaison.

items.fr: Nous avons marché longtemps entre les étals.
items.en: We walked for a long time between the stalls.
items.ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ maʁ.ʃe lɔ̃.tɑ̃ ɑ̃.tʁə le.z‿e.tal/
items.notes: Longtemps contains two nasal vowels and a silent final s, easy to misspell.

items.fr: Nous préférons le thé.
items.en: We prefer tea.
items.ipa: /nu pʁe.fe.ʁɔ̃ lə te/
items.respell: noo pray-fay-ROHⁿ luh TAY
items.notes: The ending is a syllable of its own, so the é keeps its closed sound and its own accent.

items.fr: L'enseignante craint que certains élèves n'aient pas compris la consigne.
items.en: The teacher fears that some students didn't understand the instructions.
items.ipa: l‿ɑ̃.sɛ.ɲɑ̃t kʁɛ̃ kə sɛʁ.tɛ.z‿e.lɛv nɛ pa kɔ̃.pʁi la kɔ̃.siɲ
items.notes: "consigne" prend un g suivi de n, à ne pas confondre avec "consine".

items.fr: Elle achète du pain.
items.en: She buys bread.
items.ipa: /ɛl a.ʃɛt dy pɛ̃/
items.respell: el ah-SHET dü PAⁿ
items.notes: The silent -e pulls the stress back, and the bare e of the stem opens to è.

items.fr: Nous achetons du pain.
items.en: We buy bread.
items.ipa: /nu.zaʃ.tɔ̃ dy pɛ̃/
items.respell: noo zahsh-TOHⁿ dü PAⁿ
items.notes: The ending sounds, so nothing moves and the e disappears from the sound altogether.

items.fr: Quand il était petit, il oubliait souvent son cartable.
items.en: When he was little, he often forgot his school bag.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ i.l‿e.tɛ pə.ti i.l‿u.bli.jɛ su.vɑ̃ sɔ̃ kaʁ.tabl
items.notes: Imparfait ending "-ait" sounds identical to "-aient" and "-é", a common spelling trap; also a silent final t in "petit".

items.fr: Nous rangeons la cuisine.
items.en: We are tidying the kitchen.
items.ipa: /nu ʁɑ̃.ʒɔ̃ la kɥi.zin/
items.respell: noo rahⁿ-ZHOHⁿ la kwee-ZEEN
items.notes: A third -ger verb taking the same e. The pattern is about the letters, not about the word.

items.fr: lancer
items.en: to throw
items.ipa: /lɑ̃se/
items.respell: lahⁿ-SAY

items.fr: Tu finis tôt.
items.en: You finish early.
items.ipa: /ty fi.ni to/
items.respell: tü fee-nee TOH
items.notes: The -s is silent, exactly as it was on an -er verb. Only tu tells you.

items.fr: Je finis tôt.
items.en: I finish early.
items.ipa: /ʒə fi.ni to/
items.respell: zhuh fee-nee TOH
items.notes: Said exactly like Tu finis tôt and Il finit tôt. Three spellings, one sound.

items.fr: Il finit tôt.
items.en: He finishes early.
items.ipa: /il fi.ni to/
items.respell: eel fee-nee TOH
items.notes: The -t is silent. This is the half of the pair the ear can settle against the plural.

items.fr: Nous finissons tôt.
items.en: We finish early.
items.ipa: /nu fi.ni.sɔ̃ to/
items.respell: noo fee-nee-sohⁿ TOH
items.notes: A whole syllable more than the singular. Out loud most rooms say on finit instead.

items.fr: Vous finissez tôt.
items.en: You finish early.
items.ipa: /vu fi.ni.se to/
items.respell: voo fee-nee-say TOH
items.notes: A whole syllable more as well, and it does not sound like the naming form finir.

items.fr: Ils finissent tôt.
items.en: They finish early.
items.ipa: /il fi.nis to/
items.respell: eel fee-nees TOH
items.notes: One sound more than Il finit tôt, at the very end of the verb, and nothing else.

items.fr: Elle choisit.
items.en: She chooses.
items.ipa: /ɛl ʃwa.zi/
items.respell: el shwah-ZEE
items.notes: One person.

items.fr: Elles choisissent.
items.en: They choose.
items.ipa: /ɛl ʃwa.zis/
items.respell: el shwah-ZEES
items.notes: Several. The s of elles is silent as ever, so the verb is the only evidence there is.

items.fr: Il réussit toujours.
items.en: He always succeeds.
items.ipa: /il ʁe.y.si tu.ʒuʁ/
items.respell: eel ray-ü-see too-ZHOOR

items.fr: Elle grandit vite.
items.en: She is growing up fast.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɡʁɑ̃.di vit/
items.respell: el grahⁿ-dee VEET

items.fr: Elle a remercié son collègue pour son aide précieuse.
items.en: She thanked her colleague for his valuable help.
items.ipa: ɛl a ʁə.mɛʁ.sje sɔ̃ kɔ.lɛg puʁ sɔ̃.n‿ɛd pʁe.sjøz

items.fr: Elles grandissent vite.
items.en: They are growing up fast.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɡʁɑ̃.dis vit/
items.respell: el grahⁿ-dees VEET
items.notes: A third verb, the same one sound, and elles against elle is again the whole difference.

items.fr: Je remplis le formulaire.
items.en: I am filling in the form.
items.ipa: /ʒə ʁɑ̃.pli lə fɔʁ.my.lɛʁ/
items.respell: zhuh rahⁿ-plee luh for-mü-LEHR
items.notes: Ends in -is.

items.fr: Tu remplis le formulaire.
items.en: You are filling in the form.
items.ipa: /ty ʁɑ̃.pli lə fɔʁ.my.lɛʁ/
items.respell: tü rahⁿ-plee luh for-mü-LEHR
items.notes: Also ends in -is, and sounds the same as the je row.

items.fr: Il remplit le formulaire.
items.en: He is filling in the form.
items.ipa: /il ʁɑ̃.pli lə fɔʁ.my.lɛʁ/
items.respell: eel rahⁿ-plee luh for-mü-LEHR
items.notes: Ends in -it, and sounds the same as both of the others.

items.fr: Nous réfléchissons ensemble.
items.en: We are thinking it over together.
items.ipa: /nu ʁe.fle.ʃi.sɔ̃ ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl/
items.respell: noo ray-flay-shee-sohⁿ ahⁿ-SAHⁿBL
items.notes: The nous ending is a syllable of its own, exactly as it was on an -er verb.

items.fr: Elle les y a laissés.
items.en: She left them there.
items.ipa: /ɛl le zi a lɛ.se/
items.respell: ehl lay zee a leh-SAY

items.fr: Je le lui ai rappelé deux fois.
items.en: I reminded him of it twice.
items.ipa: /ʒə lə lɥi e ʁa.pə.le dø fwa/
items.respell: zhuh luh lwee ay ra-puh-LAY deu FWA

items.fr: Ils réussissent toujours.
items.en: They always succeed.
items.ipa: /il ʁe.y.sis tu.ʒuʁ/
items.respell: eel ray-ü-sees too-ZHOOR
items.notes: The same one sound at the end of the verb, on a second verb.

items.fr: Le public applaudit.
items.en: The audience applauds.
items.ipa: /lə py.blik a.plo.di/
items.respell: luh pü-bleek a-ploh-DEE
items.notes: A noun subject, and it is singular, so the verb takes the short form.

items.fr: Les enfants applaudissent.
items.en: The children applaud.
items.ipa: /le zɑ̃.fɑ̃ a.plo.dis/
items.respell: lay zahⁿ-fahⁿ a-ploh-DEES
items.notes: The same verb with a plural subject, and the sound at the end says so.

items.fr: Le bus ralentit ici.
items.en: The bus slows down here.
items.ipa: /lə bys ʁa.lɑ̃.ti i.si/
items.respell: luh büs ra-lahⁿ-tee ee-SEE

items.fr: Les voitures ralentissent ici.
items.en: The cars slow down here.
items.ipa: /le vwa.tyʁ ʁa.lɑ̃.tis i.si/
items.respell: lay vwah-tür ra-lahⁿ-tees ee-SEE
items.notes: Nothing in the sentence is plural to the ear except the verb.

items.fr: Nous remplissons les papiers.
items.en: We are filling in the papers.
items.ipa: /nu ʁɑ̃.pli.sɔ̃ le pa.pje/
items.respell: noo rahⁿ-plee-sohⁿ lay pa-PYAY
items.notes: The same stem as Je remplis le formulaire, with a syllable on the end of it.

items.fr: Je choisis un cours dans la semaine.
items.en: I pick a class during the week.
items.ipa: /ʒə ʃwa.zi œ̃ kuʁ dɑ̃ la sə.mɛn/
items.respell: zhuh shwah-zee uhⁿ koor dahⁿ la suh-MEN
items.notes: The n of semaine is a real n and is said. The two nasal vowels before it are not.

items.fr: Je pars tôt.
items.en: I leave early.
items.ipa: /ʒə paʁ to/
items.respell: zhuh par TOH
items.notes: The t of the stem is gone. Said exactly like Tu pars tôt and Il part tôt.

items.fr: Vous obéissez aux règles.
items.en: You follow the rules.
items.ipa: /vu zɔ.be.i.se o ʁɛɡl/
items.respell: voo zo-bay-ee-say o REHGL
items.notes: The silent s of vous wakes up in front of the vowel, and the ending is still a syllable.

items.fr: Ils guérissent vite.
items.en: They get better quickly.
items.ipa: /il ɡe.ʁis vit/
items.respell: eel gay-rees VEET

items.fr: Ils couvrent tout.
items.en: They cover everything.
items.ipa: /il kuvʁ tu/
items.respell: eel koovr TOO
items.notes: Seven letters at the end and not one of them sounds. Identical to Il couvre tout.

items.fr: Nous couvrons tout.
items.en: We cover everything.
items.ipa: /nu ku.vʁɔ̃ tu/
items.respell: noo koo-vrohⁿ TOO
items.notes: One of the two the ear gets, and it is the -ons of an -er verb.

items.fr: Vous couvrez tout.
items.en: You cover everything.
items.ipa: /vu ku.vʁe tu/
items.respell: voo koo-vray TOO
items.notes: The other one, and it is -ez. Two audible out of six, exactly as in lesson 1 in A2.

items.fr: Il y en avait encore hier.
items.en: There were still some yesterday.
items.ipa: /i ljɑ̃ na.vɛ ɑ̃.kɔʁ jɛʁ/
items.respell: ee-lyahⁿ-na-VEH ahⁿ-kor YEHR

items.fr: Tu me l’as dit à voix basse.
items.en: You said it to me quietly.
items.ipa: /ty mə la di a vwa bas/
items.respell: tü muh la DEE a vwa BASS

items.fr: Je vends ici.
items.en: I sell here.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɑ̃ i.si/
items.respell: zhuh vahⁿ ee-SEE
items.notes: Said exactly like Tu vends ici and Il vend ici. Three spellings, one sound, and the d is silent in all three.

items.fr: Tu vends ici.
items.en: You sell here.
items.ipa: /ty vɑ̃ i.si/
items.respell: tü vahⁿ ee-SEE
items.notes: The same -s tu took on an -er and an -ir verb, and it is silent here too.

items.fr: Il vend ici.
items.en: He sells here.
items.ipa: /il vɑ̃ i.si/
items.respell: eel vahⁿ ee-SEE
items.notes: THE BARE FORM. Nothing is written after the stem, and nothing is missing.

items.fr: Nous perdons du temps.
items.en: We are wasting time.
items.ipa: /nu pɛʁ.dɔ̃ dy tɑ̃/
items.respell: noo pehr-dohⁿ dü TAHⁿ

items.fr: Il descend ici.
items.en: He gets off here.
items.ipa: /il de.sɑ̃ i.si/
items.respell: eel day-sahⁿ ee-SEE
items.notes: The longest naming form in the set and the shortest third person: descendre gives descend and stops.

items.fr: Ils descendent ici.
items.en: They get off here.
items.ipa: /il de.sɑ̃d i.si/
items.respell: eel day-sahⁿd ee-SEE
items.notes: ils is said exactly like il, so the d is carrying the whole sentence.

items.fr: Vous répondez vite.
items.en: You answer quickly.
items.ipa: /vu ʁe.pɔ̃.de vit/
items.respell: voo ray-pohⁿ-day VEET

items.fr: On vend des billets ici.
items.en: We sell tickets here.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ vɑ̃ de bi.jɛ i.si/
items.respell: ohⁿ vahⁿ day bee-YEH ee-SEE
items.notes: on means we and takes the il form, so the spoken we takes the bare form as well.

items.fr: Nous vendons des billets.
items.en: We sell tickets.
items.ipa: /nu vɑ̃.dɔ̃ de bi.jɛ/
items.respell: noo vahⁿ-dohⁿ day bee-YEH
items.notes: The written we, saying the same thing as the row above it.

items.fr: descendre
items.en: to get off
items.ipa: /de.sɑ̃dʁ/
items.respell: day-SAHⁿDR

items.fr: attendre
items.en: to wait for
items.ipa: /atɑ̃dʁ/
items.respell: ah-TAHⁿDR
items.notes: regular -re verb · j'attends, nous attendons

items.fr: rendre
items.en: to give back
items.ipa: /ʁɑ̃dʁ/
items.respell: RAHⁿDR
items.notes: regular re verb · je rends, nous rendons

items.fr: Nous avons attendu longtemps, mais le train n'est jamais arrivé.
items.en: We waited a long time, but the train never arrived.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ a.tɑ̃.dy lɔ̃.tɑ̃ mɛ lə tʁɛ̃ n‿ɛ ʒa.mɛ a.ʁi.ve
items.notes: Do not lose the "ne" in front of "est jamais", which is easy to drop when speaking. There is a link in "train n'est".

items.fr: Je vais au parc.
items.en: I go to the park.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ o paʁk/
items.respell: zhuh veh oh PARK
items.notes: vais, and there is no all- in it anywhere. This is the form to stop looking for a reason for.

items.fr: Tu vas au parc.
items.en: You go to the park.
items.ipa: /ty va o paʁk/
items.respell: tü vah oh PARK
items.notes: vas, said exactly like Il va au parc. The pronoun is the only difference out loud.

items.fr: Il revient tôt.
items.en: He comes back early.
items.ipa: /il ʁə.vjɛ̃ to/
items.respell: eel ruh-vyaⁿ TOH
items.notes: Il vient tôt with re- on the front, and nothing else about it moved.

items.fr: Ils sont joyeux.
items.en: They are cheerful.
items.ipa: /il sɔ̃ ʒwa.jø/
items.respell: eel sohⁿ zhwah-YUH
items.notes: Plural, and still no s anywhere. Every word in this family behaves this way.

items.fr: Elle est impulsive.
items.en: She is impulsive.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ ɛ̃.pyl.siv/
items.respell: el eh aⁿ-pewl-SEEV
items.notes: A second -if adjective, and the f has done the same thing again.

items.fr: Ils sont impulsifs.
items.en: They are impulsive.
items.ipa: /il sɔ̃ ɛ̃.pyl.sif/
items.respell: eel sohⁿ aⁿ-pewl-SEEF
items.notes: The f is back, because this is the masculine again, and the s is silent.

items.fr: faire une promenade
items.en: to go for a walk
items.ipa: /fɛʁ yn pʁɔmnad/
items.respell: fair ün prom-NAHD

items.fr: sérieuse
items.en: serious (feminine)
items.ipa: /se.ʁjøz/
items.respell: say-RYUHZ
items.notes: The x has become se. Say it and you will hear the buzz on the end.

items.fr: Elle est curieuse.
items.en: She is curious.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ ky.ʁjøz/
items.respell: el eh kü-RYUHZ
items.notes: Second adjective, same move. curieux loses its x and gains se.

items.fr: Elles sont curieuses.
items.en: They are curious.
items.ipa: /ɛl sɔ̃ ky.ʁjøz/
items.respell: el sohⁿ kü-RYUHZ
items.notes: And the plural s goes on the end of the feminine, exactly as it did with sérieuses.

items.fr: Elle est généreuse.
items.en: She is generous.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ ʒe.ne.ʁøz/
items.respell: el eh zhay-nay-RUHZ
items.notes: Third adjective, third time the same two letters do the same job.

items.fr: On s’en est bien sorti.
items.en: We came out of it all right.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ sɑ̃ nɛ bjɛ̃ sɔʁ.ti/
items.respell: ohⁿ sahⁿ neh byehⁿ sor-TEE

items.fr: Je vous y attends à dix heures.
items.en: I will be waiting for you there at ten.
items.ipa: /ʒə vu zi a.tɑ̃ a di.zœʁ/
items.respell: zhuh voo zee a-TAHⁿ a dee-ZUHR

items.fr: Après nous, vous, les et en, la liaison se fait.
items.en: After nous, vous, les and en, the liaison is made.
items.ipa: /a.pʁɛ nu vu le e ɑ̃ la ljɛ.zɔ̃ sə fɛ/
items.respell: a-PREH noo VOO lay ay AHⁿ la lyeh-zohⁿ suh FEH
items.notes: Un z : le s de nous se prononce et passe sur la syllabe suivante.
items.prompt: Qu’entend-on entre nous et y dans « elle nous y emmène » ?

items.fr: Je te le promets.
items.en: I promise you.
items.ipa: /ʒə tə lə pʁɔ.mɛ/
items.respell: zhuh tuh luh pro-MEH

items.fr: Il me l'a confirmé ce matin.
items.en: He confirmed it to me this morning.
items.ipa: /il mə la kɔ̃.fiʁ.me sə ma.tɛ̃/
items.respell: eel muh la kohⁿ-feer-MAY suh ma-TEHⁿ

items.fr: Passe-la-moi, je m’en occupe.
items.en: Pass it to me, I will take care of it.
items.ipa: /pas la mwa ʒə mɑ̃ nɔ.kyp/
items.respell: pass-la-MWA zhuh mahⁿ no-KÜP

items.fr: Ne le lui répète pas.
items.en: Do not repeat it to him.
items.ipa: /nə lə lɥi ʁe.pɛt pa/
items.respell: nuh luh lwee ray-PEHT pa

items.fr: Nous allons les leur rendre lundi.
items.en: We are going to give them back to them on Monday.
items.ipa: /nu za.lɔ̃ le lœʁ ʁɑ̃dʁ lœ̃.di/
items.respell: noo za-LOHⁿ lay luhr RAHⁿDR luhⁿ-DEE

items.fr: Elle nous en a apporté trois.
items.en: She brought us three of them.
items.ipa: /ɛl nu zɑ̃ na a.pɔʁ.te tʁwa/
items.respell: ehl noo zahⁿ na a-por-TAY TRWA

items.fr: Tu la leur montreras demain.
items.en: You will show it to them tomorrow.
items.ipa: /ty la lœʁ mɔ̃.tʁə.ʁa də.mɛ̃/
items.respell: tü la luhr mohⁿ-truh-RA duh-MEHⁿ

items.fr: Dis-le-lui ce soir.
items.en: Tell him this evening.
items.ipa: /di lə lɥi sə swaʁ/
items.respell: dee-luh-LWEE suh SWAR

items.fr: On me l'a demandé deux fois.
items.en: I have been asked for it twice.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ mə la də.mɑ̃.de dø fwa/
items.respell: ohⁿ muh la duh-mahⁿ-DAY deu FWA

items.fr: Je ne vous en veux pas.
items.en: I am not holding it against you.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə vu zɑ̃ vø pa/
items.respell: zhuh nuh voo zahⁿ VEU pa

items.fr: Je viens tôt.
items.en: I come early.
items.ipa: /ʒə vjɛ̃ to/
items.respell: zhuh vyaⁿ TOH
items.notes: The vowel is in the nose and no n is said. Identical to Tu viens tôt and Il vient tôt.

items.fr: Tu viens tôt.
items.en: You come early.
items.ipa: /ty vjɛ̃ to/
items.respell: tü vyaⁿ TOH
items.notes: Spelled the same as the je form and said the same way too.

items.fr: Il vient tôt.
items.en: He comes early.
items.ipa: /il vjɛ̃ to/
items.respell: eel vyaⁿ TOH
items.notes: Put this beside Il finit tôt and Il part tôt. All three stop dead, and for three different reasons.

items.fr: Il va au parc.
items.en: He goes to the park.
items.ipa: /il va o paʁk/
items.respell: eel vah oh PARK
items.notes: va, and it is the shortest verb form in the language. Two letters and a whole sentence stands on it.

items.fr: Nous allons au parc.
items.en: We go to the park.
items.ipa: /nu za.lɔ̃ o paʁk/
items.respell: noo za-lohⁿ oh PARK
items.notes: Here the all- appears, and the silent s of nous wakes up as a z in front of the vowel.

items.fr: Vous allez au parc.
items.en: You go to the park.
items.ipa: /vu za.le o paʁk/
items.respell: voo za-lay oh PARK
items.notes: The same all-, the same z. These two are the only cells that look like the naming form.

items.fr: Ils vont au parc.
items.en: They go to the park.
items.ipa: /il vɔ̃ o paʁk/
items.respell: eel vohⁿ oh PARK
items.notes: vont, and the all- is gone again. Four cells from v-, two from all-, and no rule joins them.

items.fr: Nous venons tôt.
items.en: We come early.
items.ipa: /nu və.nɔ̃ to/
items.respell: noo vuh-nohⁿ TOH
items.notes: ven- comes back and nothing is inserted between it and the ending. Out loud most rooms say on vient instead.

items.fr: Vous venez tôt.
items.en: You come early.
items.ipa: /vu və.ne to/
items.respell: voo vuh-nay TOH
items.notes: The same ven-, the same two endings you have had since lesson 1 in A2.

items.fr: Ils viennent tôt.
items.en: They come early.
items.ipa: /il vjɛn to/
items.respell: eel vyenn TOH
items.notes: An n arrives at the end of the verb and the vowel comes out of the nose. That is the one plural in this lesson you can hear.

items.fr: Je tiens la clé.
items.en: I am holding the key.
items.ipa: /ʒə tjɛ̃ la kle/
items.respell: zhuh tyaⁿ lah KLAY
items.notes: Change the v of viens to a t and you have it. Every cell of tenir is venir with that one letter swapped.

items.fr: Tu tiens la clé.
items.en: You are holding the key.
items.ipa: /ty tjɛ̃ la kle/
items.respell: tü tyaⁿ lah KLAY
items.notes: This form appears nowhere in the corpus. It is here because the pattern says it must exist, which is what a pattern is for.

items.fr: Il tient la clé.
items.en: He is holding the key.
items.ipa: /il tjɛ̃ la kle/
items.respell: eel tyaⁿ lah KLAY
items.notes: The third of three spellings that are one sound, exactly as on venir.

items.fr: Nous tenons la clé.
items.en: We are holding the key.
items.ipa: /nu tə.nɔ̃ la kle/
items.respell: noo tuh-nohⁿ lah KLAY
items.notes: ten- against ven-, and everything after it is the same.

items.fr: Vous tenez la clé.
items.en: You are holding the key.
items.ipa: /vu tə.ne la kle/
items.respell: voo tuh-nay lah KLAY
items.notes: Also absent from the corpus, and also exactly where the pattern puts it.

items.fr: Ils tiennent la clé.
items.en: They are holding the key.
items.ipa: /il tjɛn la kle/
items.respell: eel tyenn lah KLAY
items.notes: The n arrives and the vowel leaves the nose, the same as on viennent. Two verbs, one machine.

items.fr: Je viens de manger.
items.en: I have just eaten.
items.ipa: /ʒə vjɛ̃ də mɑ̃.ʒe/
items.respell: zhuh vyaⁿ duh mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: The first four words are the same as Je viens de Paris. What comes next is the whole difference.

items.fr: Tu viens de rentrer.
items.en: You have just got home.
items.ipa: /ty vjɛ̃ də ʁɑ̃.tʁe/
items.respell: tü vyaⁿ duh rahⁿ-TRAY
items.notes: The verb after de never changes for the person. Only viens does.

items.fr: Il vient de partir.
items.en: He has just left.
items.ipa: /il vjɛ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ/
items.respell: eel vyaⁿ duh par-TEER
items.notes: The most useful sentence in the lesson. It is what you say when somebody asks for a person who has gone.

items.fr: Rends-les-moi quand tu peux.
items.en: Give them back to me when you can.
items.ipa: /ʁɑ̃ le mwa kɑ̃ ty pø/
items.respell: rahⁿ-lay-MWA kahⁿ tü PEU

items.fr: Elle leur en a gardé une part.
items.en: She kept a slice of it for them.
items.ipa: /ɛl lœ.ʁɑ̃ na ɡaʁ.de yn paʁ/
items.respell: ehl luh-rahⁿ na gar-DAY ünn PAR

items.fr: Une seule file, cinq places, et elle ne quitte pas son verbe.
items.en: One queue, five places, and it never leaves its verb.
items.ipa: /yn sœl fil sɛ̃k plas e ɛl nə kit pa sɔ̃ vɛʁb/
items.respell: ünn suhl FEEL sehⁿk PLASS ay ehl nuh keet pa sohⁿ VEHRB
items.notes: Une file, cinq places, collée au verbe, et l’ordre affirmatif la fait passer derrière.
items.prompt: Résume toute la leçon en une phrase.

items.fr: Je vais le leur envoyer ce soir.
items.en: I am going to send it to them this evening.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ lə lœ.ʁɑ̃.vwa.je sə swaʁ/
items.respell: zhuh veh luh luh-rahⁿ-vwa-YAY suh SWAR

items.fr: Ne m’en parle plus.
items.en: Do not talk to me about it any more.
items.ipa: /nə mɑ̃ paʁl ply/
items.respell: nuh mahⁿ PARL PLÜ

items.fr: On vous les remettra à l’accueil.
items.en: They will be handed to you at reception.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ vu le ʁə.mɛ.tʁa a la.kœj/
items.respell: ohⁿ voo lay ruh-meh-TRA a la-KUHY

items.fr: La salle a été réservée par le directeur.
items.en: The room was booked by the director.
items.ipa: /la sal a e.te ʁe.zɛʁ.ve paʁ lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ/
items.respell: la SAL a ay-tay ray-zehr-VAY par luh dee-rehk-TUHR

items.fr: On a réservé la salle.
items.en: Someone booked the room.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃.na ʁe.zɛʁ.ve la sal/
items.respell: ohⁿ-na ray-zehr-VAY la SAL

items.fr: faire une erreur
items.en: to make a mistake
items.ipa: /fɛʁ yn ɛ.ʁœʁ/
items.respell: FEHR ün eh-RUHR
items.notes: The one expression here an English speaker guesses right, and it is worth having for that reason.

items.fr: faire de la musique
items.en: to play music
items.ipa: /fɛʁ də la my.zik/
items.respell: FEHR duh lah mü-ZEEK
items.notes: English plays music and plays sport; French does both with faire and a small word in front of the noun.

items.fr: faire un voyage
items.en: to take a trip
items.ipa: /fɛʁ œ̃ vwa.jaʒ/
items.respell: FEHR uhⁿ vwah-YAHZH
items.notes: Take a trip, and there is no French verb for take here at all.

items.fr: faire les valises
items.en: to pack the bags
items.ipa: /fɛʁ le va.liz/
items.respell: FEHR lay vah-LEEZ
items.notes: English has a whole verb, to pack. French spends the word for suitcases instead.

items.fr: faire semblant
items.en: to pretend
items.ipa: /fɛʁ sɑ̃.blɑ̃/
items.respell: FEHR sahⁿ-BLAHⁿ
items.notes: Two nasal vowels in one word and no n said in either. The noun semblant is used for nothing else at all.

items.fr: faire plaisir
items.en: to please someone
items.ipa: /fɛʁ ple.ziʁ/
items.respell: FEHR pleh-ZEER
items.notes: Ça me fait plaisir is what somebody says when they are glad you came. There is no verb in it anywhere.

items.fr: commander
items.en: to order
items.ipa: /kɔ.mɑ̃.de/
items.respell: koh-mahⁿ-DAY

items.fr: Elle veut devenir médecin.
items.en: She wants to become a doctor.
items.ipa: /ɛl vø dəvniʁ medsɛ̃/
items.respell: ell vuh duhv-NEER med-SAⁿ
items.notes: Conjugates like venir: je deviens, nous devenons.

items.fr: Nous devons partir avant midi.
items.en: We must leave before noon.
items.ipa: /nu dəvɔ̃ paʁtiʁ avɑ̃ midi/
items.respell: noo duh-VOHⁿ par-TEER ah-VAHⁿ mee-DEE

items.fr: Nous devons payer.
items.en: We have to pay.
items.ipa: /nu də.vɔ̃ pe.je/
items.respell: noo duh-VOHⁿ pay-YAY
items.notes: The stem is dev-, and the ending is the one you have had since lesson 1 in A2.

items.fr: Je veux un café, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: I want a coffee, please.
items.ipa: ʒə vø.n‿œ̃ ka.fe, sil vu plɛ
items.respell: zhuh VUH uⁿ kah-FAY seel voo PLEH
items.notes: “veux” ends in x, not the s one might expect.

items.fr: J'ai offert des fleurs.
items.en: I gave flowers.
items.ipa: /ʒe ɔ.fɛʁ de flœʁ/
items.respell: ZHAY oh-FEHR day FLEUR
items.notes: Eighteen letters, so WORD mode. The same three letters on a verb that has nothing to do with opening.

items.fr: J'ai fait le ménage.
items.en: I did the housework.
items.ipa: /ʒe fɛ lə me.naʒ/
items.respell: ZHAY FEH luh may-NAZH
items.notes: Fifteen letters. The commonest verb in the whole set and it is in no group at all.

items.fr: Il est venu hier.
items.en: He came yesterday.
items.ipa: /il ɛ və.ny jɛʁ/
items.respell: eel eh vuh-NÜ YEHR
items.notes: The form is an ordinary member of the -u group. The first word is lesson 18's and this row carries no dictation drill for that reason.

items.fr: J'ai eu froid.
items.en: I was cold.
items.ipa: /ʒe y fʁwa/
items.respell: ZHAY Ü FRWA
items.notes: The second eu row, so the ear question has three options that differ by the consonant in front of one pure vowel rather than by the vowel itself.

items.fr: J'ai bu du thé.
items.en: I drank some tea.
items.ipa: /ʒe by dy te/
items.respell: ZHAY BÜ dü TAY
items.notes: THE OTHER HALF OF THE CIRCUMFLEX PAIR. « du » here is the word meaning "some" and it is the same sound as « dû ». Ten letters, so the dictée takes it, and the dictée cannot tell the two apart either.

items.fr: Et samedi, alors ?
items.en: And on Saturday, then?
items.ipa: /e sam.di a.lɔʁ/
items.respell: ay sam-DEE ah-LOR
items.notes: Her question, and it holds no verb he can copy a form out of.

items.fr: Samedi, j'ai pris le bus.
items.en: On Saturday I took the bus.
items.ipa: /sam.di ʒe pʁi lə bys/
items.respell: sam-DEE · ZHAY PREE luh BÜSS
items.notes: What he meant, in full, and it is the frame row with a day on the front.

items.fr: Pardon ? Tu as fait quoi ?
items.en: Sorry? You did what?
items.ipa: /paʁ.dɔ̃ ty a fɛ kwa/
items.respell: par-DOHⁿ · tü a FEH KWA
items.notes: What she says instead, and it is the point of the scene: she has not been offended and she has not corrected anything. She simply did not receive a word.

items.fr: Et toi, tu as fait quoi samedi ?
items.en: And you, what did you do on Saturday?
items.ipa: /e twa ty a fɛ kwa sam.di/
items.respell: ay TWAH · tü a FEH KWA sam-DEE
items.notes: The same colleague, later in the week, with more time. No inversion, which is how it is asked.

items.fr: J'ai vu un film.
items.en: I saw a film.
items.ipa: /ʒe vy ɛ̃ film/
items.respell: ZHAY VÜ uhⁿ FEELM
items.notes: The -u group in the first answer of the conversation.

items.fr: Tu as lu le journal ?
items.en: Did you read the paper?
items.ipa: /ty a ly lə ʒuʁ.nal/
items.respell: tü a LÜ luh zhoor-NAL
items.notes: A question in the past with no inversion, on a two-letter past form.

items.fr: Il faut que je boive quelque chose de chaud.
items.en: I need to drink something hot.
items.ipa: /il fo kə ʒə bwav kɛl.kə ʃoz də ʃo/
items.respell: eel foh kuh zhuh BWAHV kehl-kuh shohz duh SHOH

items.fr: Ils peuvent payer.
items.en: They can pay.
items.ipa: /il pœv pe.je/
items.respell: eel PUHV pay-YAY
items.notes: peu plus the v from pouv-. Same recipe as veulent, and you can now guess the third one.

items.fr: Je dois payer.
items.en: I have to pay.
items.ipa: /ʒə dwa pe.je/
items.respell: zhuh DWAH pay-YAY
items.notes: A plain -s here, not the -x. This is the singular you already met on the -RE verbs in lesson 4 in A2.

items.fr: Tu dois payer.
items.en: You have to pay.
items.ipa: /ty dwa pe.je/
items.respell: tü DWAH pay-YAY
items.notes: The same again. Every one of these three verbs hands you two spellings across three persons, and one sound.

items.fr: Il doit payer.
items.en: He has to pay.
items.ipa: /il dwa pe.je/
items.respell: eel DWAH pay-YAY
items.notes: The -t you have seen twice already in this lesson.

items.fr: Je veux payer.
items.en: I want to pay.
items.ipa: /ʒə vø pe.je/
items.respell: zhuh VUH pay-YAY
items.notes: The -x is the one new ending in this lesson. It sounds like nothing at all, exactly as the -s did.

items.fr: Tu veux payer.
items.en: You want to pay.
items.ipa: /ty vø pe.je/
items.respell: tü VUH pay-YAY
items.notes: The same spelling as the je form and the same sound. Only the pronoun separates them.

items.fr: Il veut payer.
items.en: He wants to pay.
items.ipa: /il vø pe.je/
items.respell: eel VUH pay-YAY
items.notes: A -t instead of a -x, and still the same sound. Two spellings, three persons, one thing to say.

items.fr: Nous voulons payer.
items.en: We want to pay.
items.ipa: /nu vu.lɔ̃ pe.je/
items.respell: noo voo-LOHⁿ pay-YAY
items.notes: The stem changes to voul- and the ending is the ordinary -ons from lesson 1 in A2.

items.fr: Vous voulez payer.
items.en: You want to pay.
items.ipa: /vu vu.le pe.je/
items.respell: voo voo-LAY pay-YAY
items.notes: Same stem as nous, and the ordinary -ez. Nothing here is irregular except the stem itself.

items.fr: Ils veulent payer.
items.en: They want to pay.
items.ipa: /il vœl pe.je/
items.respell: eel VUHL pay-YAY
items.notes: Take the je stem, add the consonant from the nous stem: veu plus l. The -ent is silent as always.

items.fr: Je peux payer.
items.en: I can pay.
items.ipa: /ʒə pø pe.je/
items.respell: zhuh PUH pay-YAY
items.notes: The same -x ending as veux, on the same kind of stem. Two verbs, one new letter between them.

items.fr: Tu peux payer.
items.en: You can pay.
items.ipa: /ty pø pe.je/
items.respell: tü PUH pay-YAY
items.notes: Identical to the je form on paper and in the mouth.

items.fr: Il peut payer.
items.en: He can pay.
items.ipa: /il pø pe.je/
items.respell: eel PUH pay-YAY
items.notes: A -t, and the same sound again. The pattern is the pattern veux had.

items.fr: Nous pouvons payer.
items.en: We can pay.
items.ipa: /nu pu.vɔ̃ pe.je/
items.respell: noo poo-VOHⁿ pay-YAY
items.notes: The stem goes to pouv-, exactly as vouloir went to voul-.

items.fr: Je peux arroser le jardin.
items.en: I can water the garden.
items.ipa: /ʒə pø a.ʁo.ze lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃/
items.respell: zhuh PUH ah-roh-ZAY luh zhar-DAⁿ
items.notes: Nobody taught you arroser. You did not need to be taught it, and that is the lesson.

items.fr: Tu dois arroser le jardin.
items.en: You have to water the garden.
items.ipa: /ty dwa a.ʁo.ze lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃/
items.respell: tü DWAH ah-roh-ZAY luh zhar-DAⁿ
items.notes: The same unknown verb behind a different modal. Change the front of the sentence and the back holds still.

items.fr: Je sais nager.
items.en: I know how to swim.
items.ipa: /ʒə sɛ na.ʒe/
items.respell: zhuh SEH nah-ZHAY
items.notes: A verb follows, so the sentence keeps going and savoir is the only verb that can carry it.

items.fr: Tu sais nager.
items.en: You know how to swim.
items.ipa: /ty sɛ na.ʒe/
items.respell: tü SEH nah-ZHAY
items.notes: The same spelling as the je form and the same sound. Only the word in front separates them.

items.fr: Il sait nager.
items.en: He knows how to swim.
items.ipa: /il sɛ na.ʒe/
items.respell: eel SEH nah-ZHAY
items.notes: A -t instead of the -s, and not one sound different. Lesson 7 in A2 met the same shape on three verbs at once.

items.fr: Nous savons nager.
items.en: We know how to swim.
items.ipa: /nu sa.vɔ̃ na.ʒe/
items.respell: noo sa-VOHⁿ nah-ZHAY
items.notes: The stem goes to sav- and the ending is the ordinary -ons you have had since lesson 1 in A2.

items.fr: Vous savez nager.
items.en: You know how to swim.
items.ipa: /vu sa.ve na.ʒe/
items.respell: voo sa-VAY nah-ZHAY
items.notes: Same stem as nous, and the ordinary -ez. Nothing about this form is irregular.

items.fr: Ils savent nager.
items.en: They know how to swim.
items.ipa: /il sav na.ʒe/
items.respell: eel SAV nah-ZHAY
items.notes: The -ent is silent, so what you hear is the v arriving at the end of the verb.

items.fr: Je connais Paris.
items.en: I know Paris.
items.ipa: /ʒə kɔ.nɛ pa.ʁi/
items.respell: zhuh koh-NEH pa-REE
items.notes: A name follows and the sentence stops there. That is the whole test.

items.fr: Tu connais Paris.
items.en: You know Paris.
items.ipa: /ty kɔ.nɛ pa.ʁi/
items.respell: tü koh-NEH pa-REE
items.notes: Identical to the je form on paper and in the mouth, exactly as sais and sais are.

items.fr: Il connaît Paris.
items.en: He knows Paris.
items.ipa: /il kɔ.nɛ pa.ʁi/
items.respell: eel koh-NEH pa-REE
items.notes: The circumflex arrives with the -t and changes nothing you say. It is the only place it appears in the paradigm.

items.fr: Nous connaissons Paris.
items.en: We know Paris.
items.ipa: /nu kɔ.nɛ.sɔ̃ pa.ʁi/
items.respell: noo koh-neh-SOHⁿ pa-REE
items.notes: A double s arrives in the plural and stays for all three. The circumflex does not.

items.fr: Vous connaissez Paris.
items.en: You know Paris.
items.ipa: /vu kɔ.nɛ.se pa.ʁi/
items.respell: voo koh-neh-SAY pa-REE
items.notes: This is the form you will be asked in. Somebody wanting to know whether you have been somewhere says it to you.

items.fr: Ils connaissent Paris.
items.en: They know Paris.
items.ipa: /il kɔ.nɛs pa.ʁi/
items.respell: eel koh-NEHS pa-REE
items.notes: The -ent is silent and the double s is what you hear. Nothing here is nasal.

items.fr: Je sais où elle habite.
items.en: I know where she lives.
items.ipa: /ʒə sɛ u ɛl a.bit/
items.respell: zhuh SEH oo ell ah-BEET
items.notes: A place, and it takes savoir. What follows is a whole sentence, and that is what decides it.

items.fr: battre
items.en: to beat
items.ipa: /batʁ/
items.respell: BATR
items.notes: irregular · je bats, nous battons, ils battent

items.fr: Tu connais Marie ?
items.en: Do you know Marie?
items.ipa: /ty kɔ.nɛ ma.ʁi/
items.respell: tü koh-NEH ma-REE
items.notes: A person, so it is connaître. This is the question the scene at the start got wrong.

items.fr: Je connais ce quartier.
items.en: I know this neighbourhood.
items.ipa: /ʒə kɔ.nɛ sə kaʁ.tje/
items.respell: zhuh koh-NEH suh kar-TYAY
items.notes: A place you have walked around in. The sentence lands on it and finishes.

items.fr: Nous connaissons ce restaurant.
items.en: We know this restaurant.
items.ipa: /nu kɔ.nɛ.sɔ̃ sə ʁɛs.tɔ.ʁɑ̃/
items.respell: noo koh-neh-SOHⁿ suh rehs-toh-RAHⁿ
items.notes: We have eaten there. Knowing a fact about it would be the other verb.

items.fr: Tu peux me donner le dossier ?
items.en: Can you give me the file?
items.ipa: /ty pø mə dɔ.ne lə dɔ.sje/
items.respell: tü puh muh doh-nay luh doh-SYAY

items.fr: Tu prends la clé.
items.en: You take the key.
items.ipa: /ty pʁɑ̃ la kle/
items.respell: tü PRAHⁿ la KLAY
items.notes: The same spelling as the je form and the same sound. Only the word in front separates them.

items.fr: Il prend la clé.
items.en: He takes the key.
items.ipa: /il pʁɑ̃ la kle/
items.respell: eel PRAHⁿ la KLAY
items.notes: One letter shorter on the page and not one sound different in the mouth.

items.fr: apprendre
items.en: to learn
items.ipa: a.pʁɑ̃dʁ
items.respell: a-PRAHⁿDR

example.en: I've been learning French for a year.
example.fr: J'apprends le français depuis un an.

items.fr: combattre
items.en: to fight
items.ipa: /kɔ̃batʁ/
items.respell: kohⁿ-BATR
items.notes: irregular · takes every ending battre takes

items.fr: remettre
items.en: to put back, to hand in
items.ipa: /ʁəmɛtʁ/
items.respell: ruh-MEHTR
items.notes: irregular · takes every ending mettre takes

items.fr: Je prends la clé.
items.en: I take the key.
items.ipa: /ʒə pʁɑ̃ la kle/
items.respell: zhuh PRAHⁿ la KLAY
items.notes: The d is written and not said. What you hear at the end of the verb is the nasal vowel.

items.fr: Elle demande comment tu vas.
items.en: She is asking how you are.
items.ipa: /ɛl də.mɑ̃d kɔ.mɑ̃ ty va/
items.respell: ehl duh-MAHⁿD ko-mahⁿ tü VA

items.fr: Nous prenons la clé.
items.en: We take the key.
items.ipa: /nu pʁə.nɔ̃ la kle/
items.respell: noo pruh-NOHⁿ la KLAY
items.notes: The d goes, and there is ONE n. The ending is the ordinary -ons you have had since lesson 1 in A2.

items.fr: Vous prenez la clé.
items.en: You take the key.
items.ipa: /vu pʁə.ne la kle/
items.respell: voo pruh-NAY la KLAY
items.notes: Same stem as nous, one n again, and the ordinary -ez. Nothing here is irregular.

items.fr: Ils prennent la clé.
items.en: They take the key.
items.ipa: /il pʁɛn la kle/
items.respell: eel PREN la KLAY
items.notes: TWO n, and the -ent makes no sound. The second n is there so that something is left to hear.

items.fr: Je mets la clé.
items.en: I put the key down.
items.ipa: /ʒə mɛ la kle/
items.respell: zhuh MEH la KLAY
items.notes: One t, and the s is silent. Two letters shorter than the infinitive and a completely ordinary sound.

items.fr: Tu mets la clé.
items.en: You put the key down.
items.ipa: /ty mɛ la kle/
items.respell: tü MEH la KLAY
items.notes: Identical to the je form on the page and in the mouth, exactly as the prendre pair is.

items.fr: Il met la clé.
items.en: He puts the key down.
items.ipa: /il mɛ la kle/
items.respell: eel MEH la KLAY
items.notes: The s goes and nothing else does. Three persons, two spellings, one sound.

items.fr: Nous mettons la clé.
items.en: We put the key down.
items.ipa: /nu mɛ.tɔ̃ la kle/
items.respell: noo meh-TOHⁿ la KLAY
items.notes: The second t arrives here and it stays for all three plural forms. That is the whole of mettre.

items.fr: Vous mettez la clé.
items.en: You put the key down.
items.ipa: /vu mɛ.te la kle/
items.respell: voo meh-TAY la KLAY
items.notes: Two t again. Where prendre changed its stem between nous and ils, mettre does not.

items.fr: Ce sera prêt vendredi.
items.en: It will be ready on Friday.
items.ipa: /sə sə.ʁa pʁɛ vɑ̃.dʁə.di/
items.respell: suh suh-ra preh vahⁿ-druh-DEE

items.fr: Ils mettent la clé.
items.en: They put the key down.
items.ipa: /il mɛt la kle/
items.respell: eel MET la KLAY
items.notes: The -ent is silent, so the t you have been writing since nous is the thing you now hear.

items.fr: Oui, j'apprends le français ici.
items.en: Yes, I am learning French here.
items.ipa: /wi ʒa.pʁɑ̃ lə fʁɑ̃.sɛ i.si/
items.respell: wee, zha-PRAHⁿ luh frahⁿ-SEH ee-SEE
items.notes: The answer, and it is the question with one letter changed at the front of the verb.

items.fr: crème
items.en: cream
items.ipa: kʁɛm
items.respell: KREM
items.notes: Invariable as a color. Des rideaux crème, cream curtains.

items.fr: nombreux
items.en: numerous, many
items.ipa: nɔ̃bʁø
items.respell: nohⁿ-BRUH
items.notes: Feminine: nombreuse. De nombreux amis, many friends.

items.fr: impulsif
items.en: impulsive
items.ipa: ɛ̃pylsif
items.respell: aⁿ-pewl-SEEF
items.notes: Feminine: impulsive.

items.fr: sportive
items.en: sporty (feminine)
items.ipa: /spɔʁ.tiv/
items.respell: spor-TEEV
items.notes: The f has become a v, which is the only thing that ever happens to this family.

items.fr: Il est grand.
items.en: He is tall.
items.ipa: /il ɛ ɡʁɑ̃/
items.respell: eel eh GRAHⁿ
items.notes: The form you start from. Nothing has been added to it yet.

items.fr: Elle est grande.
items.en: She is tall.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ ɡʁɑ̃d/
items.respell: el eh GRAHⁿD
items.notes: An e arrives and the d wakes up. This is the one you can hear.

items.fr: Ils sont grands.
items.en: They are tall.
items.ipa: /il sɔ̃ ɡʁɑ̃/
items.respell: eel sohⁿ GRAHⁿ
items.notes: An s arrives and nothing at all happens to the sound.

items.fr: Elles sont grandes.
items.en: They are tall.
items.ipa: /ɛl sɔ̃ ɡʁɑ̃d/
items.respell: el sohⁿ GRAHⁿD
items.notes: Both endings at once, and it sounds exactly like the feminine singular.

items.fr: Il est sérieux.
items.en: He is serious.
items.ipa: /il ɛ se.ʁjø/
items.respell: eel eh say-RYUH
items.notes: Ends in x. Remember that, because it decides two of the next three.

items.fr: Elle est sérieuse.
items.en: She is serious.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ se.ʁjøz/
items.respell: el eh say-RYUHZ
items.notes: The x becomes se, and the ending gains a buzz you can hear across a room.

items.fr: Ils sont sérieux.
items.en: They are serious.
items.ipa: /il sɔ̃ se.ʁjø/
items.respell: eel sohⁿ say-RYUH
items.notes: The same word as the singular. There is no room after an x for anything else.

items.fr: Elles sont sérieuses.
items.en: They are serious.
items.ipa: /ɛl sɔ̃ se.ʁjøz/
items.respell: el sohⁿ say-RYUHZ
items.notes: Once the feminine has arrived the plural s goes on the end of it as usual.

items.fr: Il est sportif.
items.en: He is sporty.
items.ipa: /il ɛ spɔʁ.tif/
items.respell: eel eh spor-TEEF
items.notes: Ends in f, and the f is said. Both of those matter in the next cell.

items.fr: Elle est sportive.
items.en: She is sporty.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ spɔʁ.tiv/
items.respell: el eh spor-TEEV
items.notes: The f turns into a v. Nothing else in the word moves.

items.fr: Ils sont sportifs.
items.en: They are sporty.
items.ipa: /il sɔ̃ spɔʁ.tif/
items.respell: eel sohⁿ spor-TEEF
items.notes: An ordinary s, and it is silent like every other plural s.

items.fr: Elles sont sportives.
items.en: They are sporty.
items.ipa: /ɛl sɔ̃ spɔʁ.tiv/
items.respell: el sohⁿ spor-TEEV
items.notes: The v from the feminine, then the s. They stack in that order every time.

items.fr: Il est marron.
items.en: It is brown.
items.ipa: /il ɛ ma.ʁɔ̃/
items.respell: eel eh mah-ROHⁿ
items.notes: A bag, a coat, anything. The word is the word.

items.fr: Elle est marron.
items.en: It is brown.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ ma.ʁɔ̃/
items.respell: el eh mah-ROHⁿ
items.notes: No e. Compare the row above this one, where an e was the whole story.

items.fr: Ils sont marron.
items.en: They are brown.
items.ipa: /il sɔ̃ ma.ʁɔ̃/
items.respell: eel sohⁿ mah-ROHⁿ
items.notes: No s either. Writing marrons is the one slip a French reader always notices.

items.fr: Elles sont marron.
items.en: They are brown.
items.ipa: /ɛl sɔ̃ ma.ʁɔ̃/
items.respell: el sohⁿ mah-ROHⁿ
items.notes: Feminine and plural and still the same six letters. All four rows are one word.

items.fr: sportif
items.en: sporty
items.ipa: /spɔʁ.tif/
items.respell: spor-TEEF
items.notes: The masculine. The f at the end is what puts it in its family.

items.fr: Mes rideaux sont kaki.
items.en: My curtains are khaki.
items.ipa: /me ʁi.do sɔ̃ ka.ki/
items.respell: may ree-DOH sohⁿ kah-KEE
items.notes: Kaki is a dust colour named after the dust. It has never agreed with anything.

items.fr: nouvelle
items.en: new (feminine)
items.ipa: nu.vɛl
items.respell: noo-VEL

example.en: Here is my new address.
example.fr: Voici ma nouvelle adresse.

items.fr: évident
items.en: obvious
items.ipa: /e.vi.dɑ̃/
items.respell: ay-vee-DAHⁿ
items.notes: Ends in -ent, and that ending is about to be taken off rather than added to.

items.fr: constant
items.en: constant
items.ipa: /kɔ̃s.tɑ̃/
items.respell: kohⁿs-TAHⁿ
items.notes: Ends in -ant. Same story as the one above and a different vowel on the page.

items.fr: Il est lent.
items.en: He is slow.
items.ipa: /il ɛ lɑ̃/
items.respell: eel eh LAHⁿ
items.notes: The t is on the page and nowhere else. Say it and listen for what is missing.

items.fr: Elle est lente.
items.en: She is slow.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ lɑ̃t/
items.respell: eel eh LAHⁿT
items.notes: And now the t arrives. One letter on the page and one sound in the mouth, and the long word keeps both.

items.fr: Il est beau.
items.en: He is good-looking.
items.ipa: /il ɛ bo/
items.respell: eel eh BOH
items.notes: The plain form, and the one you learn the word in.

items.fr: Elle est belle.
items.en: She is beautiful.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ bɛl/
items.respell: el eh BEL
items.notes: Nothing about this one is regular, and you have had it since lesson 17 in A1. Say it out loud, because the next form borrows the sound.

items.fr: Il est vieux.
items.en: He is old.
items.ipa: /il ɛ vjø/
items.respell: eel eh VYUH
items.notes: Already ends in an x, which decides the plural before you get there.

items.fr: Ils sont beaux.
items.en: They are good-looking.
items.ipa: /il sɔ̃ bo/
items.respell: eel sohⁿ BOH
items.notes: An x, not an s, and it makes no more sound than an s would. This is the one you have to have seen.

items.fr: Les murs sont crème.
items.en: The walls are cream.
items.ipa: /le myʁ sɔ̃ kʁɛm/
items.respell: lay MÜR sohⁿ KREM
items.notes: Cream is a thing you can pour. Borrowed as a colour, it keeps the thing’s shape.

items.fr: Ses gants sont bleu marine.
items.en: Her gloves are navy blue.
items.ipa: /se ɡɑ̃ sɔ̃ blø ma.ʁin/
items.respell: say GAHⁿ sohⁿ bluh mah-REEN
items.notes: Two words, so neither of them moves. Not bleus, not marines.

items.fr: Mes chaises sont bleu clair.
items.en: My chairs are light blue.
items.ipa: /me ʃɛz sɔ̃ blø klɛʁ/
items.respell: may SHEHZ sohⁿ BLUH KLEHR
items.notes: Feminine and plural, and the colour is two words, so it stays exactly as it is.

items.fr: Ses vestes sont vertes.
items.en: Her jackets are green.
items.ipa: /se vɛst sɔ̃ vɛʁt/
items.respell: say VEST sohⁿ VEHRT
items.notes: An ordinary colour on a feminine plural noun: e for the gender, s for the number.

items.fr: Ses vestes sont marron.
items.en: Her jackets are brown.
items.ipa: /se vɛst sɔ̃ ma.ʁɔ̃/
items.respell: say VEST sohⁿ mah-ROHⁿ
items.notes: Same jackets, same sentence, and this one refuses both endings.

items.fr: Elle est sérieuse, votre colocataire ?
items.en: Is your flatmate serious?
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ se.ʁjøz vɔtʁ kɔ.lɔ.ka.tɛʁ/
items.respell: el eh say-RYUHZ | votr koh-loh-ka-TEHR
items.notes: The question that stopped the sentence. The form is in it, and it is not the one you own.

items.fr: Oui, elle est très sérieuse.
items.en: Yes, she is very serious.
items.ipa: /wi ɛl ɛ tʁɛ se.ʁjøz/
items.respell: WEE | el eh treh say-RYUHZ
items.notes: Four words, and the only one you had to build is the last.

items.fr: Les jumeaux sont sportifs.
items.en: The twin boys are athletic.
items.ipa: le ʒy.mo sɔ̃ spɔʁ.tif
items.respell: lay zhü-MOH sohⁿ spor-TEEF
items.notes: “sportif” takes a simple s in the masculine plural, “sportifs”.

items.fr: Les jumelles sont sportives.
items.en: The twin girls are athletic.
items.ipa: le ʒy.mɛl sɔ̃ spɔʁ.tiv
items.respell: lay zhü-MEL sohⁿ spor-TEEV
items.notes: “sportif” changes f to v before adding the feminine e, giving “sportive”.

items.fr: C'est un vieux sac.
items.en: It is an old bag.
items.ipa: /s‿ɛ tœ̃ vjø sak/
items.respell: seh-tuhⁿ vyuh SAK
items.notes: Third one, and the last time in this lesson that the plain form is what you want in front of a thing.

items.fr: C'est un grand appartement ?
items.en: Is it a big flat?
items.ipa: /s‿ɛ tœ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ t‿a.paʁ.tə.mɑ̃/
items.respell: seh-tuhⁿ grahⁿ-ta-par-tuh-MAHⁿ
items.notes: The question that started the sentence. Everything in it is lesson 18 in A1 and the answer is not.

items.fr: Oui, et c'est un bel immeuble.
items.en: Yes, and it is a lovely building.
items.ipa: /wi e s‿ɛ tœ̃ bɛ.li.mœbl/
items.respell: wee ay seh-tuhⁿ beh-lee-MUHBL
items.notes: Six words, and the only one that had to be built is the fifth.

items.fr: nouvel
items.en: new (before a vowel)
items.ipa: /nu.vɛl/
items.respell: noo-VEL
items.notes: The only one of the three that had no card anywhere in this course. Same sound as nouvelle, two letters shorter.

items.fr: lentement
items.en: slowly
items.ipa: lɑ̃t.mɑ̃
items.respell: lahⁿt-MAHⁿ
items.notes: lent + -ment

items.fr: doucement
items.en: gently, softly
items.ipa: dus.mɑ̃
items.respell: doos-MAHⁿ
items.notes: doux, douce + -ment

items.fr: sérieusement
items.en: seriously
items.ipa: se.ʁjøz.mɑ̃
items.respell: say-ryuhz-MAHⁿ
items.notes: sérieux, sérieuse + -ment

items.fr: rapidement
items.en: quickly
items.ipa: ʁa.pid.mɑ̃
items.respell: ra-peed-MAHⁿ
items.notes: rapide + -ment

items.fr: facilement
items.en: easily
items.ipa: fa.sil.mɑ̃
items.respell: fa-seel-MAHⁿ
items.notes: facile + -ment

items.fr: souvent
items.en: often
items.ipa: /suvɑ̃/
items.respell: soo-VAHⁿ
items.notes: Silent t, like 'soo-vahn'.

items.fr: lent
items.en: slow
items.ipa: /lɑ̃/
items.respell: LAHⁿ
items.notes: Feminine: lente. Opposite: rapide. Un bus lent.

items.fr: lente
items.en: slow (feminine)
items.ipa: /lɑ̃t/
items.respell: LAHⁿT
items.notes: The plain form is lent and you cannot hear its t. Here you can, and the long word keeps it.

items.fr: douce
items.en: soft, gentle (feminine)
items.ipa: /dus/
items.respell: DOOS
items.notes: An s arrives on the end and it is a sound rather than a letter. Doux has none of it.

items.fr: Il travaille sérieusement.
items.en: He works seriously.
items.ipa: /il tʁa.vaj se.ʁjøz.mɑ̃/
items.respell: eel tra-VAHY say-ryuhz-MAHⁿ
items.notes: The z is the third consonant and the third one you can hear.

items.fr: Il lit rapidement.
items.en: He reads quickly.
items.ipa: /il li ʁa.pid.mɑ̃/
items.respell: eel LEE ra-peed-MAHⁿ
items.notes: Rapide already ends in an e, so the woman form is the same word and the ending goes straight on.

items.fr: Il lit facilement.
items.en: He reads easily.
items.ipa: /il li fa.sil.mɑ̃/
items.respell: eel LEE fa-seel-MAHⁿ
items.notes: And the second one, with the same subject and the same verb, so the only thing that moved is the word on the end.

items.fr: Il est doux.
items.en: He is gentle.
items.ipa: /il ɛ du/
items.respell: eel eh DOO
items.notes: An x that has never been pronounced by anybody.

items.fr: Elle est douce.
items.en: She is gentle.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ dus/
items.respell: eel eh DOOS
items.notes: The x has become ce and it makes an s you can hear across a room. That s is the one the long word uses.

items.fr: Il parle lentement.
items.en: He speaks slowly.
items.ipa: /il paʁl lɑ̃t.mɑ̃/
items.respell: eel PARL lahⁿt-MAHⁿ
items.notes: Sixteen letters, which is exactly what the dictée will take. The t you can hear is the middle of the word.

items.fr: Il parle doucement.
items.en: He speaks gently.
items.ipa: /il paʁl dus.mɑ̃/
items.respell: eel PARL doos-MAHⁿ
items.notes: Same verb, same position, different ending on the front half. The s is doing the work.

items.fr: C'est un bon jour.
items.en: It is a good day.
items.ipa: /s‿ɛ tœ̃ bɔ̃ ʒuʁ/
items.respell: seh-tuhⁿ bohⁿ ZHOOR
items.notes: Bon is in front of a thing here, which is where bon goes and where bien never does.

items.fr: Le monsieur qui est près de la fenêtre attend depuis une heure.
items.en: The gentleman who is near the window has been waiting an hour.
items.ipa: /lə mə.sjø ki ɛ pʁɛ də la fə.nɛtʁ a.tɑ̃ də.pɥi y.nœʁ/
items.respell: luh muh-SYUH kee eh preh duh lah fuh-NETR · ah-tahⁿ duh-püee ü-NUHR

items.fr: Je mange souvent.
items.en: I often eat.
items.ipa: /ʒə mɑ̃ʒ su.vɑ̃/
items.respell: zhuh MAHⁿZH soo-VAHⁿ
items.notes: Fourteen letters and the whole of the placement rule. English would put the middle word first.

items.fr: Elle chante bien.
items.en: She sings well.
items.ipa: /ɛl ʃɑ̃t bjɛ̃/
items.respell: el SHAHⁿT BYEHⁿ
items.notes: Not built from anything, and the one you will reach for most often.

items.fr: Il chante mal.
items.en: He sings badly.
items.ipa: /il ʃɑ̃t mal/
items.respell: eel SHAHⁿT MAL
items.notes: The opposite of the one above, and it is not mauvaisement either.

items.fr: Il parle vite.
items.en: He speaks fast.
items.ipa: /il paʁl vit/
items.respell: eel PARL VEET
items.notes: No adjective behind it at all. It is a word on its own and it always has been.

items.fr: Les chevaux ont couru dans le champ et ils ont sauté par-dessus la barrière.
items.en: The horses ran in the field and jumped over the fence.
items.ipa: le ʃəvo ɔ̃ kuʁy dɑ̃ lə ʃɑ̃ e ilz‿ɔ̃ sote paʁdəsu la baʁjɛʁ
items.notes: "couru", from courir, takes no final e even though "les chevaux" is masculine plural, and "champ" ends in a silent p.

items.fr: Je vais chez le médecin.
items.en: I am going to the doctor's.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ ʃe lə med.sɛ̃/
items.respell: zhuh veh shay luh mayd-SEHⁿ
items.notes: A person, so chez, and the le stays exactly where it was.

items.fr: Je vais à Paris.
items.en: I am going to Paris.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ a pa.ʁi/
items.respell: zhuh veh a pa-REE
items.notes: A city has no article to fold with, so à goes straight on.

items.fr: Je vais au marché.
items.en: I am going to the market.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ o maʁ.ʃe/
items.respell: zhuh veh oh mar-SHAY
items.notes: À and le folded into one word, which is lesson 24 in A1's rule with a shop behind it.

items.fr: la banque
items.en: the bank
items.ipa: /bɑ̃k/
items.respell: BAHⁿK

items.fr: passer chez quelqu'un
items.en: to drop by someone's place
items.ipa: pa.se ʃe kɛl.kœ̃
items.respell: pah-SAY SHAY kehl-KUHⁿ
items.notes: Chez means at the home of.

items.fr: Je vais en France.
items.en: I am going to France.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ ɑ̃ fʁɑ̃s/
items.respell: zhuh veh ahⁿ FRAHⁿSS
items.notes: La France has an article and en throws it away. Fourteen letters, and the country half of this is a1.22's.

items.fr: chez le médecin
items.en: at the doctor's
items.ipa: /ʃe lə med.sɛ̃/
items.respell: shay luh mayd-SEHⁿ
items.notes: Three words and they stay three words. This is the phrase the whole lesson is built to produce.

items.fr: chez la dentiste
items.en: at the dentist's
items.ipa: /ʃe la dɑ̃.tist/
items.respell: shay lah dahⁿ-TEEST
items.notes: The same word with la instead of le, and chez does nothing to that either. Dentiste is the same word for a man and a woman.

items.fr: chez le boulanger
items.en: at the baker's
items.ipa: /ʃe lə bu.lɑ̃.ʒe/
items.respell: shay luh boo-lahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: The man who bakes. Half of the pair this lesson exists for.

items.fr: Je vais chez le boulanger.
items.en: I am going to the baker's.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ ʃe lə bu.lɑ̃.ʒe/
items.respell: zhuh veh shay luh boo-lahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: The person.

items.fr: chez Marie
items.en: at Marie's
items.ipa: /ʃe ma.ʁi/
items.respell: shay ma-REE
items.notes: A name, so there is no article to leave alone. Nine letters and the shortest thing in the lesson.

items.fr: à la boulangerie
items.en: at the bakery
items.ipa: /a la bu.lɑ̃ʒ.ʁi/
items.respell: ah lah boo-lahⁿzh-REE
items.notes: The shop where the man works. À and la do not fold, which lesson 24 in A1 measured and this lesson leans on.

items.fr: Je vais à la boulangerie.
items.en: I am going to the bakery.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ a la bu.lɑ̃ʒ.ʁi/
items.respell: zhuh veh ah lah boo-lahⁿzh-REE
items.notes: The shop. Same errand, same door, and not one word in common with the line above except the first two.

items.fr: C'est la même porte.
items.en: It is the same door.
items.ipa: /sɛ la mɛm pɔʁt/
items.respell: seh lah mem PORT
items.notes: Fifteen letters, and it is the sentence that makes the pair worth learning rather than worth memorising.

items.fr: C'est à toi.
items.en: It's yours.
items.respell: seh tah TWAH

items.fr: Le sac est à moi.
items.en: The bag is mine.
items.respell: luh SAK eh tah MWAH

items.fr: Le directeur de l'école a annoncé un changement d'horaire.
items.en: The school principal announced a schedule change.
items.ipa: lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ də l‿e.kɔl a a.nɔ̃.se œ̃ ʃɑ̃ʒ.mɑ̃ dɔ.ʁɛʁ
items.notes: "horaire" starts with a silent h, so the elision in "d'horaire" is compulsory.

items.fr: Nous avons acheté six cahiers et huit crayons pour la rentrée.
items.en: We bought six notebooks and eight pencils for the start of school.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ aʃ.te si ka.je e ɥi kʁɛ.jɔ̃ puʁ la ʁɑ̃.tʁe
items.notes: The x of "six" and the t of "huit" are not said before a consonant.

items.fr: Le bulletin de ma fille indique une bonne moyenne générale.
items.en: My daughter's report card shows a good overall average.
items.ipa: lə byl.tɛ̃ də ma fij ɛ̃.dik yn bɔn mwa.jɛn ʒe.ne.ʁal
items.notes: "moyenne" takes two n, and writing only one is a common slip.

items.fr: Les enseignants se réunissent chaque mois pour discuter des élèves.
items.en: The teachers meet every month to discuss the students.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.sɛ.ɲɑ̃ sə ʁe.y.nis ʃak mwa puʁ dis.ky.te de.z‿e.lɛv
items.notes: "enseignants" ends in -ants. Do not confuse it with "enseignements".

items.fr: J'ai payé les frais de scolarité avant la date limite.
items.en: I paid the tuition fees before the deadline.
items.ipa: ʒe pe.je le fʁɛ də sko.la.ʁi.te a.vɑ̃ la dat li.mit
items.notes: "frais" ends in -ais with a silent s, which is easy to forget.

items.fr: La bibliothécaire a rangé les livres sur l'étagère du fond.
items.en: The librarian put the books away on the back shelf.
items.ipa: la bi.bli.jɔ.te.kɛʁ a ʁɑ̃.ʒe le livʁ syʁ l‿e.ta.ʒɛʁ dy fɔ̃
items.notes: "bibliothécaire" has a silent h after the first bi, and it is often left out.

items.fr: Mon fils apprend son vocabulaire tous les soirs avant le dîner.
items.en: My son learns his vocabulary every evening before dinner.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fis a.pʁɑ̃ sɔ̃ vɔ.ka.by.lɛʁ tu le swaʁ a.vɑ̃ lə di.ne
items.notes: "dîner" keeps the circumflex on the i in the traditional spelling.

items.fr: Les élèves ont écouté attentivement la nouvelle enseignante.
items.en: The students listened attentively to the new teacher.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv ɔ̃.t‿e.ku.te a.tɑ̃.ti.vmɑ̃ la nu.vɛl ɑ̃.sɛ.ɲɑ̃t
items.notes: There are two links here, and "ont" before "écouté" is said ɔ̃t.

items.fr: depuis deux heures
items.en: for two hours, and still going
items.ipa: /də.pɥi dø zœʁ/
items.respell: duh-PWEE duh ZUHR
items.notes: The same two hours as the row above and the other end left open.

items.fr: Le professeur a noté sept fautes dans ma dictée.
items.en: The teacher noted seven mistakes in my dictation.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ a nɔ.te sɛt fot dɑ̃ ma dik.te
items.notes: "sept" is said with its final t, unlike "cent".

items.fr: Nous avons rempli le formulaire pour la classe de francisation.
items.en: We filled out the form for the francization class.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.pli lə fɔʁ.my.lɛʁ puʁ la klas də fʁɑ̃.si.za.sjɔ̃
items.notes: "francisation" takes a c, not an s, whatever the sound suggests.

items.fr: L'agent a vérifié l'orthographe de son nom sur le certificat.
items.en: The clerk checked the spelling of his name on the certificate.
items.ipa: l‿a.ʒɑ̃ a ve.ʁi.fje l‿ɔʁ.tɔ.gʁaf də sɔ̃ nɔ̃ syʁ lə sɛʁ.ti.fi.ka
items.notes: "orthographe" is written with an h after the t, and it is often left out.

items.fr: Le conseil scolaire a envoyé un avis aux familles cette semaine.
items.en: The school board sent a notice to families this week.
items.ipa: lə kɔ̃.sɛj sko.lɛʁ a ɑ̃.vwa.je œ̃.n‿a.vi o fa.mij sɛt sə.mɛn
items.notes: "conseil" ends in -eil. Do not confuse it with "conseille".

items.fr: Les enfants ont chanté ensemble pendant la fête de fin d'année.
items.en: The children sang together during the end-of-year party.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃.z‿ɔ̃ ʃɑ̃.te ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la fɛt də fɛ̃ da.ne
items.notes: The link between "enfants" and "ont" is said as a z.

items.fr: Le directeur a reçu une lettre du conseil scolaire ce matin.
items.en: The principal received a letter from the school board this morning.
items.ipa: lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ a ʁə.sy yn lɛtʁ dy kɔ̃.sɛj sko.lɛʁ sə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: "reçu" takes a cedilla under the c before the u, to keep the s sound.

items.fr: J'ai révisé mes verbes irréguliers avant l'examen oral.
items.en: I reviewed my irregular verbs before the oral exam.
items.ipa: ʒe ʁe.vi.ze me vɛʁb i.ʁe.gy.lje a.vɑ̃ l‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃ ɔ.ʁal
items.notes: "irréguliers" takes two r, and one is often dropped.

items.fr: Les élèves ont applaudi leur professeur le dernier jour d'école.
items.en: The students applauded their teacher on the last day of school.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv ɔ̃.t‿a.plo.di lœʁ pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ lə dɛʁ.nje ʒuʁ de.kɔl
items.notes: "applaudi" takes two p, and writing one is a common mistake.

items.fr: Ma collègue a suivi une formation continue le week-end dernier.
items.en: My colleague took a continuing-education course last weekend.
items.ipa: ma kɔ.lɛg a sɥi.vi yn fɔʁ.ma.sjɔ̃ kɔ̃.ti.ny lə wik.ɛnd dɛʁ.nje
items.notes: "week-end" keeps its English spelling, with a hyphen in French.

items.fr: Nous avons demandé une attestation officielle après le stage.
items.en: We requested an official attestation after the internship.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ də.mɑ̃.de yn a.tɛs.ta.sjɔ̃ ɔ.fi.sjɛl a.pʁɛ lə staʒ
items.notes: "officielle" takes two f and ends in -ielle, not -ièle.

items.fr: Les parents ont assisté à la remise des diplômes samedi.
items.en: The parents attended the diploma ceremony on Saturday.
items.ipa: le pa.ʁɑ̃.z‿ɔ̃.t‿a.sis.te a la ʁə.miz de di.plom sam.di
items.notes: "assisté" takes two s to hold the s sound between vowels.

items.fr: J'ai vérifié l'horaire des examens sur le site de l'école.
items.en: I checked the exam schedule on the school's website.
items.ipa: ʒe ve.ʁi.fje l‿ɔ.ʁɛʁ de.z‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃ syʁ lə sit də l‿e.kɔl
items.notes: "horaire" starts with a silent h, which allows the elision.

items.fr: L'enseignant a noté nos progrès dans le carnet de suivi.
items.en: The teacher noted our progress in the tracking booklet.
items.ipa: l‿ɑ̃.sɛ.ɲɑ̃ a nɔ.te no pʁɔ.gʁɛ dɑ̃ lə kaʁ.nɛ də sɥi.vi
items.notes: "progrès" ends in a silent s, like "après".

items.fr: Nous avons choisi un tuteur pour aider notre fils en lecture.
items.en: We chose a tutor to help our son with reading.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʃwa.zi œ̃ ty.tœʁ puʁ ɛ.de nɔtʁ fis ɑ̃ lɛk.tyʁ
items.notes: "choisi" loses the t of "choisit" in the passé composé. Keep the two forms apart.

items.fr: La secrétaire a remis le certificat directement aux parents.
items.en: The secretary handed the certificate directly to the parents.
items.ipa: la sə.kʁe.tɛʁ a ʁə.mi lə sɛʁ.ti.fi.ka di.ʁɛk.tə.mɑ̃ o pa.ʁɑ̃
items.notes: "secrétaire" takes an acute accent then a grave one, and the two are often mixed up.

items.fr: Les élèves ont appris un nouveau poème pour la fête de l'école.
items.en: The students learned a new poem for the school celebration.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv ɔ̃.t‿a.pʁi œ̃ nu.vo pɔ.ɛm puʁ la fɛt də l‿e.kɔl
items.notes: "poème" takes a grave accent on the e, not a circumflex.

items.fr: en une heure
items.en: in an hour, that is how long it takes
items.ipa: /ɑ̃n yn œʁ/
items.respell: AHⁿ NÜN UHR
items.notes: The fifth card of a set the corpus published four fifths of.

items.fr: Le directeur adjoint surveille la cour pendant la récréation.
items.en: The vice principal watches the yard during recess.
items.ipa: lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ ad.ʒwɛ̃ syʁ.vɛj la kuʁ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la ʁe.kʁe.a.sjɔ̃
items.notes: "adjoint" ends in -oint. Keep the silent t in writing.

items.fr: J'ai signé le registre d'absence à l'accueil de l'école.
items.en: I signed the absence register at the school's front desk.
items.ipa: ʒe si.ɲe lə ʁə.ʒistʁ dab.sɑ̃s a l‿a.kœj də l‿e.kɔl
items.notes: "accueil" takes two c and is said a-keuille, not ak-seuille.

items.fr: Les enseignants ont préparé un examen commun pour tous les élèves.
items.en: The teachers prepared a common exam for all the students.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.sɛ.ɲɑ̃.z‿ɔ̃ pʁe.pa.ʁe œ̃.n‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃ kɔ.mœ̃ puʁ tu le.z‿e.lɛv
items.notes: "commun" takes two m. Do not confuse it with "comment".

items.fr: L'élève a demandé la permission de sortir de la classe.
items.en: The student asked for permission to leave the classroom.
items.ipa: l‿e.lɛv a də.mɑ̃.de la pɛʁ.mi.sjɔ̃ də sɔʁ.tiʁ də la klas
items.notes: "permission" takes two s to hold the s sound between vowels.

items.fr: J'habite ici depuis trois ans.
items.en: I have lived here for three years.
items.ipa: /ʒa.bit i.si də.pɥi tʁwa.zɑ̃/
items.respell: zha-BEET ee-SEE duh-PWEE trwah-ZAHⁿ
items.notes: The sentence the whole lesson exists to produce. The English is a perfect and the French is a present, and nothing in the French moves.

items.fr: Il y a un problème.
items.en: There is a problem.
items.ipa: /il i a œ̃ pʁɔ.blɛm/
items.respell: eel ee ah uhⁿ proh-BLEM
items.notes: A thing behind it, so the three words mean there is.

items.fr: Il y a deux jours.
items.en: Two days ago.
items.ipa: /il i a dø ʒuʁ/
items.respell: eel ee ah duh ZHOOR
items.notes: A measurement behind it and nothing after that, so the same three words mean ago. No verb in it at all, which is why it can be here.

items.fr: Je vais partir.
items.en: I am going to leave.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ paʁ.tiʁ/
items.respell: zhuh veh par-TEER
items.notes: Aller in the present and the naming form behind it, untouched.

items.fr: Il y a une heure de retard.
items.en: There is an hour of delay.
items.ipa: /il i a yn œʁ də ʁə.taʁ/
items.respell: eel ee ah ün UHR duh ruh-TAR
items.notes: The sharp one. Four words in common with « il y a une heure » and the fifth turns the hour back into a thing. This is why the rule is about the full stop and not about the noun.

items.fr: Tu vas partir.
items.en: You are going to leave.
items.ipa: /ty va paʁ.tiʁ/
items.respell: tü vah par-TEER
items.notes: The person moved and the second verb did not.

items.fr: Il va partir.
items.en: He is going to leave.
items.ipa: /il va paʁ.tiʁ/
items.respell: eel vah par-TEER
items.notes: The shortest of the six, ten letters, and the one the dictée uses for the pair because its negative also fits.

items.fr: Tu vas travailler ce soir ?
items.en: Are you going to work tonight?
items.ipa: /ty va tʁa.va.je sə swaʁ/
items.respell: tü vah trah-vah-YAY suh SWAR
items.notes: Her question, and every word in it is one the learner has had since lesson 1 in A2. The answer is one word longer than the question.

items.fr: Je ne vais pas travailler.
items.en: No, I am not going to work.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə vɛ pa tʁa.va.je/
items.respell: zhuh nuh veh pah trah-vah-YAY
items.notes: What he meant, in full. Twenty letters, so it is not a dictée target either.

items.fr: Ah, d'accord. À ce soir, alors.
items.en: Ah, all right. See you tonight, then.
items.ipa: /a da.kɔʁ a sə swaʁ a.lɔʁ/
items.respell: ah da-KOR · a suh SWAR ah-LOR
items.notes: She books him in, cheerfully, on the strength of a sentence that was correct. Nobody corrected anything, so nothing was learned and he is now expected.

items.fr: Tu vas faire quoi ce soir ?
items.en: What are you going to do tonight?
items.ipa: /ty va fɛʁ kwa sə swaʁ/
items.respell: tü vah FEHR kwah suh SWAR
items.notes: The commonest question in the language after « ça va ? », and it is this construction with a question word dropped into the slot.

items.fr: Nous allons partir.
items.en: We are going to leave.
items.ipa: /nu.za.lɔ̃ paʁ.tiʁ/
items.respell: noo za-lohⁿ par-TEER
items.notes: The liaison pulls a z across into allons and the nasal survives it.

items.fr: Le film que tout le monde recommande sort vendredi.
items.en: The film everybody recommends comes out on Friday.
items.ipa: /lə film kə tu lə mɔ̃d ʁə.kɔ.mɑ̃d sɔʁ vɑ̃.dʁə.di/
items.respell: luh FEELM kuh too luh mohⁿd ruh-koh-MAHⁿD · sor vahⁿ-druh-DEE

items.fr: Ils vont partir.
items.en: They are going to leave.
items.ipa: /il vɔ̃ paʁ.tiʁ/
items.respell: eel vohⁿ par-TEER
items.notes: The plural of the form the singular already had, and partir has still not moved.

items.fr: Tu ne vas pas partir.
items.en: You are not going to leave.
items.ipa: /ty nə va pa paʁ.tiʁ/
items.respell: tü nuh vah pah par-TEER

items.fr: Il ne va pas partir.
items.en: He is not going to leave.
items.ipa: /il nə va pa paʁ.tiʁ/
items.respell: eel nuh vah pah par-TEER
items.notes: The pair with row 503 is the one the dictée runs, because both halves of it fit.

items.fr: Je ne vais pas partir.
items.en: I am not going to leave.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə vɛ pa paʁ.tiʁ/
items.respell: zhuh nuh veh pah par-TEER
items.notes: In the futur proche the negative wraps aller, not the verb after it: ne vais pas partir.

items.fr: Vous allez partir.

items.fr: Nous n'allons pas partir.

items.ipa: /nu na.lɔ̃ pa paʁ.tiʁ/
items.respell: noo na-lohⁿ pah par-TEER
items.notes: The ne elides in front of the vowel and the liaison z goes with it: noo na-lohⁿ, not noo za-lohⁿ.

items.fr: Vous n'allez pas partir.
items.en: You are not going to leave. (to more than one person, or politely)
items.ipa: /vu na.le pa paʁ.tiʁ/
items.respell: voo na-lay pah par-TEER
items.notes: The same elision and the same lost liaison.

items.respell: eel nuh vohⁿ pah par-TEER

items.notes: The -ER group, and lesson 1's own headline verb. An -ER naming form ends in -er and its past form ends in -é, and those are the same sound.

items.respell: eel nohⁿ pa mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: Six persons, one gap, and the past form has stayed outside it every time.

items.fr: en bus
items.en: by bus

items.fr: Nous riions beaucoup.

items.en: We could see the sea.

items.en: Have you decided?
items.ipa: /vu.z‿a.ve ʃwa.zi/
items.respell: voo-z a-vay shwa-ZEE
items.notes: The pivot of the meal, and it arrives in the passé composé.

items.en: Have you made your choice?
items.ipa: /vu.z‿a.ve fɛ vɔtʁ ʃwa/

items.notes: The same question in different words. A real script is not a fixed string.

items.respell: zhuh voo kohⁿ-SEHY luh pla dü ZHOOR

items.fr: Et comme entrée ?
items.en: And for a starter?
items.ipa: /e kɔm ɑ̃.tʁe/
items.respell: ay kom ahⁿ-TRAY
items.notes: The same comme frame as Et comme boisson ?

items.fr: Tout se passe bien ?
items.en: Is everything all right?
items.ipa: /tu sə pas bjɛ̃/
items.respell: too suh pass BYEHⁿ
items.notes: Asked mid-meal. It wants only oui, or a problem.

items.fr: le code
items.en: the PIN
items.ipa: /lə kɔd/
items.respell: luh KOD
items.notes: What a card machine asks for. Le code secret is the formal term; at a till it is just le code.

items.fr: le paiement sans contact

items.ipa: /lə pɛ.mɑ̃ sɑ̃ kɔ̃.takt/
items.respell: luh peh-MAHⁿ sahⁿ kohⁿ-TAKT

items.notes: Le ticket, not le ticket de caisse, at the counter. The long form is what is printed on it.

items.en: the subtotal
items.ipa: /lə su.tɔ.tal/
items.respell: luh soo-to-TAL
items.notes: The line on a receipt above the discounts. Reading it is s19; nothing in this lesson asks you to compute from it.

items.fr: la passe
items.en: the transit pass
items.ipa: /la pas/
items.respell: lah PAHSS
items.notes: Quebec for l'abonnement. Structural vocabulary rather than a fare product, so it does not age with the operator.

items.en: by metro

items.en: Was everything OK?
items.ipa: /sa a e.te/
items.respell: sa a ay-TAY
