items.fr: Il manque une couverture dans la chambre.
items.en: There is a blanket missing in the room.

items.fr: La clé ne marche pas.
items.en: The key does not work.

items.fr: Il n'y a plus d'eau chaude.
items.en: There is no hot water left.

items.fr: Je suis désolée, c'est complet ce soir.
items.en: I am sorry, we are full this evening.

items.fr: Je ne peux rien faire ce soir, monsieur.
items.en: There is nothing I can do this evening, sir.

items.fr: Je vais voir ce que je peux faire.
items.en: I will see what I can do.

items.fr: Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais avec toi.
items.en: If I had time, I would come with you.
items.ipa: /si ʒa.vɛ lə tɑ̃ ʒə vjɛ̃.dʁɛ a.vɛk twa/
items.respell: see zha-VEH luh TAHⁿ zhuh vyehⁿ-DREH ah-vek TWAH

items.fr: Je voudrais un café.
items.en: I would like a coffee.
items.ipa: /ʒə vu.dʁɛ œ̃ ka.fe/
items.respell: zhuh voo-DREH uhⁿ kah-FAY

items.fr: En espèces, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: In cash, please.
items.ipa: /ɑ̃.n‿ɛs.pɛs sil vu plɛ/
items.respell: ahⁿ-n ess-PESS seel voo PLEH
items.notes: The answer form of payer en espèces: in cash.

items.fr: Je travaillais dans une agence de voyages.
items.en: I worked at a travel agency.
items.ipa: /ʒə tʁa.va.jɛ dɑ̃.zy.na.ʒɑ̃s də vwa.jaʒ/
items.respell: zhuh trah-vah-YEH dahⁿ-zü-nah-ZHAHⁿS duh vwah-YAZH

items.fr: Je voudrais parler au responsable, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: I would like to speak to the manager, please.

items.fr: Est-ce que quelqu'un peut venir voir ?
items.en: Could somebody come and look?

items.fr: Est-ce que je peux parler à quelqu'un d'autre ?
items.en: Could I speak to somebody else?

items.fr: Ça fait combien ?
items.en: How much is that?
items.ipa: /sa fɛ kɔ̃.bjɛ̃/
items.respell: sa feh kohⁿ-BYEHⁿ
items.notes: The single most frequent question in a French shop and it existed nowhere in this corpus. Store it whole: it is not ça + faire + combien.

items.fr: Qui est-ce que je peux voir pour ce problème ?
items.en: Who can I see about this problem?

items.fr: Bonjour, je voudrais une baguette, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: Hello, I would like a baguette, please.
items.ipa: /bɔ̃.ʒuʁ ʒə vu.dʁɛ yn ba.ɡɛt sil vu plɛ/
items.respell: bohⁿ-ZHOOR zhuh voo-DREH ün ba-GET seel voo PLEH
items.notes: Greeting and request in one breath. In a French shop the bonjour is not optional and it comes before the noun, never after.

items.fr: Par carte, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: By card, please.
items.ipa: /paʁ kaʁt sil vu plɛ/
items.respell: par KART seel voo PLEH
items.notes: Three words answer the payment question completely. Building a sentence around it marks you out as translating.

items.fr: Ça fait quatre-vingt-dix-sept euros trente.
items.en: That comes to ninety-seven euros thirty.
items.ipa: /sa fɛ ka.tʁə.vɛ̃.dis.sɛt ø.ʁo tʁɑ̃t/
items.respell: sa feh ka-truh-vaⁿ-dee-SET eu-ro TRAHⁿT
items.notes: The number from the scene. Ninety-seven and thirty, said as one run, and the only clue it has finished is that she stops.

items.fr: Ça vous fait vingt-trois euros quarante.
items.en: That comes to twenty-three euros forty.
items.ipa: /sa vu fɛ vɛ̃t.tʁwa ø.ʁo ka.ʁɑ̃t/
items.respell: sa voo feh vaⁿt-TRWA eu-ro ka-RAHⁿT
items.notes: The same move with vous inside it. The extra syllable is the only difference and it changes nothing you have to do.

items.fr: La climatisation ne marche pas non plus.
items.en: The air conditioning does not work either.

items.fr: C'est la deuxième nuit avec le même bruit.
items.en: This is the second night with the same noise.

items.fr: Il fait aussi froid qu'hier.
items.en: It is as cold as yesterday.
items.respell: EEL FEH oh-see FRWAH KYEHR

items.fr: Ce café est aussi fort que le thé.
items.en: This coffee is as strong as the tea.
items.respell: suh ka-FAY eh toh-see FOR kuh luh TAY

items.fr: moins grand
items.en: less big
items.respell: mwehⁿ GRAHⁿ

items.fr: aussi cher
items.en: just as expensive
items.respell: oh-see SHEHR

items.fr: Le responsable est là ce soir ?
items.en: Is the manager here this evening?

items.fr: La chambre n'a pas été faite.
items.en: The room has not been made up.

items.fr: Il n'y a pas de serviettes dans la salle de bain.
items.en: There are no towels in the bathroom.

items.fr: La fenêtre ne ferme pas.
items.en: The window does not close.

items.fr: Le chauffage est trop fort.
items.en: The heating is too high.

items.fr: Il fait très froid dans la chambre.
items.en: It is very cold in the room.

items.fr: Je vais prévenir le responsable.
items.en: I will let the manager know.

items.fr: Le responsable arrive à huit heures demain.
items.en: The manager gets in at eight tomorrow.

items.fr: Je suis vraiment désolée pour le dérangement.
items.en: I am very sorry for the trouble.

items.fr: Vous pouvez épeler votre nom, madame ?
items.en: Could you spell your name, madam?

items.fr: Quelqu'un va monter dans dix minutes.
items.en: Somebody will come up in ten minutes.

items.fr: Cette rue est aussi longue que l'avenue.
items.en: This street is as long as the avenue.
items.respell: set RÜ eh toh-see LOHⁿG kuh lav-NÜ

items.fr: Ce livre est aussi intéressant que le film.
items.en: This book is as interesting as the film.
items.respell: suh LEEVR eh toh-see ahⁿ-tay-reh-SAHⁿ kuh luh FEELM

items.fr: Alors, deux baguettes, ça fait deux euros quarante.
items.en: So, two baguettes, that comes to two euros forty.
items.ipa: /a.lɔʁ dø ba.ɡɛt sa fɛ dø.z‿ø.ʁo ka.ʁɑ̃t/
items.respell: a-LOR deu ba-GET sa feh deu-z eu-ro ka-RAHⁿT
items.notes: The baker counts your order back at you before the figure. Alors is the half-second of warning that a number is coming.

items.fr: Ça fait six euros quatre-vingt-quinze.
items.en: That comes to six euros ninety-five.
items.ipa: /sa fɛ si.z‿ø.ʁo ka.tʁə.vɛ̃.kɛ̃z/
items.respell: sa feh see-z eu-ro ka-truh-vaⁿ-KAⁿZ
items.notes: The cents run longer than the euros. Lesson 3 in A1 taught quatre-vingt-quinze against quatre-vingt-dix-neuf; here it arrives after a currency word.

items.fr: Ça fera huit euros dix, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: That will be eight euros ten, please.
items.ipa: /sa fə.ʁa ɥi.t‿ø.ʁo dis sil vu plɛ/
items.respell: sa fuh-RA weet eu-ro DEESS seel voo PLEH
items.notes: A future tense for a thing that is true now. Recognising fera as the same move as fait is the whole point of s09.

items.fr: Merci, on vous rappelle la semaine prochaine.
items.en: Thank you, we will call you back next week.

items.fr: Vous travaillez dans quoi ?
items.en: What field do you work in?

items.fr: Alors, vous faites quoi dans la vie ?
items.en: So, what do you do for a living?

items.fr: Ah bon ? Et ça vous plaît ?
items.en: Really? And do you enjoy it?

items.fr: Vous êtes là depuis longtemps ?
items.en: Have you been there long?

items.fr: Vous préférez travailler en équipe ou de votre côté ?
items.en: Do you prefer working in a team or on your own?

items.fr: Et après, vous avez fait quoi ?
items.en: And after that, what did you do?

items.fr: Vous vous occupez de quoi, exactement ?
items.en: What do you handle, exactly?

items.fr: Le total est de quarante-deux euros.
items.en: The total is forty-two euros.
items.ipa: /lə tɔ.tal ɛ də ka.ʁɑ̃t.dø ø.ʁo/
items.respell: luh to-TAL eh duh ka-rahⁿt-DEU-zeu-ro
items.notes: The supermarket screen version, and the most formal of the four. No cents, so nothing follows the currency word.

items.fr: Ça fait quinze euros soixante, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: That comes to fifteen euros sixty, please.
items.ipa: /sa fɛ kɛ̃.z‿ø.ʁo swa.sɑ̃t sil vu plɛ/
items.respell: sa feh kaⁿ-z eu-ro swa-SAHⁿT seel voo PLEH
items.notes: The s'il vous plaît on the end is not politeness about the price. It is the request to hand something over, and it means she has finished.

items.fr: Ça fait cinquante euros pile.
items.en: That comes to exactly fifty euros.
items.ipa: /sa fɛ sɛ̃.kɑ̃t‿ø.ʁo pil/
items.respell: sa feh saⁿ-kahⁿt eu-ro PEEL
items.notes: Pile means on the nose. It is the one word that tells you there are no cents coming, so you can stop listening.

items.fr: C'est un peu cher pour moi.
items.en: That is a bit expensive for me.
items.ipa: /sɛ.t‿œ̃ pø ʃɛʁ puʁ mwa/
items.respell: say-t uhⁿ peu SHEHR poor MWA
items.notes: Un peu is what makes it sayable. C'est cher on its own sounds like a complaint about the shop rather than about your wallet.

items.fr: Ça vous fait dix-neuf euros quatre-vingt-dix.
items.en: That comes to nineteen euros ninety.
items.ipa: /sa vu fɛ diz.nœ.v‿ø.ʁo ka.tʁə.vɛ̃.dis/
items.respell: sa voo feh deez-NUH-v eu-ro ka-truh-vaⁿ-DEESS
items.notes: Two nineteens and two nineties in one sentence, and the currency word is the only thing separating the euros from the cents.

items.fr: Insérez votre carte et tapez votre code.
items.en: Insert your card and enter your PIN.
items.ipa: /ɛ̃.se.ʁe vɔtʁ kaʁt e ta.pe vɔtʁ kɔd/
items.respell: aⁿ-say-RAY votr KART ay ta-PAY votr KOD
items.notes: Two imperatives and no please, which is the register of a machine instruction rather than rudeness.

items.fr: Vous pouvez retirer votre carte.
items.en: You can take your card out.
items.ipa: /vu pu.ve ʁə.ti.ʁe vɔtʁ kaʁt/
items.respell: voo poo-vay ruh-tee-RAY votr KART
items.notes: The transaction is finished. Nothing else is required of you, and the receipt question comes next or not at all.

items.fr: Je regarde seulement, merci.
items.en: I am just looking, thanks.
items.ipa: /ʒə ʁə.ɡaʁd sœl.mɑ̃ mɛʁ.si/
items.respell: zhuh ruh-GARD seul-MAHⁿ mehr-SEE
items.notes: The answer to Je peux vous aider ?. Without it a learner either buys something or leaves, and both happen a lot.

items.fr: pendant deux ans
items.en: for two years
items.ipa: /pɑ̃.dɑ̃ dø.zɑ̃/
items.respell: pahⁿ-dahⁿ deu-ZAHⁿ

items.respell: plü moh-VEH

items.en: faster
items.respell: plü VEET

items.en: more slowly
items.respell: mwehⁿ VEET

items.fr: aussi vite
items.en: just as fast
items.respell: oh-see VEET

items.en: Are you looking for something?
items.ipa: /vu ʃɛʁ.ʃe kɛl.kə ʃoz/
items.respell: voo shehr-shay kel-kuh SHOHZ
items.notes: Are you looking for something? The shop assistant's approach.

items.fr: Vous faites quelle taille ?
items.en: What size are you?
items.ipa: /vu fɛt kɛl taj/
items.respell: voo fet kel TAHY
items.notes: The clothing shop swaps this in where the market stall asks a quantity.

items.fr: D'habitude, il arrivait à huit heures.
items.en: He usually arrived at eight.
items.ipa: /da.bi.tyd i.la.ʁi.vɛ a ɥi.tœʁ/
items.respell: da-bee-TÜD ee-la-ree-veh a wee-TUHR

items.en: That morning I did what I usually do: I took the bus.

items.respell: suh ma-tehⁿ-LA zhay feh kom da-bee-TÜD zhay pree luh BÜS

items.en: Do you have this in a thirty-eight?
items.ipa: /vu.z‿a.ve sa ɑ̃ tʁɑ̃t.ɥit/
items.respell: voo-z a-vay sa ahⁿ trahⁿt-WEET
items.notes: The size question without the word for size. French sizes are numbers, so the number does all the work and ça points at the garment.

items.fr: Je vous rends deux euros soixante.
items.en: Here is two euros sixty change.
items.ipa: /ʒə vu ʁɑ̃ dø.z‿ø.ʁo swa.sɑ̃t/
items.respell: zhuh voo rahⁿ deu-z eu-ro swa-SAHⁿT
items.notes: The second number of the transaction, and it arrives once, faster than the first. Rendre is lesson 4 in A2's verb, used whole.

items.fr: Tout à coup, je n'avais plus envie de rire.
items.en: All of a sudden I did not feel like laughing any more.
items.ipa: /tu.ta.ku ʒə na.vɛ ply.zɑ̃.vi də ʁiʁ/
items.respell: too-ta-KOO zhuh na-veh plü-zahⁿ-VEE duh REER

items.notes: Ne...plus de, not ne...plus des. The bad news arrives before you have finished asking, and it is the one deviation this script has.

items.en: How are you paying?
items.ipa: /vu ʁe.ɡle kɔ.mɑ̃/
items.respell: voo ray-glay ko-MAHⁿ
items.notes: Comment is how, not how much. Lesson 24 in A2 taught this at a restaurant table; the till asks it the same way and the answer is still three words.

items.fr: Voilà votre monnaie.
items.en: Here is your change.
items.ipa: /vwa.la vɔtʁ mɔ.nɛ/
items.respell: vwa-LA votr mo-NEH
items.notes: No figure at all. The coins are counted into your hand and you are expected to have been listening to the first number.

items.fr: Souvent, le dimanche, nous allions chez ma tante.
items.en: Often, on Sundays, we went to my aunt’s.
items.ipa: /su.vɑ̃ lə di.mɑ̃ʃ nu.za.ljɔ̃ ʃe ma tɑ̃t/
items.respell: soo-VAHⁿ luh dee-MAHⁿSH noo-za-LYOHⁿ shay ma TAHⁿT

items.respell: zhuh voo rahⁿ lah mo-NEH sür vaⁿt-EU-ro

items.respell: suh dee-mahⁿsh-LA noo som-za-LAY shay ma TAHⁿT

items.respell: soo-DEHⁿ

items.respell: luh rahⁿ-DÜ
items.notes: The noun printed on a receipt under the amount tendered. It is not the participle rendu: a participle is never a corpus item in this band.

items.fr: un jour
items.en: one day
items.ipa: /œ̃ ʒuʁ/

items.fr: tous les jours

items.respell: oo ah-vay VOO mal eg-zakt-MAHⁿ

items.respell: voo pruh-NAY dohtr may-dee-ka-MAHⁿ

items.respell: luh kar-tyay neh pa dü too KALM

items.fr: Tu as des enfants ?
items.en: Do you have children?
items.ipa: /ty a de.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃/
items.respell: tü AH day zahⁿ-FAHⁿ
items.notes: des, which lesson 8 in A1 owns, and which en takes away along with the noun.

items.fr: Oui, j'en prends.
items.en: Yes, I do.
items.ipa: /wi ʒɑ̃ pʁɑ̃/
items.respell: wee, zhahⁿ PRAHⁿ
items.notes: Twelve letters, and the same three English words again. English answers this question with the auxiliary and French answers it with the object.

items.fr: Oui, j'en ai trois.
items.en: Yes, I have three.
items.ipa: /wi ʒɑ̃.n‿e tʁwa/
items.respell: wee, zhahⁿ nay TRWAH
items.notes: THE NUMBER STAYS AND THE NOUN GOES, which is the shape English has no equivalent for at all: "I have three" says nothing about what three of.

items.fr: J'en ai beaucoup.
items.en: I have a lot.
items.ipa: /ʒɑ̃.n‿e bo.ku/
items.respell: zhahⁿ nay boh-KOO
items.notes: beaucoup de is lesson 8 in A1's and the de went inside en with the noun.

items.fr: J'en ai assez.
items.en: I have enough.
items.ipa: /ʒɑ̃.n‿e a.se/
items.respell: zhahⁿ nay ah-SAY
items.notes: assez de, and the de is gone again. Four quantity words and the same disappearance each time.

items.fr: J'en veux un peu.
items.en: I want a little.
items.ipa: /ʒɑ̃ vø œ̃ pø/
items.respell: zhahⁿ VUH uhⁿ PUH
items.notes: En replaces du café, de la soupe, des pommes. The quantity word stays behind.

items.fr: C'est quel quai, s'il vous plaît ?
items.en: Which platform is it, please?
items.ipa: /sɛ kɛl kɛ sil vu plɛ/
items.respell: seh kel KEH seel voo PLEH
items.notes: Quel is lesson 23 in A1's question word. The useful part here is that this is the question you ask AFTER he has already told you.

items.fr: Tu prends du sucre ?
items.en: Do you take sugar?
items.ipa: /ty pʁɑ̃ dy sykʁ/
items.respell: tü PRAHⁿ dü SÜKR
items.notes: A second verb, so the learner does not read the rule as a fact about avoir.

items.fr: nous finirions
items.en: we would finish
items.ipa: /nu fi.ni.ʁjɔ̃/
items.respell: noo fee-nee-RYOHⁿ

items.en: they would finish
items.ipa: /il fi.ni.ʁɛ/
items.respell: eel fee-nee-REH
items.prompt: finir · conditionnel · ils

items.fr: je vendrais
items.en: I would sell
items.ipa: /ʒə vɑ̃.dʁɛ/
items.respell: zhuh vahⁿ-DREH
items.prompt: vendre · conditionnel · je

items.fr: j'habiterais
items.en: I would live
items.ipa: /ʒa.bi.tə.ʁɛ/
items.respell: zhah-bee-tuh-REH
items.prompt: habiter · conditionnel · je

items.fr: Oui, j'y vais tous les samedis.
items.en: Yes, I go every Saturday.
items.ipa: /wi ʒi vɛ tu le sam.di/
items.respell: wee, zhee VEH too lay sam-DEE
items.notes: Role play turn.

items.fr: je ferais
items.en: I would do, I would make
items.ipa: /ʒə fə.ʁɛ/
items.respell: zhuh fuh-REH
items.prompt: faire · conditionnel · je

items.fr: il ferait
items.en: he would do, he would make
items.ipa: /il fə.ʁɛ/
items.respell: eel fuh-REH
items.prompt: faire · conditionnel · il

items.fr: Il s'est douché.
items.en: He showered.
items.ipa: /il sɛ du.ʃe/
items.respell: eel seh doo-SHAY
items.notes: The singular against 819s plural, and only the writing tells them apart.

items.fr: Je me suis douché et je me suis habillé.
items.en: I showered and got dressed.
items.ipa: /ʒə mə sɥi du.ʃe e ʒə mə sɥi za.bi.je/
items.respell: zhuh muh swee doo-SHAY ay zhuh muh swee zah-bee-YAY
items.notes: Role play turn 2. Two of them in one sentence, and the first word is repeated rather than shared.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes levés en même temps.
items.en: We got up at the same time.
items.ipa: /nu nu sɔm lə.ve ɑ̃ mɛm tɑ̃/
items.respell: noo noo somm luh-VAY ahⁿ mem TAHⁿ
items.notes: Role play turn 3. The doubled form and the plural ending, produced rather than read.

items.fr: Non, je ne me suis pas couché tard.
items.en: No, I did not go to bed late.
items.ipa: /nɔ̃ ʒə nə mə sɥi pa ku.ʃe taʁ/
items.respell: nohⁿ, zhuh nuh muh swee pah koo-SHAY TAR
items.notes: Role play turn 4. The negative, on a verb the six-person walk never carried.

items.fr: Ils se sont dépêchés ce matin.
items.en: They hurried this morning.
items.ipa: /il sə sɔ̃ de.pɛ.ʃe sə ma.tɛ̃/
items.respell: eel suh sohⁿ day-peh-SHAY suh mah-TAHⁿ
items.notes: Role play turn 5, on the verb that carries the little word and means nothing by it.

items.fr: Elle s'est reposée un peu.
items.en: She rested a little.
items.ipa: /ɛl sɛ ʁə.po.ze œ̃ pø/
items.respell: ehl seh ruh-poh-ZAY uhⁿ PUH
items.notes: A fourth verb the lesson never conjugated, with the ending on it.

items.fr: Elle s'est souvenue de mon nom.
items.en: She remembered my name.
items.ipa: /ɛl sɛ suv.ny də mɔ̃ nɔ̃/
items.respell: ehl seh soov-NÜ duh mohⁿ NOHⁿ
items.notes: THE SECOND WORD IS NOT BUILT FROM THE ENDING THIS LESSON USES. souvenue comes off venir, which is a2.20s -u group, and the ending goes on it exactly the same way.

items.fr: Tu t'es couché tard.
items.en: You went to bed late.
items.ipa: /ty tɛ ku.ʃe taʁ/
items.respell: tü teh koo-SHAY TAR
items.notes: Fifteen letters, and the elided little word in a sentence with nothing else going on.

items.fr: est-ce que vous pourriez
items.en: would you be able to
items.ipa: /ɛs kə vu pu.ʁje/
items.respell: es kuh voo poo-RYAY

items.fr: Depuis quand es-tu ici ?
items.en: How long have you been here?
items.ipa: /də.pɥi kɑ̃ ɛ.ty i.si/
items.respell: duh-PWEE KAHⁿ eh-TÜ ee-SEE
items.notes: The question that gets asked, and the reason the scene stalls. Depuis quand is two words and the answer needs a present tense.

items.fr: Je suis ici depuis six mois.
items.en: I have been here for six months.
items.ipa: /ʒə sɥi i.si də.pɥi si mwa/
items.respell: zhuh SWEE ee-SEE duh-PWEE see MWAH
items.notes: The answer to the question above, and the sentence the scene never reached. Être in the present, which is a1.06's and the first verb the learner ever had.

items.fr: On mange dans une heure ?
items.en: Shall we eat in an hour?
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ mɑ̃ʒ dɑ̃.zyn œʁ/
items.respell: ohⁿ MAHⁿZH dAHⁿ zün UHR
items.notes: A point ahead, in the present, and the third of the five in three turns.

items.fr: Oui, je finis en dix minutes.
items.en: Yes, I finish in ten minutes.
items.ipa: /wi ʒə fi.ni ɑ̃ di mi.nyt/
items.respell: wee zhuh fee-NEE AHⁿ dee mee-NÜT
items.notes: And the fourth, in the answer, where the two are one word apart and mean different things. Dans is when she starts eating; en is how long his job takes.

items.fr: Tu pars tôt.
items.en: You leave early.
items.ipa: /ty paʁ to/
items.respell: tü par TOH
items.notes: Same sound again. Only the pronoun separates the three.

items.fr: Il part tôt.
items.en: He leaves early.
items.ipa: /il paʁ to/
items.respell: eel par TOH
items.notes: Put this beside Il finit tôt from the last lesson. Both stop dead.

items.fr: Ils partent tôt.
items.en: They leave early.
items.ipa: /il paʁt to/
items.respell: eel part TOH
items.notes: One consonant more than Il part tôt, at the very end. That T is the whole difference.

items.fr: Nous partons tôt.
items.en: We leave early.
items.ipa: /nu paʁ.tɔ̃ to/
items.respell: noo par-tohⁿ TOH
items.notes: The t is back and it brings a whole syllable with it.

items.fr: Vous partez tôt.
items.en: You leave early.
items.ipa: /vu paʁ.te to/
items.respell: voo par-tay TOH
items.notes: The same t, the same extra syllable. Only the singular ever drops it.

items.fr: Tu couvres tout.
items.en: You cover everything.
items.ipa: /ty kuvʁ tu/
items.respell: tü koovr TOO
items.notes: An -es ending. Silent, and only tu takes it.

items.fr: Ils courent vite.
items.en: They run fast.
items.ipa: /il kuʁ vit/
items.respell: eel koor VEET
items.notes: The same sound as Il court vite. courir sheds nothing, so it has nothing to give back.

items.fr: Je dors bien ici.
items.en: I sleep well here.
items.ipa: /ʒə dɔʁ bjɛ̃ i.si/
items.respell: zhuh dor byaⁿ ee-SEE

items.fr: Ils dorment encore.
items.en: They are still asleep.
items.ipa: /il dɔʁm ɑ̃.kɔʁ/
items.respell: eel dorm ahⁿ-KOR
items.notes: The m of the stem comes back, and it is the only thing saying more than one.

items.fr: Nous sortons ce soir.
items.en: We are going out tonight.
items.ipa: /nu sɔʁ.tɔ̃ sə swaʁ/
items.respell: noo sor-tohⁿ suh SWAR

items.fr: Vous servez le dîner ?
items.en: Are you serving dinner?
items.ipa: /vu sɛʁ.ve lə di.ne/
items.respell: voo sehr-vay luh dee-NAY

items.fr: On ment rarement ici.
items.en: People rarely lie here.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ mɑ̃ ʁaʁ.mɑ̃ i.si/
items.respell: ohⁿ mahⁿ rar-mahⁿ ee-SEE
items.notes: on takes the il form, so the t stays away even though on means we.

items.fr: Ils offrent un cadeau.
items.en: They are giving a present.
items.ipa: /il.zɔfʁ œ̃ ka.do/
items.respell: eel-zofr uhⁿ ka-DOH
items.notes: The verb sounds the same as il offre. The z in front of it is what says several.

items.fr: Tu découvres la ville.
items.en: You are discovering the city.
items.ipa: /ty de.kuvʁ la vil/
items.respell: tü day-koovr la VEEL

items.fr: On souffre en silence.
items.en: People suffer in silence.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ sufʁ ɑ̃ si.lɑ̃s/
items.respell: ohⁿ soofr ahⁿ see-LAHⁿS

items.fr: sentir
items.en: to smell, to feel
items.ipa: /sɑ̃tiʁ/
items.respell: sahⁿ-TEER
items.notes: irregular · je sens, tu sens, il sent

items.fr: mentir
items.en: to lie
items.ipa: /mɑ̃tiʁ/
items.respell: mahⁿ-TEER
items.notes: Irregular; conjugates like partir.

items.fr: Vous réglez comment ?

items.ipa: /vu ʁe.ɡle kɔ.mɑ̃/

items.respell: ahⁿ-SAHⁿBL oo say-pa-ray-MAHⁿ

items.respell: luh sehr-VEESS eh kohⁿ-PREE

items.respell: bon swa-RAY mehr-SEE duh votr vee-ZEET
items.notes: The close. The encounter has an end, and it is better to leave than to hover.

items.fr: Ils devraient arriver vers huit heures.
items.en: They should arrive around eight.
items.ipa: /il də.vʁɛ.ta.ʁi.ve vɛʁ ɥi.tœʁ/
items.respell: eel duh-vreh-tah-ree-vay vehr wee-TUHR

items.en: You should not worry.
items.ipa: /ty nə də.vʁɛ pa tɛ̃.kje.te/
items.respell: tü nuh duh-vreh pah tehⁿ-kyay-TAY

items.fr: Nous partageons une pizza.
items.en: We are sharing a pizza.
items.ipa: /nu paʁ.ta.ʒɔ̃ yn pid.za/
items.respell: noo par-tah-ZHOHⁿ ün peed-ZA

items.ipa: /ʒɛs.pɛʁ a.ʁi.ve a.vɑ̃ mi.di/
items.respell: zhes-PEHR a-ree-vay a-vahⁿ mee-DEE
items.notes: j espère, and the verb after it stays in the naming form, which is lesson 1 in A2 territory.

items.en: You shop at the market.
items.ipa: /vu.zaʃ.te o maʁ.ʃe/
items.respell: voo zahsh-TAY o mar-SHAY
items.notes: vous keeps the plain stem, exactly like nous. Two of the six cells never move.

items.en: We finish at six.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ fi.ni a si zœʁ/
items.respell: ohⁿ fee-nee a see-ZEUR

items.en: I would not be able to come before six.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə pu.ʁɛ pa və.niʁ a.vɑ̃ si.zœʁ/
items.respell: zhuh nuh poo-reh pah vuh-neer ah-vahⁿ see-ZUHR

items.ipa: /a.vɛ.kœ̃ pø ply də plas ɔ̃ sə.ʁɛ tʁɛ bjɛ̃ i.si/
items.respell: ah-veh-kuhⁿ puh plü duh plas ohⁿ suh-reh treh byehⁿ ee-SEE

items.respell: noo na-VOHⁿ plü duh so-MOHⁿ suh SWAR
items.notes: The same deviation without the pronouns, so the learner has a version they can parse. plus de is the lesson 8 in A1 reduction under negation, quoted as recall, not retaught.

items.fr: Je vais prendre le plat du jour.
items.en: I'll have the dish of the day.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ pʁɑ̃dʁ lə pla dy ʒuʁ/
items.respell: zhuh veh PRAHⁿDR luh pla dü ZHOOR
items.notes: The futur proche applied to ordering: je vais prendre.

items.respell: suh suh-ra TOO poor MWA mehr-SEE
items.notes: Your answer to the waiter's Ce sera tout ?

items.en: We'll have two set menus.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ va pʁɑ̃dʁ dø mə.ny/
items.respell: ohⁿ va PRAHⁿDR deu muh-NÜ
items.notes: Ordering for the table, and on rather than nous, which is what French actually says.

items.fr: C'est à quel nom ?
items.en: What name is it under?
items.ipa: /sɛ.t‿a kɛl nɔ̃/
items.respell: seh-t a kehl NOHⁿ
items.notes: OFF SCRIPT. Only ever asked if you said you had booked, so it belongs to no stage of a walk-in. Four words and the answer is your surname, which is the one word a learner is least ready to say aloud in French.

items.fr: Selon la police, le suspect serait en fuite.

items.ipa: /da.pʁɛ lə ʒuʁ.nal ly.zin fɛʁ.mə.ʁɛ ɑ̃ ʒɥɛ̃/
items.respell: dah-preh luh zhoor-nal lü-zeen fehr-muh-reh ahⁿ ZHWEHⁿ

items.fr: Le maire aurait une autre solution.
items.en: The mayor reportedly has another solution.
items.ipa: /lə mɛ.ʁo.ʁɛ y.no.tʁə sɔ.ly.sjɔ̃/
items.respell: luh meh-roh-reh ü-noh-truh soh-lü-SYOHⁿ

items.fr: Attention, c'est très chaud.
items.en: Careful, it's very hot.
items.ipa: /a.tɑ̃.sjɔ̃ sɛ tʁɛ ʃo/
items.respell: a-tahⁿ-SYOHⁿ seh treh SHOH
items.notes: OFF SCRIPT. A warning, and nothing is being asked. A learner running the script hears a question in it and answers oui, which is how you burn your hand.

items.fr: Il vous faut autre chose ?
items.en: Do you need anything else?
items.ipa: /il vu fo otʁ ʃoz/
items.respell: eel voo FOH otr SHOHZ
items.notes: OFF SCRIPT, and it looks like stage 6 without being it: this is asked mid-meal about bread or water, not about a dessert you might buy.

items.fr: Ils battent Paul.
items.en: They beat Paul.
items.ipa: /il bat pɔl/
items.respell: eel BAT POL
items.notes: Silent -ent, audible t. If you can hear this one you can hear ils mettent, which is the same trick.

items.fr: Non, je ne le connais pas.
items.en: No, I do not know him.
items.ipa: /nɔ̃ ʒə nə lə kɔ.nɛ pa/
items.respell: nohⁿ, zhuh nuh luh koh-neh PAH

items.fr: Tu me dois de l'argent.
items.en: You owe me money.
items.ipa: /ty mə dwa də laʁ.ʒɑ̃/
items.respell: tü muh DWAH duh lar-ZHAHⁿ
items.notes: The same verb with no second verb after it. Here it means owe, and that is the whole of what to know for now.

items.fr: Je dois acheter du pain.
items.en: I have to buy some bread.
items.ipa: /ʒə dwa aʃ.te dy pɛ̃/
items.respell: zhuh DWAH ahsh-TAY dü PAⁿ
items.notes: acheter was never taught here. It came from somewhere else and the modal did not care.

items.fr: Tu peux m'aider ?
items.en: Can you help me?
items.ipa: /ty pø mɛ.de/
items.respell: tü PUH meh-DAY
items.notes: Four words, and it works in a shop, a station and a doorway.

items.fr: Donne-moi le dossier.
items.en: Give me the file.
items.ipa: /dɔn.mwa lə dɔ.sje/
items.respell: donn-mwah luh doh-SYAY

items.fr: Nous devons attendre le bus.
items.en: We have to wait for the bus.
items.ipa: /nu də.vɔ̃ a.tɑ̃dʁ lə bys/
items.respell: noo duh-VOHⁿ ah-TAHⁿ-druh luh BÜS
items.notes: attendre is an -RE verb from lesson 4 in A2 and it does not conjugate here. After a modal, nothing does.

items.fr: Vous voulez choisir ?
items.en: Would you like to choose?
items.ipa: /vu vu.le ʃwa.ziʁ/
items.respell: voo voo-LAY shwa-ZEER
items.notes: choisir is an -IR verb from lesson 3 in A2, and it arrives here in its dictionary shape.

items.fr: Je bats Paul.
items.en: I beat Paul.
items.ipa: /ʒə ba pɔl/
items.respell: zhuh BA POL
items.notes: One t, silent s. Exactly the shape mettre has, on a verb you met a minute ago.

items.fr: Il bat Paul.
items.en: He beats Paul.
items.ipa: /il ba pɔl/
items.respell: eel BA POL
items.notes: Three letters, and the same sound as the je form. Nothing to learn that mettre did not give you.

items.fr: Nous battons Paul.
items.en: We beat Paul.
items.ipa: /nu ba.tɔ̃ pɔl/
items.respell: noo ba-TOHⁿ POL
items.notes: Two t from here on, and they do not move again. Read it beside nous mettons and nothing is new.

items.fr: J'apprends le français.
items.en: I am learning French.
items.ipa: /ʒa.pʁɑ̃ lə fʁɑ̃.sɛ/
items.respell: zha-PRAHⁿ luh frahⁿ-SEH
items.notes: prends with two letters in front of it. The verb did not change at all.

items.fr: Nous apprenons le français.
items.en: We are learning French.
items.ipa: /nu.za.pʁə.nɔ̃ lə fʁɑ̃.sɛ/
items.respell: noo-za-pruh-NOHⁿ luh frahⁿ-SEH
items.notes: One n, same as nous prenons. The stem does what the head verb does and asks for nothing new.

items.fr: Ils apprennent le français.
items.en: They are learning French.
items.ipa: /il.za.pʁɛn lə fʁɑ̃.sɛ/
items.respell: eel-za-PREN luh frahⁿ-SEH
items.notes: Two n, same as ils prennent, and for the same reason: the -ent has no sound in it.

items.fr: Je comprends la question.
items.en: I understand the question.
items.ipa: /ʒə kɔ̃.pʁɑ̃ la kɛs.tjɔ̃/
items.respell: zhuh kohⁿ-PRAHⁿ la kes-TYOHⁿ
items.notes: A different front and the same verb behind it. Four letters added and nothing else touched.

items.fr: Nous comprenons la question.
items.en: We understand the question.
items.ipa: /nu kɔ̃.pʁə.nɔ̃ la kɛs.tjɔ̃/
items.respell: noo kohⁿ-pruh-NOHⁿ la kes-TYOHⁿ
items.notes: One n. If you can build nous prenons you have already built this one.

items.fr: Tu réponds vite.
items.en: You answer quickly.
items.ipa: /ty ʁe.pɔ̃ vit/
items.respell: tü ray-pohⁿ VEET
items.notes: Spelled exactly like the je form and said exactly like it too.

items.fr: Il répond vite.
items.en: He answers quickly.
items.ipa: /il ʁe.pɔ̃ vit/
items.respell: eel ray-pohⁿ VEET
items.notes: One letter shorter than the other two and said the same way. The bare form on a second verb.

items.fr: Elle attend le bus.
items.en: She is waiting for the bus.
items.ipa: /ɛ.la.tɑ̃ lə bys/
items.respell: e la-tahⁿ luh BÜS
items.notes: The bare form again, and the l of elle moves across onto the verb because attendre begins with a vowel.

items.fr: Ils attendent le bus.
items.en: They are waiting for the bus.
items.ipa: /il.za.tɑ̃d lə bys/
items.respell: eel za-tahⁿd luh BÜS
items.notes: The silent s of ils wakes up in front of the vowel, and the d wakes up in front of the -ent.

items.fr: Il entend le train.
items.en: He can hear the train.
items.ipa: /i.lɑ̃.tɑ̃ lə tʁɛ̃/
items.respell: ee lahⁿ-tahⁿ luh TRAⁿ
items.notes: Three nasal vowels and not one N sound in the whole sentence.

items.fr: Ils entendent le train.
items.en: They can hear the train.
items.ipa: /il.zɑ̃.tɑ̃d lə tʁɛ̃/
items.respell: eel zahⁿ-tahⁿd luh TRAⁿ

items.fr: Elle rend le livre.
items.en: She is giving the book back.
items.ipa: /ɛl ʁɑ̃ lə livʁ/
items.respell: el rahⁿ luh LEEVR

items.fr: Elles rendent le livre.
items.en: They are giving the book back.
items.ipa: /ɛl ʁɑ̃d lə livʁ/
items.respell: el rahⁿd luh LEEVR
items.notes: elle and elles are one sound, so the d at the end of the verb is the only evidence there is.

items.fr: Tu appelles Marie.
items.en: You are calling Marie.
items.ipa: /ty a.pɛl ma.ʁi/
items.respell: tü ah-PEL ma-REE
items.notes: Two l. The doubled consonant is how -eler writes the open è.

items.fr: ralentir
items.en: to slow down
items.ipa: /ʁa.lɑ̃.tiʁ/
items.respell: rah-lahⁿ-TEER

items.fr: grandir
items.en: to grow up
items.ipa: gʁɑ̃.diʁ
items.respell: grahⁿ-DEER

example.en: Children grow up fast.
example.fr: Les enfants grandissent vite.

items.fr: guérir
items.en: to heal, to recover
items.ipa: ge.ʁiʁ
items.respell: gay-REER

example.en: He recovered quickly from his flu.
example.fr: Il a guéri rapidement de sa grippe.

items.fr: Nous les invitons.
items.en: We invite them.
items.ipa: /nu le zɛ̃.vi.tɔ̃/
items.respell: noo lay zaⁿ-vee-TOHⁿ
items.notes: The liaison on les is audible before the vowel of invitons.

items.fr: Elle la connaît.
items.en: She knows her.
items.ipa: /ɛl la kɔ.nɛ/
items.respell: ehl lah koh-NEH
items.notes: Feminine subject and feminine pronoun, and they have nothing to do with each other. The pronoun takes the gender of the noun it stands for.

items.fr: Vous le voyez.
items.en: You see it.
items.ipa: /vu lə vwa.je/
items.respell: voo luh vwah-YAY
items.notes: The vous cell. Nothing about the pronoun responds to the subject changing.

items.fr: montrer
items.en: to show
items.ipa: /mɔ̃tʁe/
items.respell: mohⁿ-TRAY
items.notes: regular -er verb

items.fr: Ils répètent la phrase.
items.en: They repeat the sentence.
items.ipa: /il ʁe.pɛt la fʁaz/
items.respell: eel ray-PET la FRAZ
items.notes: The -ent is four letters and no sound, so the stem is the last thing heard and the vowel opens.

items.fr: Nous répétons la phrase.
items.en: We repeat the sentence.
items.ipa: /nu ʁe.pe.tɔ̃ la fʁaz/
items.respell: noo ray-pay-TOHⁿ la FRAZ
items.notes: Same verb, audible ending, closed vowel. The rule is about the ending, not about the verb.

items.fr: Nous appelons Marie.
items.en: We are calling Marie.
items.ipa: /nu.za.plɔ̃ ma.ʁi/
items.respell: noo zah-PLOHⁿ ma-REE
items.notes: One l. The ending sounds, so the stem goes back to the spelling the infinitive had.

items.fr: Tu achètes du pain.
items.en: You buy bread.
items.ipa: /ty a.ʃɛt dy pɛ̃/
items.respell: tü ah-SHET dü PAⁿ
items.notes: Same shape of infinitive as appeler, same open è, and an accent instead of a doubled letter.

items.fr: il faudrait
items.en: it would need, we should
items.ipa: /il fo.dʁɛ/
items.respell: eel foh-DREH

items.fr: Il parle ici.
items.en: He speaks here.
items.ipa: /il paʁl i.si/
items.respell: eel parl ee-SEE
items.notes: The -ER third person, from lesson 1 in A2. One letter after the stem, and it is silent.

items.fr: Nous vendons ici.
items.en: We sell here.
items.ipa: /nu vɑ̃.dɔ̃ i.si/
items.respell: noo vahⁿ-dohⁿ ee-SEE
items.notes: The same -ons as lesson 1 in A2 and lesson 3 in A2, and the d in front of it is said. Out loud most rooms say on vend instead.

items.fr: Vous vendez ici.
items.en: You sell here.
items.ipa: /vu vɑ̃.de i.si/
items.respell: voo vahⁿ-day ee-SEE
items.notes: The same -ez, and the d is said in front of it as well.

items.fr: Ils vendent ici.
items.en: They sell here.
items.ipa: /il vɑ̃d i.si/
items.respell: eel vahⁿd ee-SEE
items.notes: The -ent is silent and the d in front of it is not, so this is the one plural you can hear against Il vend ici.

items.fr: J'ai couru vite.
items.en: I ran fast.
items.ipa: /ʒe ku.ʁy vit/
items.respell: ZHAY koo-RÜ VEET
items.notes: AN -IR VERB WHOSE PAST FORM IS NOT -i. Lesson 16 in A2 taught -IR to -i and courir is one of the verbs that refuses it.

items.fr: Vous venez souvent ici ?
items.en: Do you come here often?
items.ipa: /vu və.ne su.vɑ̃ i.si/
items.respell: voo vuh-NAY soo-VAHⁿ ee-SEE
items.notes: Her question, and every word in it is one you have had since a1.

items.fr: Oui, je mange souvent ici.
items.en: Yes, I often eat here.
items.ipa: /wi ʒə mɑ̃ʒ su.vɑ̃ i.si/
items.respell: wee zhuh MAHⁿZH soo-VAHⁿ ee-SEE
items.notes: Five words, all of them yours, and the only difficulty was which order they go in.

items.fr: évidemment
items.en: obviously
items.ipa: e.vi.da.mɑ̃
items.respell: ay-vee-da-MAHⁿ
items.notes: évident; -emment is pronounced like -amment

items.fr: constamment
items.en: constantly
items.ipa: kɔ̃s.ta.mɑ̃
items.respell: kohⁿs-ta-MAHⁿ
items.notes: constant + -amment

items.fr: Au Québec, les taxes s'ajoutent à la caisse.
items.en: In Quebec, the taxes are added at the till.
items.ipa: /o ke.bɛk le taks sa.ʒut a la kɛs/
items.respell: oh kay-BEK lay taks sa-ZHOOT a lah KESS
items.notes: The number on the shelf is not the number you pay. No rate is named and no sum is ever asked for.

items.fr: Non, je ne vais pas venir.
items.en: No, I am not going to come.
items.ipa: /nɔ̃ ʒə nə vɛ pa və.niʁ/
items.respell: nohⁿ zhuh nuh veh pah vuh-NEER
items.notes: The refusal, in full, which is the sentence the scene never reached.

items.fr: Ils ne vont pas venir à la fête.
items.en: They aren't going to come to the party.
items.ipa: /il nə vɔ̃ pa və.niʁ a la fɛt/
items.respell: eel nuh vohⁿ pah vuh-NEER a la FEHT
items.notes: Vont is easy to confuse with on or ont by sound, so check the subject ils carefully.

items.fr: Ils ont mangé au restaurant.
items.en: They ate at the restaurant.
items.ipa: /il zɔ̃ mɑ̃.ʒe o ʁɛs.to.ʁɑ̃/
items.respell: eel zohⁿ mahⁿ-ZHAY oh res-toh-RAHⁿ

items.fr: C'est plutôt une douleur sourde.
items.en: It is more of a dull ache.
items.ipa: /sɛ ply.to yn du.lœʁ suʁd/
items.respell: seh plü-TOH ün doo-leur SOORD
items.notes: The answer to ça vous lance ou ça vous brûle ? when neither is right. Plutôt is the hedge that makes an approximate answer acceptable.

items.fr: Ça fait mal ici.
items.en: It hurts here.
items.ipa: /sa fɛ mal i.si/
items.respell: sa feh mal ee-SEE
items.notes: Four words and a finger. It is the answer to montrez-moi où ça fait mal and it needs no body-part noun at all.

items.fr: Vous pourriez parler un peu plus fort ?
items.en: Could you speak a little louder?
items.ipa: /vu pu.ʁje paʁ.le œ̃ pø ply fɔʁ/
items.respell: voo poo-ryay par-lay uhⁿ puh plü FOR

items.fr: Non, nous n'avons pas fini.
items.en: No, we have not finished.
items.ipa: /nɔ̃ nu na.vɔ̃ pa fi.ni/
items.respell: nohⁿ · noo na-vohⁿ pa fee-NEE
items.notes: The nous negative, where the ne shortens and takes the liaison with it. Twenty letters, so it is not a dictée target.

items.fr: J'ai couvert le plat.
items.en: I covered the dish.
items.ipa: /ʒe ku.vɛʁ lə pla/
items.respell: ZHAY koo-VEHR luh PLA
items.notes: Ouvert with a c on the front, and the corpus publishes it as a weather word meaning "overcast".

items.fr: J'ai beaucoup souffert.
items.en: I suffered a lot.
items.ipa: /ʒe bo.ku su.fɛʁ/
items.respell: ZHAY boh-KOO soo-FEHR
items.notes: The fourth and last member, with lesson 16 in A2's adverb sitting in the gap where that lesson put it.

items.fr: J'ai été malade.
items.en: I was ill.
items.ipa: /ʒe e.te ma.lad/
items.respell: ZHAY ay-TAY ma-LAD
items.notes: From nowhere. There is no route from être to été, and the same three letters are also the word for summer.

items.fr: J'ai eu peur.
items.en: I was frightened.
items.ipa: /ʒe y pœʁ/
items.respell: ZHAY Ü PUHR
items.notes: NINE LETTERS AND THE HARDEST TWO IN THE LESSON. Eu is one sound, it is not the sound either letter suggests, and a dropped letter survives a fold so the dictée CAN test it.

items.fr: Il est né ici.
items.en: He was born here.
items.ipa: /il ɛ ne i.si/
items.respell: eel eh NAY ee-SEE
items.notes: Shorter than the verb it comes from, which nothing else in the set is. Masculine singular, deliberately: agreement is lesson 18's and no row here shows one.

items.fr: J’ai sorti la poubelle.
items.en: I took the bin out.
items.ipa: /ʒe sɔʁ.ti la pu.bɛl/
items.respell: zhay sor-TEE lah poo-BELL

items.fr: Elle est passée devant la gare.
items.en: She went past the station.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ pɑ.se də.vɑ̃ la ɡaʁ/
items.respell: ehl eh pah-SAY duh-VAHⁿ lah GAHR

items.fr: Elle a passé un examen.
items.en: She took an exam.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pɑ.se œ̃ nɛɡ.za.mɛ̃/
items.respell: ehl ah pah-SAY uhⁿ neg-zah-MEHⁿ

items.fr: Ils sont morts en mars.
items.en: They died in March.
items.ipa: /il sɔ̃ mɔʁ ɑ̃ maʁs/
items.respell: eel sohⁿ MOR ahⁿ MARSS

items.fr: Elle est née ici.
items.en: She was born here.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ ne i.si/
items.respell: ehl eh NAY ee-SEE

items.fr: pendant deux heures
items.en: for two hours
items.ipa: /pɑ̃.dɑ̃ dø zœʁ/
items.respell: pahⁿ-DAHⁿ duh ZUHR
items.notes: Pendant answers how long something lasted. Its partner depuis deux heures answers since when.

items.fr: depuis trois ans
items.en: for three years
items.ipa: /də.pɥi tʁwa.zɑ̃/
items.respell: duh-PWEE trwah-ZAHⁿ
items.notes: The liaison carries the s of trois onto ans and the nasal survives it.

items.fr: dans dix minutes
items.en: in ten minutes
items.ipa: /dɑ̃ di mi.nyt/
items.respell: dAHⁿ dee mee-NÜT
items.notes: A point ahead, and the present tense goes in front of it.

items.fr: il y a trois jours
items.en: three days ago
items.ipa: /il i a tʁwa ʒuʁ/
items.respell: EEL EE AH trwah ZHOOR

items.fr: Tu es ici depuis longtemps ?
items.en: Have you been here long?
items.ipa: /ty ɛ i.si də.pɥi lɔ̃.tɑ̃/
items.respell: tü eh ee-SEE duh-PWEE lohⁿ-TAHⁿ
items.notes: Her question, and every word in it is one the learner has had since a1.

items.fr: Il pleut pendant deux heures.
items.en: It rains for two hours.
items.ipa: /il plø pɑ̃.dɑ̃ dø zœʁ/
items.respell: eel PLEU pahⁿ-DAHⁿ duh ZUHR
items.notes: The same weather as row 177 and the other word, so the pair differs by one thing. Here the rain stops.

items.fr: en deux heures
items.en: in two hours, that is how long it took
items.ipa: /ɑ̃ dø zœʁ/
items.respell: AHⁿ duh ZUHR
items.notes: Twelve letters, and the shortest thing in the lesson. Same two hours as pendant and depuis, and a third answer.

items.fr: Le film commence dans une heure.
items.en: The film starts in an hour.
items.ipa: /lə film kɔ.mɑ̃s dɑ̃.zyn œʁ/
items.respell: luh FEELM ko-MAHⁿS dAHⁿ zün UHR
items.notes: Something on a timetable, which is where dans lives. The present tense is doing future work and nobody has to be told.

items.fr: Euh... six mois.
items.en: Uh... six months.
items.ipa: /ø si mwa/
items.respell: EU · see MWAH
items.notes: What he says. It is not wrong and it is not a sentence, and the pause in front of it is the whole cost of the lesson.

items.fr: Ah, tu es ici depuis six mois. Et avant ?
items.en: Ah, you have been here for six months. And before that?
items.ipa: /a ty ɛ i.si də.pɥi si mwa e a.vɑ̃/
items.respell: ah tü eh ee-SEE duh-PWEE see MWAH · ay a-VAHⁿ
items.notes: She says his sentence back to him, correctly, without noticing she has done it, and moves on. Nobody corrected anything, so nothing was learned.

items.fr: Tu travailles ici depuis quand ?
items.en: How long have you been working here?
items.ipa: /ty tʁa.vaj i.si də.pɥi kɑ̃/
items.respell: tü tra-VAY ee-SEE duh-PWEE KAHⁿ
items.notes: Depuis quand at the end, which is where a French speaker actually puts it in conversation.

items.fr: Depuis deux ans. Et toi ?
items.en: For two years. And you?
items.ipa: /də.pɥi dø.zɑ̃ e twa/
items.respell: duh-PWEE duh-ZAHⁿ · ay TWAH
items.notes: The answer with no verb in it, which is what people say, and the question straight back.

items.fr: Je voudrais juste vérifier une chose.
items.en: I would just like to check one thing.
items.ipa: /ʒə vu.dʁɛ ʒyst ve.ʁi.fje yn ʃoz/
items.respell: zhuh voo-dreh zhüst vay-ree-fyay ün SHOHZ

items.fr: Nous nous reposons le soir.
items.en: We rest in the evening.
items.ipa: /nu nu ʁə.po.zɔ̃ lə swaʁ/
items.respell: noo noo ruh-poh-ZOHⁿ luh SWAHR
items.notes: se reposer, and the time expression is a1.25s.

items.fr: Je m'habille vite.
items.en: I get dressed quickly.
items.ipa: /ʒə ma.bij vit/
items.respell: zhuh mah-BEEY VEET
items.notes: THE PRONOUN ELIDES. me becomes m before a vowel, which is sons.07s rule arriving on a word the learner now has to choose.

items.fr: Ils s'habillent vite.
items.en: They get dressed quickly.
items.ipa: /il sa.bij vit/
items.respell: eel sah-BEEY VEET
items.notes: And se becomes s. The same rule, and it is the only thing the pronoun ever does besides change.

items.fr: Tu te réveilles tard.
items.en: You wake up late.
items.ipa: /ty tə ʁe.vɛj taʁ/
items.respell: tü tuh ray-VEY TAR
items.notes: se réveiller, and lesson 28 in A1 taught the je cell of it as a whole phrase.

items.fr: Je me réveille à six heures.
items.en: I wake up at six.
items.ipa: /ʒə mə ʁe.vɛj a si zœʁ/
items.respell: zhuh muh ray-VEY ah see ZUHR
items.notes: Role play turn 1.

items.fr: Je me douche et je m'habille.
items.en: I shower and get dressed.
items.ipa: /ʒə mə duʃ e ʒə ma.bij/
items.respell: zhuh muh DOOSH ay zhuh mah-BEEY
items.notes: Role play turn 2. Two pronominal verbs in one sentence, one of them elided. Lesson 28 in A1 ships the same shape.

items.fr: Nous nous levons à la même heure.
items.en: We get up at the same time.
items.ipa: /nu nu lə.vɔ̃ a la mɛm œʁ/
items.respell: noo noo luh-VOHⁿ ah lah mem UHR
items.notes: Role play turn 3. The doubled form produced rather than read.

items.fr: Non, je ne me couche pas tard.
items.en: No, I do not go to bed late.
items.ipa: /nɔ̃ ʒə nə mə kuʃ pa taʁ/
items.respell: nohⁿ, zhuh nuh muh koosh pah TAR
items.notes: Role play turn 4. The negative, on a verb the paradigm never carried.

items.fr: Ils se dépêchent le matin.
items.en: They hurry in the morning.
items.ipa: /il sə de.pɛʃ lə ma.tɛ̃/
items.respell: eel suh day-PESH luh mah-TAHⁿ
items.notes: Role play turn 5, and it is one of the ones that is not reflexive at all.

items.fr: J'ai couché les enfants.
items.en: I put the children to bed.
items.ipa: /ʒe ku.ʃe le zɑ̃.fɑ̃/
items.respell: zhay koo-SHAY lay zahⁿ-FAHⁿ
items.notes: Second pair, and coucher without the little word means putting somebody else to bed.

items.fr: Je me suis couché.
items.en: I went to bed.
items.ipa: /ʒə mə sɥi ku.ʃe/
items.respell: zhuh muh swee koo-SHAY
items.notes: And it flips again, on a verb where nobody would guess it from the meaning.

items.fr: J'ai réveillé mon frère.
items.en: I woke my brother up.
items.ipa: /ʒe ʁe.vɛ.je mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ/
items.respell: zhay ray-veh-YAY mohⁿ FREHR
items.notes: Third pair. Waking somebody else is avoir and it names who.

items.fr: Elle s'est lavé les mains.
items.en: She washed her hands.
items.ipa: /ɛl sɛ la.ve le mɛ̃/
items.respell: ehl seh lah-VAY lay MAHⁿ
items.notes: NAMED, NOT TAUGHT. Something is named after the second word and the ending goes. The reason is a2.24s. Receptive drills only: no flashcard, no voiceflash, no dictation.

items.fr: Elle s'est brossé les dents.
items.en: She brushed her teeth.
items.ipa: /ɛl sɛ bʁɔ.se le dɑ̃/
items.respell: ehl seh bro-SAY lay DAHⁿ
items.notes: The second of the two shapes lesson 28 in A1 taught, so the learner meets both in week one. Receptive only, for the same reason.

items.fr: Elle a lavé la voiture.
items.en: She washed the car.
items.ipa: /ɛl a la.ve la vwa.tyʁ/
items.respell: ehl ah lah-VAY lah vwah-TÜR
items.notes: A WOMAN, avoir, AND NOTHING ON THE END. Lesson 18 in A2 taught that and this lesson does not touch it. Set against 792, which is the same woman and the same verb.

items.fr: Il ne s'est pas levé.
items.en: He did not get up.
items.ipa: /il nə sɛ pa lə.ve/
items.respell: eel nuh seh pah luh-VAY
items.notes: The same again in the third person. Fifteen letters, and the dictée runs it against the affirmative.

items.fr: Elle ne s'est pas levée.
items.en: She did not get up.
items.ipa: /ɛl nə sɛ pa lə.ve/
items.respell: ehl nuh seh pah luh-VAY
items.notes: THE ENDING SITS OUTSIDE THE WRAP and goes on exactly as it would without one. Eighteen letters, so it is not dictated.

items.fr: Nous ne nous sommes pas levés.
items.en: We did not get up.
items.ipa: /nu nə nu sɔm pa lə.ve/
items.respell: noo nuh noo somm pah luh-VAY
items.notes: Four little words in a row and nothing shortens. Twenty-four letters, the longest row in the lesson.

items.fr: Elle s'est habillée.
items.en: She got dressed.
items.ipa: /ɛl sɛ ta.bi.je/
items.respell: ehl seh tah-bee-YAY
items.notes: s habiller, built rather than shown, and the ending is on it. Sixteen letters exactly.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes dépêchés.
items.en: We hurried.
items.ipa: /nu nu sɔm de.pɛ.ʃe/
items.respell: noo noo somm day-peh-SHAY
items.notes: Nobody hurries themselves and it takes être anyway, because the little word is there. Lesson 19 in A2 taught that this one means nothing by it.

items.fr: Vous vous êtes reposés.
items.en: You rested.
items.ipa: /vu vu zɛt ʁə.po.ze/
items.respell: voo voo zeht ruh-poh-ZAY
items.notes: The doubled shape on a verb the table never carried, in the past.

items.fr: Ils se sont douchés.
items.en: They showered.
items.ipa: /il sə sɔ̃ du.ʃe/
items.respell: eel suh sohⁿ doo-SHAY
items.notes: Sixteen letters, so the dictée can ask for the plural ending on a verb that was never conjugated on a screen.

items.fr: Je me suis réveillé à sept heures.
items.en: I woke up at seven.
items.ipa: /ʒə mə sɥi ʁe.vɛ.je a sɛ tœʁ/
items.respell: zhuh muh swee ray-veh-YAY ah seh TUHR
items.notes: Role play turn 1.

items.fr: Elle s'est levée.
items.en: She got up.
items.ipa: /ɛl sɛ lə.ve/
items.respell: ehl seh luh-VAY
items.notes: Thirteen letters, and the one the dictée uses to ask for the e on the verb the six-person walk ran on.

items.fr: Ils ne se sont pas levés.
items.en: They did not get up.
items.ipa: /il nə sə sɔ̃ pa lə.ve/
items.respell: eel nuh suh sohⁿ pah luh-VAY
items.notes: The negative goes around être: ne se sont pas levés.

items.fr: On pourrait peut-être en parler lundi.
items.en: We could perhaps talk about it on Monday.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ pu.ʁɛ pø.tɛ.tʁɑ̃ paʁ.le lœ̃.di/
items.respell: ohⁿ poo-reh puh-teh-trahⁿ par-lay luhⁿ-DEE

items.fr: Je pars sans lui.
items.en: I am leaving without him.
items.ipa: /ʒə paʁ sɑ̃ lɥi/
items.respell: zhuh PAR sahⁿ LWEE
items.notes: A second little word in front, so the learner does not read the rule as a fact about avec.

items.fr: Je ne lui parle pas.
items.en: I do not talk to him.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə lɥi paʁl pa/
items.respell: zhuh nuh lwee parl PAH
items.notes: ne outside, pronoun and verb inside, pas after both. Exactly lesson 21 in A2's sentence and no new rule.

items.fr: Je ne leur parle pas.
items.en: I do not talk to them.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə lœʁ paʁl pa/
items.respell: zhuh nuh luhr parl PAH
items.notes: The plural inside the wrap and still no s.

items.fr: Il ne lui répond pas.
items.en: He does not answer her.
items.ipa: /il nə lɥi ʁe.pɔ̃ pa/
items.respell: eel nuh lwee ray-pohⁿ PAH
items.notes: A different subject and a different verb, and nothing about the wrap responds to either.

items.fr: Je ne leur écris pas.
items.en: I do not write to them.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə lœʁ e.kʁi pa/
items.respell: zhuh nuh luhr ay-kree PAH

items.fr: Le plat est froid.
items.en: The dish is cold.
items.ipa: /lə pla ɛ fʁwa/
items.respell: luh PLA eh FRWA
items.notes: Four words and a fact. Deliberately not a complaint LADDER, which is lesson 28 in A2's Owns; this is one statement, said once.

items.fr: C'est pour lui.
items.en: It is for him.
items.ipa: /sɛ puʁ lɥi/
items.respell: seh poor LWEE
items.notes: Eleven letters, and a third. Three prepositions and the same behaviour, which is what makes it a rule rather than an idiom.

items.fr: Merci d'avance, ce n'est pas urgent.
items.en: Thanks in advance, it is not urgent.
items.ipa: /mɛʁ.si da.vɑ̃s sə nɛ pa.zyʁ.ʒɑ̃/
items.respell: mer-see dah-vahⁿss suh neh pah-zür-ZHAHⁿ

items.fr: Désolé, je ne voulais pas couper.
items.en: Sorry, I did not mean to interrupt.
items.ipa: /de.zɔ.le ʒə nə vu.lɛ pa ku.pe/
items.respell: day-zoh-lay zhuh nuh voo-leh pah koo-PAY

items.fr: Je suis vraiment désolé de vous déranger encore.
items.en: I am really sorry to bother you again.
items.ipa: /ʒə sɥi vʁɛ.mɑ̃ de.zɔ.le də vu de.ʁɑ̃.ʒe ɑ̃.kɔʁ/
items.respell: zhuh swee vreh-mahⁿ day-zoh-lay duh voo day-rahⁿ-zhay ahⁿ-KOR

items.fr: Attendez-moi ici, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: Wait for me here, please.
items.ipa: /a.tɑ̃.de.mwa i.si sil vu plɛ/
items.respell: ah-tahⁿ-day-mwah ee-see seel voo PLEH

items.fr: Suivez-moi, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: Follow me, please.
items.ipa: /sɥi.ve.mwa sil vu plɛ/
items.respell: swee-vay-mwah seel voo PLEH

items.fr: Je vous fais une seule addition ?
items.en: Shall I make it one bill?
items.ipa: /ʒə vu fɛ yn sœl a.di.sjɔ̃/
items.respell: zhuh voo FEH ün seul a-dee-SYOHⁿ
items.notes: The follow-up to Ensemble ou séparément ?, asked again in different words.

items.fr: Alors qu'est-ce que vous me conseillez ?
items.en: So what do you recommend?
items.ipa: /a.lɔʁ kɛs kə vu mə kɔ̃.sɛ.je/
items.respell: a-LOR kess kuh voo muh kohⁿ-seh-YAY
items.notes: The hand-back. Freeze and you lose the turn; hand the choice back and you keep it.

items.fr: Il manque un plat.
items.en: A dish is missing.
items.ipa: /il mɑ̃k œ̃ pla/
items.respell: eel MAHⁿK uhⁿ PLA
items.notes: A dish is missing. Shorter and easier than Ce n'est pas ce que j'ai commandé.

items.fr: Je suis désolé, il n'y en a plus.
items.en: I'm sorry, there's none left.
items.ipa: /ʒə sɥi de.zɔ.le il njɑ̃.n‿a ply/
items.respell: zhuh süee day-zo-LAY eel nyahⁿ-n a PLÜ
items.notes: THE DEVIATION, and the line the whole of act 4 turns on. UNANALYSED LEXIS: il n'y en a plus contains both y and en, which belong to lesson 23 in A2 (which HAS shipped). It is never glossed, never decomposed, and never in a scored surface that turns on the pronouns. The learner recognises the chunk and reaches for a rung.

items.fr: Voilà pour vous.
items.en: Here you are.
items.ipa: /vwa.la puʁ vu/
items.respell: vwa-LA poor VOO
items.notes: Said on every delivery, at any stage, and it is the single most frequent thing a waiter says. Deliberately not tied to one stage.

items.fr: Excusez-moi pour l'attente.
items.en: Sorry for the wait.
items.ipa: /ɛks.ky.ze mwa puʁ la.tɑ̃t/
items.respell: ehks-kü-zay MWA poor la-TAHⁿT
items.notes: An apology from the other side, which the corpus had none of. The learner has to recognise that nothing is being asked of them.

items.fr: Je crois qu'il y a une erreur sur l'addition.
items.en: I think there's a mistake on the bill.
items.ipa: /ʒə kʁwa kil j‿a yn e.ʁœʁ syʁ la.di.sjɔ̃/
items.respell: zhuh KRWA keel ya ün ay-REUR sür la-dee-SYOHⁿ
items.notes: A problem with the bill rather than with the food.

items.fr: Je vous en prie, prenez votre temps.
items.en: Please do, take your time.
items.ipa: /ʒə vu.zɑ̃ pʁi pʁə.ne vɔtʁ tɑ̃/
items.respell: zhuh voo-zahⁿ pree pruh-nay votr TAHⁿ

items.fr: Ce serait gentil de me le confirmer.
items.en: It would be kind of you to confirm it for me.
items.ipa: /sə sə.ʁɛ ʒɑ̃.ti də mə lə kɔ̃.fiʁ.me/
items.respell: suh suh-reh zhahⁿ-tee duh muh luh kohⁿ-feer-MAY

items.fr: Merci beaucoup, vous me sauvez la journée.
items.en: Thank you very much, you are saving my day.
items.ipa: /mɛʁ.si bo.ku vu mə so.ve la ʒuʁ.ne/
items.respell: mer-see boh-koo voo muh soh-vay lah zhoor-NAY

items.fr: Je vous laisse mon numéro, au cas où.
items.en: I will leave you my number, just in case.
items.ipa: /ʒə vu lɛs mɔ̃ ny.me.ʁo o ka u/
items.respell: zhuh voo less mohⁿ nü-may-roh oh kah OO

items.fr: Je vous le remplace tout de suite.
items.en: I'll replace it for you right away.
items.ipa: /ʒə vu lə ʁɑ̃.plas tu d(ə) sɥit/
items.respell: zhuh voo luh rahⁿ-PLASS too duh SÜEET
items.notes: The repair from his side, and it carries the lesson 21 in A2 direct-object pronoun le in front of the verb. Exposure, not instruction: lesson 21 in A2 shipped at seq 21 and owns it.

items.fr: Je prendrais plutôt le poisson.
items.en: I'd rather have the fish.
items.ipa: /ʒə pʁɑ̃.dʁɛ ply.to lə pwa.sɔ̃/
items.respell: zhuh prahⁿ-DREH plü-TOH luh pwa-SOHⁿ
items.notes: The softest rung, and genuinely new lexis: the conditional of prendre in this use is at 0 restaurant rows. Carried as an unnamed fixed form. The conditional as a FAMILY is lesson 28 in A2's and is not named, conjugated or grouped here.

items.fr: Pour moi, ce sera l'entrecôte.
items.en: For me, it'll be the rib steak.
items.ipa: /puʁ mwa sə sə.ʁa lɑ̃.tʁə.kot/
items.respell: poor MWA suh suh-RA lahⁿ-truh-KOHT
items.notes: The same frame with the person restored, which is how it is said at a table of four.

items.fr: On ferme la cuisine dans dix minutes.
items.en: The kitchen closes in ten minutes.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ fɛʁm la kɥi.zin dɑ̃ di mi.nyt/
items.respell: ohⁿ fehrm la kü-ee-ZEEN dahⁿ dee mee-NÜT
items.notes: OFF SCRIPT. A statement that is really an instruction: order now or do not order. Nothing in it is a question and everything in it is urgent.

items.fr: Je reviens tout de suite.
items.en: I'll be right back.
items.ipa: /ʒə ʁə.vjɛ̃ tu d(ə) sɥit/
items.respell: zhuh ruh-VYEHⁿ too duh SÜEET
items.notes: OFF SCRIPT. He is leaving mid-turn and will finish the exchange later. The learner who does not catch it thinks they have been forgotten.

items.fr: Ça sera sur votre gauche.
items.en: It will be on your left.
items.ipa: /sa sə.ʁa syʁ vɔtʁ ɡoʃ/
items.respell: sa suh-RA sür VOH-truh GOHSH
items.notes: Sur votre gauche, not à gauche: the side of you rather than the direction to turn. The two are one word apart and mean different things.

items.fr: Continuez tout droit, puis tournez à gauche.
items.en: Keep going straight, then turn left.
items.ipa: /kɔ̃.ti.nɥe tu dʁwa pɥi tuʁ.ne a ɡoʃ/
items.respell: kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY too DRWAH pwee toor-NAY ah GOHSH
items.notes: GO then TURN, joined by puis. The cleanest two-move shape there is.

items.fr: Prenez la première à droite, puis traversez la place.
items.en: Take the first on the right, then cross the square.
items.ipa: /pʁə.ne la pʁə.mjɛʁ a dʁwat pɥi tʁa.vɛʁ.se la plas/
items.respell: pruh-NAY lah pruh-MYEHR ah DRWAHT pwee trah-vehr-SAY lah PLAHSS
items.notes: TURN then PASS, with an ordinal inside the first move.

items.fr: Tournez à gauche au feu, ensuite continuez tout droit.
items.en: Turn left at the lights, then keep going straight.
items.ipa: /tuʁ.ne a ɡoʃ o fø ɑ̃.sɥit kɔ̃.ti.nɥe tu dʁwa/
items.respell: toor-NAY ah GOHSH oh FEU ahⁿ-SWEET kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY too DRWAH
items.notes: Ensuite instead of puis. They are interchangeable here and a learner who only knows one loses half the joints.

items.fr: Allez jusqu'au carrefour, puis prenez à droite.
items.en: Go to the crossroads, then turn right.
items.ipa: /a.le ʒys.ko kaʁ.fuʁ pɥi pʁə.ne a dʁwat/
items.respell: ah-LAY zhüs-koh kar-FOOR pwee pruh-NAY ah DRWAHT
items.notes: Jusqu'au inside move one, puis between the two. Two joints, one chain, and only one of them separates moves.

items.fr: Je vais demander en cuisine.
items.en: I'll go and ask in the kitchen.
items.ipa: /ʒə vɛ də.mɑ̃.de ɑ̃ kɥi.zin/
items.respell: zhuh veh duh-mahⁿ-DAY ahⁿ kü-ee-ZEEN
items.notes: It closes the exchange without answering it, which is what actually happens.

items.fr: Traversez le pont, ensuite tournez à gauche.
items.en: Cross the bridge, then turn left.
items.ipa: /tʁa.vɛʁ.se lə pɔ̃ ɑ̃.sɥit tuʁ.ne a ɡoʃ/
items.respell: trah-vehr-SAY luh POHⁿ ahⁿ-SWEET toor-NAY ah GOHSH
items.notes: PASS then TURN. The order matters: crossing first and turning first put you on opposite banks.

items.fr: Remontez la rue, puis prenez la deuxième à droite.
items.en: Go back up the street, then take the second on the right.
items.ipa: /ʁə.mɔ̃.te la ʁy pɥi pʁə.ne la dø.zjɛm a dʁwat/
items.respell: ruh-mohⁿ-TAY lah RÜ pwee pruh-NAY lah deu-ZYEM ah DRWAHT
items.notes: The ordinal sits at the end, unstressed, between two content words. That is where it goes missing.

items.fr: Longez le parc, ensuite traversez la rue.
items.en: Follow the park along, then cross the street.
items.ipa: /lɔ̃.ʒe lə paʁk ɑ̃.sɥit tʁa.vɛʁ.se la ʁy/
items.respell: lohⁿ-ZHAY luh PARK ahⁿ-SWEET trah-vehr-SAY lah RÜ
items.notes: Two PASS moves in a row. Nothing changes heading, which is what makes them easy to collapse into one.

items.fr: Passez devant la poste, puis c'est sur votre droite.
items.en: Go past the post office, then it is on your right.
items.ipa: /pa.se də.vɑ̃ la pɔst pɥi sɛ syʁ vɔtʁ dʁwat/
items.respell: pah-SAY duh-VAHⁿ lah POST pwee seh sür VOH-truh DRWAHT
items.notes: PASS then ARRIVE. Puis in front of an ARRIVE move is the signal the instruction has finished.

items.fr: Continuez jusqu'au rond-point, ensuite prenez la sortie à droite.
items.en: Carry on to the roundabout, then take the right exit.
items.ipa: /kɔ̃.ti.nɥe ʒys.ko ʁɔ̃.pwɛ̃ ɑ̃.sɥit pʁə.ne la sɔʁ.ti a dʁwat/
items.respell: kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY zhüs-koh rohⁿ-PWEHⁿ ahⁿ-SWEET pruh-NAY lah sor-TEE ah DRWAHT
items.notes: Le rond-point is published as a headword in four themes and used in an instruction in none of them.

items.fr: Prenez le boulevard, puis vous verrez la gare.
items.en: Take the boulevard, then you will see the station.
items.ipa: /pʁə.ne lə bul.vaʁ pɥi vu vɛ.ʁe la ɡaʁ/
items.respell: pruh-NAY luh bool-VAR pwee voo veh-RAY lah GAHR
items.notes: GO then ARRIVE, with no TURN at all. A two-move chain does not have to change heading.

items.fr: Tournez à droite après la banque, puis continuez tout droit.
items.en: Turn right after the bank, then keep going straight.
items.ipa: /tuʁ.ne a dʁwat a.pʁɛ la bɑ̃k pɥi kɔ̃.ti.nɥe tu dʁwa/
items.respell: toor-NAY ah DRWAHT ah-PREH lah BAHⁿK pwee kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY too DRWAH
items.notes: Après inside move one and puis between the moves. Two joints of different jobs in one short chain.

items.fr: Allez au bout de la rue, puis tournez à gauche.
items.en: Go to the end of the street, then turn left.
items.ipa: /a.le o bu də la ʁy pɥi tuʁ.ne a ɡoʃ/
items.respell: ah-LAY oh BOO duh lah RÜ pwee toor-NAY ah GOHSH
items.notes: Au bout de is a joint of four words. Heard fast it is one syllable and a learner hears only bout.

items.fr: Traversez la place, ensuite c'est juste en face.
items.en: Cross the square, then it is just opposite.
items.ipa: /tʁa.vɛʁ.se la plas ɑ̃.sɥit sɛ ʒyst ɑ̃ fas/
items.respell: trah-vehr-SAY lah PLAHSS ahⁿ-SWEET seh zhüst ahⁿ FAHSS
items.notes: En face is the preposition en, not the pronoun. Lesson 23 in A2 owns the pronoun and this unit does not touch it.

items.fr: Prenez la deuxième à gauche, puis longez le canal.
items.en: Take the second on the left, then follow the canal.
items.ipa: /pʁə.ne la dø.zjɛm a ɡoʃ pɥi lɔ̃.ʒe lə ka.nal/
items.respell: pruh-NAY lah deu-ZYEM ah GOHSH pwee lohⁿ-ZHAY luh ka-NAL
items.notes: The ordinal and the verb with no English equivalent, in one chain. Both are droppable and dropping either loses the route.

items.fr: Continuez tout droit, tournez à gauche, c'est en face.
items.en: Keep straight, turn left, it is opposite.
items.ipa: /kɔ̃.ti.nɥe tu dʁwa tuʁ.ne a ɡoʃ sɛ.tɑ̃ fas/
items.respell: kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY too DRWAH toor-NAY ah GOHSH seh-tahⁿ FAHSS
items.notes: GO, TURN, ARRIVE with commas doing the joints' work. A comma is a joint you cannot hear, which is the hardest case.

items.fr: Prenez la première à droite, traversez la place, puis continuez.
items.en: Take the first right, cross the square, then carry on.
items.ipa: /pʁə.ne la pʁə.mjɛʁ a dʁwat tʁa.vɛʁ.se la plas pɥi kɔ̃.ti.nɥe/
items.respell: pruh-NAY lah pruh-MYEHR ah DRWAHT trah-vehr-SAY lah PLAHSS pwee kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY
items.notes: One spoken joint and one comma. The learner who counts only puis counts two moves and walks two thirds of the route.

items.fr: Allez jusqu'au feu, tournez à droite, c'est après la pharmacie.
items.en: Go to the lights, turn right, it is after the chemist.
items.ipa: /a.le ʒys.ko fø tuʁ.ne a dʁwat sɛ.ta.pʁɛ la faʁ.ma.si/
items.respell: ah-LAY zhüs-koh FEU toor-NAY ah DRWAHT seh-tah-PREH lah far-mah-SEE
items.notes: Après appears here as part of an ARRIVE move rather than as a joint. The same word does both jobs.

items.fr: Traversez le pont, puis longez le quai jusqu'à la place.
items.en: Cross the bridge, then follow the quay to the square.
items.ipa: /tʁa.vɛʁ.se lə pɔ̃ pɥi lɔ̃.ʒe lə kɛ ʒys.ka la plas/
items.respell: trah-vehr-SAY luh POHⁿ pwee lohⁿ-ZHAY luh KEH zhüs-KA lah PLAHSS
items.notes: Le quai is a station platform at a1 and a riverside here. Same word, and the context is the only thing that separates them.

items.fr: Remontez la rue, prenez la deuxième à gauche, c'est au coin.
items.en: Go up the street, take the second left, it is on the corner.
items.ipa: /ʁə.mɔ̃.te la ʁy pʁə.ne la dø.zjɛm a ɡoʃ sɛ.to kwɛ̃/
items.respell: ruh-mohⁿ-TAY lah RÜ pruh-NAY lah deu-ZYEM ah GOHSH seh-toh KWEHⁿ
items.notes: Three moves, no spoken joint at all. Only the commas separate them and a comma has no sound.

items.fr: Sortez de la gare, tournez à droite, puis continuez tout droit.
items.en: Leave the station, turn right, then keep going straight.
items.ipa: /sɔʁ.te də la ɡaʁ tuʁ.ne a dʁwat pɥi kɔ̃.ti.nɥe tu dʁwa/
items.respell: sor-TAY duh lah GAHR toor-NAY ah DRWAHT pwee kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY too DRWAH
items.notes: The move a learner standing at a station actually needs first, and it is published nowhere.

items.fr: Passez devant la mairie, traversez la place, c'est sur votre gauche.
items.en: Go past the town hall, cross the square, it is on your left.
items.ipa: /pa.se də.vɑ̃ la mɛ.ʁi tʁa.vɛʁ.se la plas sɛ syʁ vɔtʁ ɡoʃ/
items.respell: pah-SAY duh-VAHⁿ lah meh-REE trah-vehr-SAY lah PLAHSS seh sür VOH-truh GOHSH
items.notes: Two PASS moves then ARRIVE. Nothing turns, so a learner listening for a turn hears no instruction at all.

items.fr: Prenez le pont, ensuite la première à droite, puis tout droit.
items.en: Take the bridge, then the first right, then straight on.
items.ipa: /pʁə.ne lə pɔ̃ ɑ̃.sɥit la pʁə.mjɛʁ a dʁwat pɥi tu dʁwa/
items.respell: pruh-NAY luh POHⁿ ahⁿ-SWEET lah pruh-MYEHR ah DRWAHT pwee too DRWAH
items.notes: Moves two and three have no verb in them at all. The joint is carrying the whole move, which is the strongest argument for counting joints.

items.fr: Continuez jusqu'au rond-point, prenez la troisième sortie, c'est en face.
items.en: Carry on to the roundabout, take the third exit, it is opposite.
items.ipa: /kɔ̃.ti.nɥe ʒys.ko ʁɔ̃.pwɛ̃ pʁə.ne la tʁwa.zjɛm sɔʁ.ti sɛ.tɑ̃ fas/
items.respell: kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY zhüs-koh rohⁿ-PWEHⁿ pruh-NAY lah trwah-ZYEM sor-TEE seh-tahⁿ FAHSS
items.notes: The one place an ordinal counts exits rather than streets, and getting it wrong at a roundabout is a whole different road.

items.fr: Longez le parc, tournez à gauche au feu, puis vous verrez.
items.en: Follow the park, turn left at the lights, then you will see it.
items.ipa: /lɔ̃.ʒe lə paʁk tuʁ.ne a ɡoʃ o fø pɥi vu vɛ.ʁe/
items.respell: lohⁿ-ZHAY luh PARK toor-NAY ah GOHSH oh FEU pwee voo veh-RAY
items.notes: Vous verrez as a whole ARRIVE move with no place named. It means you cannot miss it, and it names nothing you can check.

items.fr: Allez tout droit, traversez la rue, c'est juste après la banque.
items.en: Go straight, cross the street, it is just after the bank.
items.ipa: /a.le tu dʁwa tʁa.vɛʁ.se la ʁy sɛ ʒyst a.pʁɛ la bɑ̃k/
items.respell: ah-LAY too DRWAH trah-vehr-SAY lah RÜ seh zhüst ah-PREH lah BAHⁿK
items.notes: Allez rather than continuez for the same GO move. Four verbs mean go and the choice between them carries nothing.

items.fr: Tournez à gauche, continuez jusqu'au bout, c'est le bâtiment gris.
items.en: Turn left, carry on to the end, it is the grey building.
items.ipa: /tuʁ.ne a ɡoʃ kɔ̃.ti.nɥe ʒys.ko bu sɛ lə ba.ti.mɑ̃ ɡʁi/
items.respell: toor-NAY ah GOHSH kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY zhüs-koh BOO seh luh bah-tee-MAHⁿ GREE
items.notes: Jusqu'au bout with no noun after it. The joint has swallowed the landmark, which is normal and unteachable from a word list.

items.fr: Prenez la rue à droite, passez devant l'école, puis tournez à gauche.
items.en: Take the street on the right, pass the school, then turn left.
items.ipa: /pʁə.ne la ʁy a dʁwat pa.se də.vɑ̃ le.kɔl pɥi tuʁ.ne a ɡoʃ/
items.respell: pruh-NAY lah RÜ ah DRWAHT pah-SAY duh-VAHⁿ lay-KOL pwee toor-NAY ah GOHSH
items.notes: TURN, PASS, TURN. Two changes of heading with a landmark between them, and the landmark is not where you stop.

items.fr: Continuez tout droit, tournez à gauche, traversez la place, c'est en face.
items.en: Straight on, turn left, cross the square, it is opposite.
items.ipa: /kɔ̃.ti.nɥe tu dʁwa tuʁ.ne a ɡoʃ tʁa.vɛʁ.se la plas sɛ.tɑ̃ fas/
items.respell: kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY too DRWAH toor-NAY ah GOHSH trah-vehr-SAY lah PLAHSS seh-tahⁿ FAHSS
items.notes: One of each move type, in order, with no spoken joint. Twelve words and four things to hold.

items.fr: Prenez la deuxième à droite, longez le parc, traversez la rue, c'est là.
items.en: Second right, follow the park, cross the street, it is there.
items.ipa: /pʁə.ne la dø.zjɛm a dʁwat lɔ̃.ʒe lə paʁk tʁa.vɛʁ.se la ʁy sɛ la/
items.respell: pruh-NAY lah deu-ZYEM ah DRWAHT lohⁿ-ZHAY luh PARK trah-vehr-SAY lah RÜ seh LAH
items.notes: C'est là as the whole ARRIVE move. It names nothing, and a learner who was still translating move one hears it as filler.

items.fr: Allez jusqu'au feu, tournez à droite, passez le pont, c'est après.
items.en: Go to the lights, turn right, cross the bridge, it is after.
items.ipa: /a.le ʒys.ko fø tuʁ.ne a dʁwat pa.se lə pɔ̃ sɛ.ta.pʁɛ/
items.respell: ah-LAY zhüs-koh FEU toor-NAY ah DRWAHT pah-SAY luh POHⁿ seh-tah-PREH
items.notes: C'est après with nothing after it. The landmark is the bridge you just crossed and the sentence does not say so.

items.fr: Sortez de la gare, tout droit, deuxième à gauche, c'est au coin.
items.en: Out of the station, straight on, second left, on the corner.
items.ipa: /sɔʁ.te də la ɡaʁ tu dʁwa dø.zjɛm a ɡoʃ sɛ.to kwɛ̃/
items.respell: sor-TAY duh lah GAHR too DRWAH deu-ZYEM ah GOHSH seh-toh KWEHⁿ
items.notes: Moves two, three and four have no verb. This is what a hurried passer-by actually says and no word list prepares a learner for it.

items.fr: Traversez la place, remontez la rue, prenez la première à droite, continuez.
items.en: Cross the square, up the street, first right, carry on.
items.ipa: /tʁa.vɛʁ.se la plas ʁə.mɔ̃.te la ʁy pʁə.ne la pʁə.mjɛʁ a dʁwat kɔ̃.ti.nɥe/
items.respell: trah-vehr-SAY lah PLAHSS ruh-mohⁿ-TAY lah RÜ pruh-NAY lah pruh-MYEHR ah DRWAHT kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY
items.notes: Ends on a GO with no destination. The instruction stops before the route does, which is the commonest real shape.

items.fr: Tournez à gauche, allez jusqu'au pont, traversez, c'est sur votre droite.
items.en: Turn left, go to the bridge, cross, it is on your right.
items.ipa: /tuʁ.ne a ɡoʃ a.le ʒys.ko pɔ̃ tʁa.vɛʁ.se sɛ syʁ vɔtʁ dʁwat/
items.respell: toor-NAY ah GOHSH ah-LAY zhüs-koh POHⁿ trah-vehr-SAY seh sür VOH-truh DRWAHT
items.notes: Traversez alone, with no object. The bridge from the move before is what you cross and nothing in the words says it.

items.fr: Prenez le boulevard, puis la troisième à gauche, traversez, c'est en face.
items.en: Take the boulevard, then third left, cross, it is opposite.
items.ipa: /pʁə.ne lə bul.vaʁ pɥi la tʁwa.zjɛm a ɡoʃ tʁa.vɛʁ.se sɛ.tɑ̃ fas/
items.respell: pruh-NAY luh bool-VAR pwee lah trwah-ZYEM ah GOHSH trah-vehr-SAY seh-tahⁿ FAHSS
items.notes: One spoken joint out of three. Counting puis gives you two moves and there are four.

items.fr: Continuez jusqu'au rond-point, deuxième sortie, longez le canal, c'est là.
items.en: On to the roundabout, second exit, follow the canal, it is there.
items.ipa: /kɔ̃.ti.nɥe ʒys.ko ʁɔ̃.pwɛ̃ dø.zjɛm sɔʁ.ti lɔ̃.ʒe lə ka.nal sɛ la/
items.respell: kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY zhüs-koh rohⁿ-PWEHⁿ deu-ZYEM sor-TEE lohⁿ-ZHAY luh ka-NAL seh LAH
items.notes: Deuxième sortie with no verb and no article on sortie. Four moves in eleven words.

items.fr: Descendez ici, traversez la rue, prenez la première à droite, continuez.
items.en: Get off here, cross the street, first right, carry on.
items.ipa: /de.sɑ̃.de i.si tʁa.vɛʁ.se la ʁy pʁə.ne la pʁə.mjɛʁ a dʁwat kɔ̃.ti.nɥe/
items.respell: day-sahⁿ-DAY ee-SEE trah-vehr-SAY lah RÜ pruh-NAY lah pruh-MYEHR ah DRWAHT kohⁿ-tee-nü-AY
items.notes: Said by a driver or another passenger rather than by somebody in the street. Same shape, different speaker.

items.fr: Passez devant l'église, tournez à gauche, allez tout droit, c'est là.
items.en: Past the church, turn left, go straight, it is there.
items.ipa: /pa.se də.vɑ̃ le.ɡliz tuʁ.ne a ɡoʃ a.le tu dʁwa sɛ la/
items.respell: pah-SAY duh-VAHⁿ lay-GLEEZ toor-NAY ah GOHSH ah-LAY too DRWAH seh LAH
items.notes: PASS, TURN, GO, ARRIVE. The landmark comes first here, which is where a learner expects the endpoint.

items.fr: Remontez la rue, traversez le carrefour, première à droite, c'est après.
items.en: Up the street, across the crossroads, first right, it is after.
items.ipa: /ʁə.mɔ̃.te la ʁy tʁa.vɛʁ.se lə kaʁ.fuʁ pʁə.mjɛʁ a dʁwat sɛ.ta.pʁɛ/
items.respell: ruh-mohⁿ-TAY lah RÜ trah-vehr-SAY luh kar-FOOR pruh-MYEHR ah DRWAHT seh-tah-PREH
items.notes: Première with no article at all. Under speed the ordinal is one unstressed syllable between two content words.

items.fr: Allez tout droit, deuxième à gauche, passez la banque, c'est en face.
items.en: Straight on, second left, past the bank, it is opposite.
items.ipa: /a.le tu dʁwa dø.zjɛm a ɡoʃ pa.se la bɑ̃k sɛ.tɑ̃ fas/
items.respell: ah-LAY too DRWAH deu-ZYEM ah GOHSH pah-SAY lah BAHⁿK seh-tahⁿ FAHSS
items.notes: Twelve words, four moves, no joint you can hear. This is the rung-4 shape the trap drill gates on.

items.fr: la deuxième à droite
items.en: the second on the right
items.ipa: /la dø.zjɛm a dʁwat/
items.respell: lah deu-ZYEM ah DRWAHT
items.notes: Two unstressed syllables between la and à. The half of the pair that goes missing.

items.fr: la troisième à droite
items.en: the third on the right
items.ipa: /la tʁwa.zjɛm a dʁwat/
items.respell: lah trwah-ZYEM ah DRWAHT
items.notes: Troisième is longer and survives speed better than deuxième, which is why the confusion runs one way.

items.fr: la deuxième à gauche
items.en: the second on the left
items.ipa: /la dø.zjɛm a ɡoʃ/
items.respell: lah deu-ZYEM ah GOHSH
items.notes: The same ordinal with the other side. Getting the ordinal right and the side wrong is a different street.

items.fr: la première rue à gauche
items.en: the first street on the left
items.ipa: /la pʁə.mjɛʁ ʁy a ɡoʃ/
items.respell: lah pruh-MYEHR RÜ ah GOHSH
items.notes: With rue put back in. The full form is easier and is not what is said in a hurry.

items.fr: Ce n'est pas la première, c'est la deuxième.
items.en: It is not the first, it is the second.
items.ipa: /sə nɛ pa la pʁə.mjɛʁ sɛ la dø.zjɛm/
items.respell: suh neh pah lah pruh-MYEHR seh lah deu-ZYEM
items.notes: A correction, which is what a passer-by says when they see you set off wrong. Negation is lesson 21 in A1's and is used here, not taught.

items.fr: Prenez la troisième, pas la deuxième.
items.en: Take the third, not the second.
items.ipa: /pʁə.ne la tʁwa.zjɛm pa la dø.zjɛm/
items.respell: pruh-NAY lah trwah-ZYEM pah lah deu-ZYEM
items.notes: Both ordinals in one line so the contrast is audible rather than described.

items.fr: C'est la deuxième rue, après le feu.
items.en: It is the second street, after the lights.
items.ipa: /sɛ la dø.zjɛm ʁy a.pʁɛ lə fø/
items.respell: seh lah deu-ZYEM RÜ ah-PREH luh FEU
items.notes: The ordinal is counted from the lights, not from where you stand. Nothing in the sentence says so.

items.fr: Comptez deux rues, puis tournez à droite.
items.en: Count two streets, then turn right.
items.ipa: /kɔ̃.te dø ʁy pɥi tuʁ.ne a dʁwat/
items.respell: kohⁿ-TAY deu RÜ pwee toor-NAY ah DRWAHT
items.notes: A cardinal doing an ordinal's job. Deux rues then turn is the third street, not the second, and that off-by-one is real.

items.fr: Le train à destination de Lyon partira voie douze.
items.en: The train for Lyon will depart from platform twelve.
items.ipa: /lə tʁɛ̃ a dɛs.ti.na.sjɔ̃ də ljɔ̃ paʁ.ti.ʁa vwa duz/
items.respell: luh TREHⁿ ah des-tee-nah-SYOHⁿ duh lee-OHⁿ par-tee-RA vwah DOOZ
items.notes: The canonical shape: destination fronted, then the platform as a bare number. Zero rows in the corpus had it.

items.fr: Le train en provenance de Marseille entre en gare.
items.en: The train from Marseille is arriving.
items.ipa: /lə tʁɛ̃ ɑ̃ pʁɔv.nɑ̃s də maʁ.sɛj ɑ̃tʁ ɑ̃ ɡaʁ/
items.respell: luh TREHⁿ ahⁿ prov-NAHⁿSS duh mar-SEY ahⁿtr ahⁿ GAHR
items.notes: En provenance de is arriving and à destination de is leaving. Four syllables apart and opposite platforms.

items.fr: Attention au départ, voie quatorze.
items.en: Stand clear, departure from platform fourteen.
items.ipa: /a.tɑ̃.sjɔ̃ o de.paʁ vwa ka.tɔʁz/
items.respell: ah-tahⁿ-SYOHⁿ oh day-PAR vwah ka-TORZ
items.notes: The doors-closing warning. Attention here is a warning, not the noun a1 taught.

items.fr: Le train aura un retard d'environ vingt minutes.
items.en: The train will be about twenty minutes late.
items.ipa: /lə tʁɛ̃ o.ʁa œ̃ ʁə.taʁ dɑ̃.vi.ʁɔ̃ vɛ̃ mi.nyt/
items.respell: luh TREHⁿ oh-RA uhⁿ ruh-TAR dahⁿ-vee-ROHⁿ vehⁿ mee-NÜT
items.notes: A nominalised delay: aura un retard rather than sera en retard. The noun is what makes it sound official.

items.fr: Éloignez-vous de la bordure du quai, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: Please stand back from the platform edge.
items.ipa: /e.lwa.ɲe vu də la bɔʁ.dyʁ dy kɛ sil vu plɛ/
items.respell: ay-lwah-NYAY VOO duh lah bor-DÜR dü KEH seel voo PLEH
items.notes: A safety instruction using the same whole-form shape as a direction. It is an instruction to obey, not a route.

items.fr: Le train à destination de Bordeaux part dans cinq minutes.
items.en: The train for Bordeaux leaves in five minutes.
items.ipa: /lə tʁɛ̃ a dɛs.ti.na.sjɔ̃ də bɔʁ.do paʁ dɑ̃ sɛ̃k mi.nyt/
items.respell: luh TREHⁿ ah des-tee-nah-SYOHⁿ duh bor-DOH par dahⁿ sehⁿk mee-NÜT
items.notes: The same frame with a time instead of a platform. The frame is fixed and what follows it is not.

items.fr: Prochain arrêt, Châtelet. Correspondance ligne quatre.
items.en: Next stop, Châtelet. Change here for line four.
items.ipa: /pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃ a.ʁɛ ʃat.lɛ kɔ.ʁɛs.pɔ̃.dɑ̃s liɲ katʁ/
items.respell: pro-SHEHⁿ ah-REH shat-LEH ko-res-pohⁿ-DAHⁿSS leeny KATR
items.notes: The metro version: two fragments, no verb in either. A line number is read as a bare cardinal.

items.fr: Ce train ne dessert pas la gare de Massy.
items.en: This train does not stop at Massy station.
items.ipa: /sə tʁɛ̃ nə de.sɛʁ pa la ɡaʁ də ma.si/
items.respell: suh TREHⁿ nuh day-SEHR pah lah GAHR duh mah-SEE
items.notes: Desservir is the announcement word for stopping at. A negative announcement is the one that costs you a journey.

items.fr: Le train pour Rennes est annoncé avec dix minutes de retard.
items.en: The train to Rennes is announced ten minutes late.
items.ipa: /lə tʁɛ̃ puʁ ʁɛn ɛ.ta.nɔ̃.se a.vɛk di mi.nyt də ʁə.taʁ/
items.respell: luh TREHⁿ poor REN eh-tah-nohⁿ-SAY ah-vek dee mee-NÜT duh ruh-TAR
items.notes: Est annoncé avec is the station's formula for a delay and means nothing outside a station.

items.fr: Terminus, tout le monde descend.
items.en: End of the line, everybody off.
items.ipa: /tɛʁ.mi.nys tu lə mɔ̃d de.sɑ̃/
items.respell: ter-mee-NÜSS too luh MOHⁿD day-SAHⁿ
items.notes: Five words that end a journey. Descend here is the same verb the direction chains use for getting off.

items.fr: En raison d'un incident, le trafic est interrompu.
items.en: Because of an incident, service is suspended.
items.ipa: /ɑ̃ ʁɛ.zɔ̃ dœ̃ ɛ̃.si.dɑ̃ lə tʁa.fik ɛ.tɛ̃.te.ʁɔ̃.py/
items.respell: ahⁿ reh-ZOHⁿ duhⁿ ehⁿ-see-DAHⁿ luh trah-FEEK eh-tehⁿ-tay-rohⁿ-PÜ
items.notes: The formula that means your line has stopped. En raison de is the announcement register for parce que.

items.fr: Le prochain métro passera dans quatre minutes.
items.en: The next metro will come in four minutes.
items.ipa: /lə pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃ me.tʁo pa.sə.ʁa dɑ̃ katʁ mi.nyt/
items.respell: luh pro-SHEHⁿ may-TROH pah-suh-RA dahⁿ katr mee-NÜT
items.notes: Passera rather than arrivera. The train passes through; it does not arrive for you.

items.fr: Attention à la marche en descendant du train.
items.en: Mind the step when getting off the train.
items.ipa: /a.tɑ̃.sjɔ̃ a la maʁʃ ɑ̃ de.sɑ̃.dɑ̃ dy tʁɛ̃/
items.respell: ah-tahⁿ-SYOHⁿ ah lah MARSH ahⁿ day-sahⁿ-DAHⁿ dü TREHⁿ
items.notes: The French of mind the gap. La marche is the step, not walking, and the two are the same word.

items.fr: Les portes vont se fermer, éloignez-vous.
items.en: The doors are closing, stand back.
items.ipa: /le pɔʁt vɔ̃ sə fɛʁ.me e.lwa.ɲe vu/
items.respell: lay PORT vohⁿ suh fer-MAY ay-lwah-NYAY VOO
items.notes: Two moves in six words, both instructions. The futur proche is lesson 1 in A2's and is used, not taught.

items.fr: Le train à destination de Lille partira du quai numéro huit.
items.en: The train for Lille will leave from platform eight.
items.ipa: /lə tʁɛ̃ a dɛs.ti.na.sjɔ̃ də lil paʁ.ti.ʁa dy kɛ ny.me.ʁo ɥit/
items.respell: luh TREHⁿ ah des-tee-nah-SYOHⁿ duh LEEL par-tee-RA dü KEH nü-may-ROH ÜEET
items.notes: Quai numéro rather than voie. Both mean platform and a station uses whichever it uses.

items.fr: Aller simple ou aller-retour ?
items.en: One way or return?
